ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p32/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p32/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p32/r3.claim: Disbelievers mock the description of Hell because they presume to know everything, but it rests on divine wisdom: truth-seekers benefit and arrogant know-it-alls ruin their fate.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p32/r3.anchor: Those who have the desire for the truth will benefit from it

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p47/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p47/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p47/r1.claim: The realities of Paradise and Hell are mutashābihāt: similes give a general idea, but their actual form is known only to God; insisting on the form risks rejection of reasoned truths.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p47/r1.anchor: the actual form and reality are only known to God

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p47/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p47/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p47/r2.claim: Qur'an 3:7 teaches that warped readers chase ambiguous passages, while grounded believers accept them as revelation and leave their reality to God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p47/r2.anchor: no one except God knows their reality

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p47/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p47/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p47/r3.claim: The nineteen angels prompt mischief among corrupt Quraysh and People of the Book, so the following warning prepares readers while increasing true students' knowledge.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p48/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p48/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p48/r1.claim: The verse is an immediate warning revealed with the preceding one: its opening conjunction links it to that verse, unlike a later, independent insertion.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p48/r1.anchor: connected to the previous verse and revealed together with it

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p48/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p48/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p48/r2.claim: The independent Medinan verse 73:20 illustrates how a later insertion differs from this closely connected verse.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p48/r2.anchor: It does not begin with a copulative particle

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p48/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p48/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p48/r3.claim: The Prophet is told that mockery is expected, but he must ignore the arrogant talk; God mentions these facts to strengthen believers and expose mischief-makers.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p48/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p48/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p48/r4.claim: God appoints angels rather than jinn or devils over Hell, just as angels manage the universe's affairs as pure servants who carry out His will without deviation.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p48/r4.anchor: the Almighty has appointed angels and not the jinn and devils to conduct all the affairs of this universe

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p49/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p49/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p49/r1.claim: The objection that angels are also in Hell is answered by distinguishing prison inmates from their guards; the condemned will learn the difference.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p49/r1.anchor: they should remember that there is a world of difference

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p49/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p49/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p49/r2.claim: The nineteen are a trial exposing hidden vice in wrongdoers and virtue in the righteous; tests reveal character and potential.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p49/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p49/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p49/r3.claim: The Prophet's heavenly journey and the Qur'an's mention of Hell's zaqqūm tree are other facts that opponents turned into trials and mocked.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p49/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p49/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p49/r4.claim: God gives devils an opportunity to oppose truth so the diseased and hardened are tested and knowledgeable people recognize truth; Islahi refers readers to his discussion of 22:53–54.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p49/r4.anchor: God gives this chance so that what the devils say against the truth becomes a trial

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p50/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p50/r1.speaker: narratives
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p50/r1.claim: Some reports say arrogant Quraysh mocked that nineteen angels were easy to overpower, with one man boasting he and a companion could handle them.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p50/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p50/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p50/r2.claim: The lām expresses consequence: the trial increases the certainty of sincere People of the Book and strengthens believers' faith.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p50/r2.anchor: the consequence of the struggle between good and evil is that the conviction of the true People of the Book will be augmented

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p50/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p50/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p50/r3.claim: Sincere People of the Book had no reason to mock the report because similar descriptions appear in their own books; such people later embraced Islam.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p50/r3.anchor: similar statements were found in their own books

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p50/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p50/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p50/r4.claim: Opponents' weak objections let believers assess both sides, making their faith reasoned and secure rather than blind and easily shaken.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p50/r4.anchor: He accepts it with full conviction and every trial increases his faith

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p50/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p50/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p50/r5.claim: The negative clause says trials protect sincere People of the Book and believers from doubt, complementing the preceding positive claim.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p50/r5.anchor: become secure from the onslaughts of doubt

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p50/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p50/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p50/r6.claim: Although some infer a Medinan date from the mention of People of the Book, Islahi rejects that view: sincere People of the Book were counted among Muslims from the beginning.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p50/r6.anchor: in my opinion this view is not correct

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p51/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p51/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p51/r1.claim: Sincere People of the Book are named with believers from the start to establish their status and role alongside the new Prophet and prepare them for coming trials.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p51/r1.anchor: what role they were required to play

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p51/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p51/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p51/r2.claim: The phrase about people with a disease in their hearts concerns jealous Jews, not hypocrites; Qur'an uses disease for envy as well, directed here at the Ishmaelites and Muhammad.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p51/r2.anchor: this word also refers to jealousy and envy, and on such occasions it refers to the Jews

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p51/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p51/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p51/r3.claim: The jealous Jews and Quraysh disbelievers, unlike sincere People of the Book, share a mocking response to ambiguous passages, asking what God means by them.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p51/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p51/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p51/r4.claim: God's leading astray or guiding through such trials follows His wise law: He misguides those who merit it and guides those worthy under that law.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p51/r4.anchor: He leads only those people astray whom He finds worthy of this treatment and those who are worthy of being guided as per His law are guided by Him

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p52/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p52/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p52/r1.claim: God alone knows the unseen constitution of His armies; critics arrogantly claim complete knowledge, and pseudo-intellectuals reject or distort what their limited intellect cannot grasp.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p52/r1.anchor: No one except the Almighty knows about His armies.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p52/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p52/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p52/r2.claim: Warnings about the Hereafter are reminders that remove people's excuse; God shows virtue and vice but leaves them free to choose rather than forcing virtue.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p52/r2.anchor: are not meant for criticism; they are meant to remind and admonish

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p52/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p52/r3.speaker: exegetes
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p52/r3.claim: Exegetes generally take the pronoun's antecedent to be Hell.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p52/r3.anchor: Our exegetes have generally regarded the antecedent of the pronoun

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p52/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p52/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p52/r4.claim: Islahi instead identifies the antecedent as the verses depicting Hell, because those verses qualify as a reminder.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p52/r4.anchor: In my opinion, however, it refers to the verses

QUSHAYRI:v3p364/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p364/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p364/r7.claim: Only God comprehends the full number of His forces; created knowledge reaches some measures but not others.
QUSHAYRI:v3p364/r7.anchor: تقاصرت علوم الخلق فلم تتعلق إلا بمقدار دون مقدار

FARRA:v3p203/r7.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p203/r7.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p203/r7.claim: The answer says the Fire's guardians are angels, asks who could overpower them, and explains their number as a test for disbelievers and confirmation for scripture's people and believers.
FARRA:v3p203/r7.anchor: فأنزل الله: «وما جعلنا أصحاب النار إلا ملائكة» (31) ، أي: فمن يطيق الملائكة؟

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p271#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p271#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p271#2/r1.claim: The guardians of Hell are angels, not humans, so no one can overpower them; their number nineteen tests and misleads unbelievers.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p271#2/r1.anchor: {وما جعلنا أصحاب النار إلا ملائكة} لا رجالا آدميين، فمن ذا يغلب الملائكة؟

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p271#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p271#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p271#2/r2.claim: The number confirms the Torah and Gospel for scriptured people; believers from them increase in faith and both scriptured people and believers are certain.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p271#2/r2.anchor: {ليستيقن الذين أوتوا الكتاب} لأنه مكتوب في التوراة والإنجيل أنهم تسعة عشر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p271#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p271#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p271#2/r3.claim: The ‘example’ is the report itself; hypocrites and Meccan polytheists ask what God intends, while He guides or misleads as He wills.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p271#2/r3.anchor: شك ونفاق {والكافرون} [مشركو مكة] (1) {ماذا أراد الله بهذا مثلا}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p271#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p271#2/r4.speaker: مقاتل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p271#2/r4.claim: The troops verse answers Abu Jahl, who asked whether Muhammad had only nineteen helpers.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p271#2/r4.anchor: قال مقاتل: هذا جواب أبي جهل حين قال: أما لمحمد أعوان إلا تسعة عشر؟

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p271#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p271#2/r5.speaker: عطاء
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p271#2/r5.claim: Only God knows the full number of angels created to punish Hell’s people; nineteen are its keepers, with innumerable angelic assistants.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p271#2/r5.anchor: قال عطاء: {وما يعلم جنود ربك إلا هو} يعني من الملائكة الذين خلقهم لتعذيب أهل النار

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p271#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p271#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p271#2/r6.claim: وما هي refers to Saqar, which serves as a reminder and admonition to humanity.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p271#2/r6.anchor: ثم رجع إلى ذكر سقر فقال: {وما هي} يعني [سقر] (2) {إلا ذكرى للبشر}

NAHHAS:v5p70/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p70/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p70/r1.claim: Aṣḥāb is a plural of ṣāḥib after deleting an augment; afʿāl does not usually pluralize faʿil/faʿl without deletion.
NAHHAS:v5p70/r1.anchor: أصحاب جمع صاحب على حذف الزائد لأن أفعالا ليس بجمع فاعل بغير حذف

NAHHAS:v5p70/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p70/r2.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p70/r2.claim: The number of keepers tests and burdens disbelievers so they learn God's power to strengthen the angels.
NAHHAS:v5p70/r2.anchor: أي شدة وتعبدا ليكفروا فيعلموا أن الله قادر على تقوية هؤلاء الملائكة

NAHHAS:v5p70/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p70/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p70/r3.claim: The lām in liyastaqina is purposive and originally prepositional; the clauses about faith and doubt coordinate with it, and a repeated lām is optional.
NAHHAS:v5p70/r3.anchor: لام كي وأصلها أنها لام الخفض لأن المعنى لاستيقان الذين أوتوا الكتاب

NAHHAS:v5p70/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p70/r4.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p70/r4.claim: In mādhā arāda, mā is the object and mādhā one unit; alternatively, if dhā means 'which,' mā is subject and dhā predicate.
NAHHAS:v5p70/r4.anchor: ما في موضع نصب بأراد وهي وذا بمنزلة شيء واحد

NAHHAS:v5p70/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p70/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p70/r5.claim: The kāf in kadhālika is an accusative adjective modifying an implied verbal noun.
NAHHAS:v5p70/r5.anchor: الكاف في موضع نصب نعت لمصدر

NAHHAS:v5p70/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p70/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p70/r6.claim: In 'none knows God's armies except Him,' huwa is nominative with yaʿlam and cannot be an accusative exception.
NAHHAS:v5p70/r6.anchor: وما يعلم جنود ربك إلا هو ) رفع بيعلم ولا يجوز النصب على الاستثناء

NAHHAS:v5p70/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p70/r7.speaker: مجاهد
NAHHAS:v5p70/r7.claim: Mujāhid says 'it is only a reminder to mankind' means Hell is a reminder; Ibn Jarīr reports the pause as complete.
NAHHAS:v5p70/r7.anchor: قال مجاهد أي وما النار إلا ذكرى للبشر وذكر محمد بن جرير أن التمام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p396#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p396#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p396#2/r1.claim: Only angels guard Hell, refuting Quraysh: their number tests unbelievers by prompting presumptuous talk and ambition.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p396#2/r1.anchor: وقوله تعالى: وما جعلنا أصحاب النار إلا ملائكة تبيين لفساد أقوال قريش

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p396#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p396#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وغيرهم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p396#2/r2.claim: People of the Book recognize the Quran as from God because the number matches their revealed books, which Muhammad neither read nor belonged to their community; the scriptures confirm one another.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p396#2/r2.anchor: وليستيقن أهل الكتاب: التوراة والإنجيل أن هذا القرآن من عند الله، إذ هم يجدوه هذه العدة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p396#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p396#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p396#2/r3.claim: Revelation of truths from God increases believers' faith and removes doubt from believing People of the Book and the faithful.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p396#2/r3.anchor: وبورود الحقائق من عند الله عز وجل يزداد كل ذي إيمان إيمانا ويزول الريب عن المصدقين من أهل الكتاب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p396#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p396#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p396#2/r4.claim: Those with sickness of heart are a hypocritical or unbelieving group who go astray and question the example contemptuously.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p396#2/r4.anchor: وليقول الذين في قلوبهم مرض الآية، نوع من الفتنة لهذا الصنف المنافق أو الكافر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p396#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p396#2/r5.speaker: الحسين بن الفضل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p396#2/r5.claim: Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl says the sura is Meccan and had no hypocrisy in Mecca, so sickness here means agitation and weakness of faith.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p396#2/r5.anchor: قال الحسين بن الفضل: السورة مكية ولم يكن بمكة نفاق فإنما المرض في هذه الآية الاضطراب وضعف الإيمان

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p397/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p397/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p397/r1.claim: God misguides those whose hearts are rusted and guides believers who know His power and affirm the truth of prophetic revelation and scripture.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p397/r1.anchor: تعالى أنه يهدي من يشاء من المؤمنين لما ورد بذلك لعلمهم بالقدرة ووقوف عقولهم على كنه سلطان الله تعالى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p397/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p397/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p397/r2.claim: Only God knows His forces; the statement indicates that reality exceeds imagination and this is only one part of divine power, since the heavens teem with constantly obedient angels.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p397/r2.anchor: وما يعلم جنود ربك إلا هو إعلاما بأن الأمر فوق ما يتوهم وأن الخبر إنما هو عن بعض القدرة لا عن كلها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p397/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p397/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p397/r3.claim: Mujahid says وما هي refers to Hell, whose reminder makes people fear and obey God.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p397/r3.anchor: قال مجاهد الضمير في قوله وما هي للنار المذكورة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p397/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p397/r4.speaker: بعض الحذاق
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p397/r4.claim: Some discerning interpreters take وما هي to mean the situation, address, and warning.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p397/r4.anchor: وقال بعض الحذاق. قوله تعالى: ما هي يراد بها الحال والمخاطبة والنذارة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p397/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p397/r5.speaker: الثعلبي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p397/r5.claim: Al-Thaʿlabi reports a view that وما هي means the worldly fire, a reminder of the fire of the afterlife.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p397/r5.anchor: قال الثعلبي: وقيل وما هي، يراد نار الدنيا، أي إن هذه تذكرة للبشر بنار الآخرة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p270#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p270#2/r1.speaker: حكيم بن حزام
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p270#2/r1.claim: A report says the Prophet heard the sky groan, with an angel bowing or prostrating on every handspan; the excerpt gives no grading.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p270#2/r1.anchor: عن حكيم بن حزام قال: بينما رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مع أصحابه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p270#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p270#2/r2.speaker: عائشة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p270#2/r2.claim: A strange Prophetic report from Aisha says no space in the lowest heaven is without an angel prostrating or standing and cites the angels’ declaration that each has a place.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p270#2/r2.anchor: عن عائشة أنها قالت: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "ما في السماء الدنيا موضع قدم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p270#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p270#2/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p270#2/r3.claim: Ibn Mas‘ud gives a stopped report that every handspan of one heaven bears an angel’s forehead or feet in prayer, then recites the angels’ declaration.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p270#2/r3.anchor: عن ابن مسعود أنه قال: إن من السماوات سماء ما فيها موضع شبر إلا وعليه جبهة ملك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p270#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p270#2/r4.speaker: العلاء بن سعد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p270#2/r4.claim: A very strange-chain report says every foot-space in the heavens has a standing, bowing, or prostrating angel and quotes the angels’ declaration.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p270#2/r4.anchor: عن أبيه العلاء بن سعد -وقد شهد الفتح وما بعده-أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال يوما لجلسائه:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p271/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p271/r1.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p271/r1.claim: In a report Ibn Kathir calls extremely objectionable, Umar relates an altercation over Abu Jahsh’s refusal to pray, then a saying that God has angels continuously bowing or prostrating who will say they never worshipped Him as He deserves.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p271/r1.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمر: أن عمر جاء والصلاة قائمة، ونفر ثلاثة جلوس،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p271/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p271/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p271/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir calls this account highly objectionable and faults its transmission: Ishaq al-Farawi was weakened by several critics, his teacher was also criticized, and Muhammad ibn Nasr failed to discuss its defects.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p271/r2.anchor: وهذا حديث غريب جدا، بل منكر نكارة شديدة، وإسحاق الفروي روى عنه البخاري،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p271/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p271/r3.speaker: محمد بن نصر المروزي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p271/r3.claim: Muhammad ibn Nasr also transmits similar versions as mursal reports through Sa‘id ibn Jubayr and al-Hasan al-Basri.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p271/r3.anchor: غير أنه رواه من وجه آخر عن سعيد بن جبير مرسلا بنحوه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p272/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p272/r1.speaker: عدي بن أرطاة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p272/r1.claim: A report with an acceptable chain says angels tremble in awe of God, some prostrating or bowing continuously since the creation of heaven and earth; when they raise their heads, they say they have not worshipped Him as He deserves.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p272/r1.anchor: سمعت عدي بن أرطاة وهو يخطبنا على منبر المدائن

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p145/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p145/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p145/r1.claim: Ibn Jurayj reports the Prophet describing Hell's keepers as terrifying, immensely strong beings who can drive an entire nation into the Fire and throw a mountain over them.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p145/r1.anchor: وروى ابن جريج أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم نعت خزنة جهنم فقال : كأن أعينهم البرق , وكأن أفواههم الصياصي ,

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p145/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p145/r2.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p145/r2.claim: The People of the Book gain certainty because the number of keepers matches the Torah and Gospel.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p145/r2.anchor: أحدهما : ليستيقنوا عدد الخزنة لموافقة التوراة والإنجيل , قاله مجاهد .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p145/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p145/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p145/r3.claim: Alternatively, the matching number of keepers assures them that Muhammad is a prophet.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p145/r3.anchor: الثاني : ليستيقنوا أن محمدا نبي لما جاء به من موافقة عدة الخزنة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p145/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p145/r4.speaker: جريج
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p145/r4.claim: The believers increase in faith through this information.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p145/r4.anchor: { ويزداد الذين آمنوا إيمانا } بذلك , قاله جريج .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p145/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p145/r5.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p145/r5.claim: The phrase that this is only a reminder for humanity refers to Hell as a warning.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p145/r5.anchor: أحدها : وما نار جهنم إلا ذكرى للبشر , قاله قتادة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p145/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p145/r6.speaker: ابن عيسى
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p145/r6.claim: It may mean the earthly fire is a reminder of the Fire of the afterlife.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p145/r6.anchor: الثاني : وما هذه النار في الدنيا إلا تذكرة لنار الآخرة , حكاه ابن عيسى .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p145/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p145/r7.speaker: ابن شجرة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p145/r7.claim: It may mean this sura is a reminder for people.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p145/r7.anchor: الثالث : وما هذه السورة إلا تذكرة للناس , قاله ابن شجرة .

ZAJJAJ:v5p248#2/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p248#2/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p248#2/r1.claim: Fire in this world serves as a reminder of the Fire in the Hereafter.
ZAJJAJ:v5p248#2/r1.anchor: جاء في التفسير أن النار في الدنيا تذكر بالنار في الآخرة

STUDYQURAN:7:11/r25.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r25.speaker: R, Z
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r25.claim: Some commentators regard Iblis’s claim that God caused him to err as true, though it does not excuse him, and relate it to verses where God lets people go astray.
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r25.anchor: some commentators have considered Iblīs’s claim to represent a true statement, albeit one that does not excuse his actions (R, Z)

RAZI-FULL:v30p179#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p179#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p179#3/r1.claim: An unattributed report says that after the nineteen keepers were mentioned, Abū Jahl mocked the claim and challenged Quraysh to overpower them; Abū al-Ashadd boasted he could take seventeen while the rest handled two.
RAZI-FULL:v30p179#3/r1.anchor: روي أنه لما نزل قوله تعالى : { عليها تسعة عشر } ( المدثر : 30 ) قال أبو جهل : لقريش ثكلتكم أمهاتكم

RAZI-FULL:v30p179#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p179#3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p179#3/r2.claim: The Muslims answered that angels cannot be compared with blacksmiths; the saying became a proverb for two incomparable things, and Rāzī explains the comparison as angels versus jailers and smiths, with the jailer confining the Fire.
RAZI-FULL:v30p179#3/r2.anchor: لما قال أبو جهل وأبو الأشد ذلك ، قال المسلمون ويحكم لا تقاس الملائكة بالحدادينا فجرى هذا مثلا في كل شيئين لا يسوى بينهما

RAZI-FULL:v30p179#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p179#3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p179#3/r3.claim: Angels were appointed rather than the punished creatures’ own kind because shared kind may incline toward pity; likewise the human messenger is of our kind so he may show compassion.
RAZI-FULL:v30p179#3/r3.anchor: ليكونوا بخلاف جنس المعذبين ، لأن الجنسية مظنة الرأفة والرحمة ، ولذلك بعث الرسول المبعوث إلينا من جنسنا ليكون له رأفة ورحمة بنا

RAZI-FULL:v30p179#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p179#3/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p179#3/r4.claim: Angels are furthest from disobeying God and strongest in carrying out arduous acts of obedience.
RAZI-FULL:v30p179#3/r4.anchor: أنهم أبعد الخلق عن معصية الله تعالى وأقواهم على الطاعات الشاقة

RAZI-FULL:v30p179#3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p179#3/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p179#3/r5.claim: Their strength exceeds that of jinn and humans.
RAZI-FULL:v30p179#3/r5.anchor: أن قوتهم أعظم من قوة الجن والإنس

RAZI-FULL:v30p179#3/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p179#3/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p179#3/r6.claim: A hypothetical objection asks how beings created from light could endure staying in fire.
RAZI-FULL:v30p179#3/r6.anchor: فإن قيل : ثبت في الأخبار ، أن الملائكة مخلوقون من النور ، والمخلوق من النور كيف يطيق المكث في النار

RAZI-FULL:v30p179#3/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p179#3/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p179#3/r7.claim: Rāzī replies that God can sustain life indefinitely in severe torment without death, so it is likewise possible for angels to remain in fire without pain.
RAZI-FULL:v30p179#3/r7.anchor: أبد الآباد ولا يموت ، فكذا لا استبعاد في بقاء الملائكة هناك من غير ألم

RAZI-FULL:v30p179#3/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p179#3/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p179#3/r8.claim: The first reason the count tests unbelievers is their mockery: why were the keepers not twenty, and what singled out this number?
RAZI-FULL:v30p179#3/r8.anchor: الأول : أن الكفار يستهزئون ، يقولون : لم لم يكونوا عشرين ، وما المقتضى لتخصيص هذا العدد بالوجود

RAZI-FULL:v30p179#3/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p179#3/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p179#3/r9.claim: The second objection is that so few keepers seem unable to punish all jinn and humans from creation to the Resurrection; believers do not heed these doubts.
RAZI-FULL:v30p179#3/r9.anchor: الثاني : أن الكفار يقولون هذا العدد القليل كيف يكونون وافين بتعذيب أكثر خلق العالم من الجن والإنس من أول ما خلق الله إلى قيام القيامة

RAZI-FULL:v30p180/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p180/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p180/r1.claim: For the question why the number is not different, Rāzī notes that every finite world and every bounded body has a definite count; one can equally ask why the world was created at one moment rather than just before or after, or why any created thing has its particular time and parts. No answer is needed beyond God’s free choice among equals, which also explains the nineteen keepers.
RAZI-FULL:v30p180/r1.anchor: أما السؤال الأول : فلأن جملة العالم متناهية ، فلا بد وأن يكون للجواهر الفردة التي منها تألفت جملة هذا العالم عدد معين

RAZI-FULL:v30p180/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p180/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p180/r2.claim: The objection from the keepers’ small number is weak: God can grant them strength enough to punish all creatures without failing.
RAZI-FULL:v30p180/r2.anchor: لا يبعد في قدرة الله تعالى أن يعطي هذا العدد من القدرة والقوة ما يصيرون به قادرين على تعذيب جملة الخلق

RAZI-FULL:v30p180/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p180/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p180/r3.claim: Both objections challenge divine omnipotence; once God’s unlimited power and the afterlife’s unlike worldly conditions are accepted, these improbabilities disappear.
RAZI-FULL:v30p180/r3.anchor: وبالجملة فمدار هذين السؤالين على القدح في كمال قدرة الله ، فأما من اعترف بكونه تعالى قادرا على مالا نهاية له من المقدورات

RAZI-FULL:v30p180#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p180#2/r1.speaker: القائلون بأن الله قد يريد الإضلال
RAZI-FULL:v30p180#2/r1.claim: Those who argue that God may will misguidance cite the verse’s statement that the keepers’ number was made a trial for unbelievers.
RAZI-FULL:v30p180#2/r1.anchor: المسألة الثانية : احتج من قال : إنه تعالى قد يريد الإضلال بهذه الآية ، قال لأن قوله تعالى : { وما جعلنا عدتهم إلا فتنة للذين كفروا }

RAZI-FULL:v30p180#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p180#2/r2.speaker: الجبائي
RAZI-FULL:v30p180#2/r2.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī says fitna means making the religious obligation more demanding, so people infer God can empower nineteen to do what one hundred thousand strong angels could not.
RAZI-FULL:v30p180#2/r2.anchor: قال الجبائي : المراد من الفتنة تشديد التعبد ليستدلوا ويعرفوا أنه تعالى قادر على أن يقوي هؤلاء التسعة عشر

RAZI-FULL:v30p180#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p180#2/r3.speaker: الكعبي
RAZI-FULL:v30p180#2/r3.claim: Al-Kaʿbī says fitna means a test in which believers entrust the wisdom of the chosen number to the Creator’s knowledge; it is an ambiguous matter they are commanded to accept in faith.
RAZI-FULL:v30p180#2/r3.anchor: قال الكعبي : المراد من الفتنة الامتحان حتى يفوض المؤمنون حكمة التخصيص بالعدد المعين إلى علم الخالق سبحانه

RAZI-FULL:v30p180#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p180#2/r4.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v30p180#2/r4.claim: A third Muʿtazilī answer takes the trial as the disbelief caused when people reject the keepers’ number and make their derisive remarks; this is punishment through withholding divine لطف.
RAZI-FULL:v30p180#2/r4.anchor: وثالثها : أن المراد من الفتنة ما وقعوا فيه من الكفر بسبب تكذيبهم بعدد الخزنة ، والمعنى إلا فتنة على الذين كفروا ليكذبوا به

RAZI-FULL:v30p180#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p180#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p180#2/r5.claim: Rāzī replies that the key question is whether ambiguous revelation strengthens the motive to disbelieve: if not, calling it a trial is pointless; if so, the motive to abstain is overcome and disbelief becomes unavoidable.
RAZI-FULL:v30p180#2/r5.anchor: والجواب : أنه لا نزاع في شيء مما ذكرتم ، إلا أنا نقول : هل لإنزال هذه المتشابهات أثر في تقوية داعية الكفر ، أم لا ؟

RAZI-FULL:v30p180#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p180#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p180#2/r6.claim: Rāzī lists four effects of the ambiguous passage: People of Scripture become certain, believers increase in faith, both groups remain free of doubt, and diseased hearts and unbelievers ask what God intended by it.
RAZI-FULL:v30p180#2/r6.anchor: واعلم أنه تعالى بين أن المقصود من إنزال هذا المتشابه أمور أربعة . أولها : { ليستيقن الذين أوتوا الكتاب } وثانيها : { ويزداد الذين ءامنوا إيمانا }

RAZI-FULL:v30p181/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p181/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p181/r1.claim: One construction supplies an omitted coordination: the number is a trial for unbelievers and also serves to make the People of Scripture certain; an “and” may be stated or omitted in such phrasing.
RAZI-FULL:v30p181/r1.anchor: التقدير : وما جعلنا عدتهم إلا فتنة للذين كفروا

RAZI-FULL:v30p181/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p181/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p181/r2.claim: Another construction says “we made their number only nineteen,” using “trial for unbelievers” in place of “nineteen”: the effect is named for its cause because that effect necessarily follows.
RAZI-FULL:v30p181/r2.anchor: وما جعلنا عدتهم إلا تسعة عشر إلا أنه وضع فتنة للذين كفروا موضع تسعة عشر

RAZI-FULL:v30p181/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p181/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p181/r3.claim: First, this count was already in the People of Scripture’s book; Muḥammad reported the same number without prior study, showing that it came by revelation, which strengthens believers from among them.
RAZI-FULL:v30p181/r3.anchor: أن هذا العدد لما كان موجودا في كتابهم ، ثم إنه عليه السلام أخبر على وفق ذلك من غير سابقة دراسة وتعلم

RAZI-FULL:v30p181/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p181/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p181/r4.claim: Second, although Torah and Gospel readers knew the number, suspected textual alteration made them hesitant to rely on it; hearing it from the Messenger strengthened their faith and certainty in its truth.
RAZI-FULL:v30p181/r4.anchor: أن التوراة والإنجيل كانا محرفين ، فأهل الكتاب كانوا يقرأون فيهما أن عدد الزبانية هو هذا القدر ، ولكنهم ما كانوا يعولون على ذلك

RAZI-FULL:v30p181/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p181/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p181/r5.claim: Third, Muḥammad knew Quraysh would mock this astonishing detail, as they mocked clearer doctrines; risking ridicule to proclaim it shows his aim was conveying revelation rather than worldly status or pleasing either believers or deniers.
RAZI-FULL:v30p181/r5.anchor: وثالثها : أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يعلم من حال قريش أنه متى أخبرهم بهذا العدد العجيب ، فإنهم يستهزئون به ويضحكون منه

RAZI-FULL:v30p182/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p182/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p182/r1.claim: A believer who recalls God’s knowledge, self-sufficiency, and freedom from falsehood can let the general certainty that God is truthful and wise overcome surprise at the number; considering these proofs deepens attention to evidence and religious submission, which is faith’s increase.
RAZI-FULL:v30p182/r1.anchor: أن المكلف مالم يستحضر كونه تعالى عالما بجميع المعلومات غنيا عن جميع الحادثات منزها عن الكذب والحلف لا يمكنه أن ينقاد لهذه العدة

RAZI-FULL:v30p182/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p182/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p182/r2.claim: For those who hold that faith’s essence admits no increase or decrease, Rāzī interprets increase as an increase in faith’s fruits, effects, and implications.
RAZI-FULL:v30p182/r2.anchor: الجواب : نحمله على ثمرات الإيمان وعلى آثاره ولوازمه

RAZI-FULL:v30p182/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p182/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p182/r3.claim: A person may gain certainty about a subtle, difficult proof, then forget a premise and fall back into doubt; restating the point guarantees firm certainty after which doubt does not arise.
RAZI-FULL:v30p182/r3.anchor: فإذا اجتهد الإنسان فيه وحصل له اليقين فربما غفل عن

RAZI-FULL:v30p182/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p182/r4.speaker: جمهور المفسرين
RAZI-FULL:v30p182/r4.claim: Most exegetes identify those with diseased hearts as unbelievers.
RAZI-FULL:v30p182/r4.anchor: جمهور المفسرين قالوا في تفسير قوله : { الذين في قلوبهم مرض } إنهم الكافرون

RAZI-FULL:v30p182/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p182/r5.speaker: الحسين بن الفضل البجلي
RAZI-FULL:v30p182/r5.claim: Al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Faḍl al-Bajalī notes that the sūra is Meccan and there was no hypocrisy in Mecca, so “disease” here cannot mean hypocrisy.
RAZI-FULL:v30p182/r5.anchor: وذكر الحسين بن الفضل البجلي أن هذه السورة مكية ولم يكن بمكة نفاق ، فالمرض في هذه الآية ليس بمعنى النفاق

RAZI-FULL:v30p182/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p182/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p182/r6.claim: Rāzī upholds the exegetes’ view: God knew hypocrisy would arise later and reported it in advance, making the fulfilled prediction a miracle.
RAZI-FULL:v30p182/r6.anchor: والجواب : قول المفسرين حق وذلك لأنه كان في معلوم الله تعالى أن النفاق سيحدث فأخبر عما سيكون ، وعلى هذا تصير هذه الآية معجزة

RAZI-FULL:v30p182/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p182/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p182/r7.claim: Alternatively, “disease” may mean doubt, since most Meccans were doubters while some were certain of the Prophet’s falsehood.
RAZI-FULL:v30p182/r7.anchor: ويجوز أيضا أن يراد بالمرض الشك لأن أهل مكة كان أكثرهم شاكين وبعضهم كانوا قاطعين بالكذب

RAZI-FULL:v30p182#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p182#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p182#2/r1.claim: On Rāzī’s own theological position, there is no difficulty in God intending the unbelievers’ and hypocrites’ response, since God guides whom He wills and misguides whom He wills.
RAZI-FULL:v30p182#2/r1.anchor: أما على أصلنا فلا إشكال لأنه تعالى يهدي من يشاء ويضل من يشاء

RAZI-FULL:v30p182#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p182#2/r2.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v30p182#2/r2.claim: The Muʿtazila say the lām describes an outcome that occurred as though it were an intended purpose, as in 28:8.
RAZI-FULL:v30p182#2/r2.anchor: وأما عند المعتزلة فإن هذه الحالة لما وقعت أشبهت الغرض في كونه واقعا ، فأدخل عليه حرف اللام

RAZI-FULL:v30p182#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p182#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p182#2/r3.claim: They called it a “parable” because the extraordinary number made them suspect that its apparent sense was not intended and that it symbolized another purpose.
RAZI-FULL:v30p182#2/r3.anchor: أنه لما كان هذا العدد عددا عجيبا ظن القوم أنه ربما لم يكن مراد الله منه ما أشعر به ظاهره بل جعله مثلا لشيء آخر

RAZI-FULL:v30p182#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p182#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p182#2/r4.claim: Although those with diseased hearts—hypocrites—outwardly acknowledged the Qur’an came from God, they voiced the question as a claim about God’s intent.
RAZI-FULL:v30p182#2/r4.anchor: أما الذين في قلوبهم مرض ، وهم المنافقون فكانوا في الظاهر معترفين بأن القرآن من عند الله فلا جرم قالوا ذلك باللسان

RAZI-FULL:v30p182#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p182#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p182#2/r5.claim: Unbelievers asked mockingly, or used the statement as an argument that a Qur’an containing such speech could not come from God.
RAZI-FULL:v30p182#2/r5.anchor: وأما الكفار فقالوه على سبيل التهكم أو على سبيل الاستدلال بأن القرآن لو كان من عند الله لما قال مثل هذا الكلام

RAZI-FULL:v30p183/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p183/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p183/r1.claim: Rāzī says the verse plainly supports his companions’ position: it first calls the number a trial for unbelievers, then quotes their response, and concludes that God guides or misguides whom He wills.
RAZI-FULL:v30p183/r1.anchor: وجه الاستدلال بالآية للأصحاب ظاهر لأنه تعالى ذكر في أول الآية قوله : { وما جعلنا عدتهم إلا فتنة للذين كفروا }

RAZI-FULL:v30p183/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p183/r2.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v30p183/r2.claim: The Muʿtazila interpret divine misguidance as withholding لطف, the divine aids that would guide people.
RAZI-FULL:v30p183/r2.anchor: أما المعتزلة فقد ذكروا الوجوه المشهورة التي لهم أحدها : أن المراد من الإضلال منع الألطاف

RAZI-FULL:v30p183/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p183/r3.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v30p183/r3.claim: They also say that people choose guidance or error when the verses arrive, making the verses seem to cause the response, as in the Qur’an’s statements that revelation increased some in faith and others in impurity.
RAZI-FULL:v30p183/r3.anchor: وثانيها : أنه لما اهتدى قوم باختيارهم عند نزول هذه الآيات وضل قوم باختيارهم عند نزولها

RAZI-FULL:v30p183/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p183/r4.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v30p183/r4.claim: Another Muʿtazilī gloss takes “misguides” and “guides” to mean that God judges a person to be astray or guided.
RAZI-FULL:v30p183/r4.anchor: وثالثها : أن المراد من قوله : { يضل } ومن قوله : { يهدي } حكم الله بكونه ضالا ويكون مهتديا

RAZI-FULL:v30p183/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p183/r5.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v30p183/r5.claim: A fourth Muʿtazilī interpretation says that on Judgment Day God leads unbelievers away from the abode of reward.
RAZI-FULL:v30p183/r5.anchor: أنه تعالى يضلهم يوم القيامة عن دار الثواب

RAZI-FULL:v30p183/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p183/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p183/r6.claim: Rāzī notes that these Muʿtazilī interpretations and replies were discussed earlier in his commentary on al-Baqara.
RAZI-FULL:v30p183/r6.anchor: وهذه الكلمات مع أجوبتها تقدمت في سورة البقرة في قوله : { يضل به كثيرا ويهدي به كثيرا } ( البقرة : 26 )

RAZI-FULL:v30p183#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p183#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p183#2/r1.claim: One answer is that each of the nineteen keepers has further angelic helpers whose number no one knows but God.
RAZI-FULL:v30p183#2/r1.anchor: أحدها : وهو الأولى أن القوم استقبلوا ذلك العدد ، فقال تعالى : { وما يعلم جنود ربك إلا هو } فهب أن هؤلاء تسعة عشر

RAZI-FULL:v30p183#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p183#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p183#2/r2.claim: Alternatively, God alone knows His vast armies; although He could make the keepers twenty, His wisdom in choosing nineteen is unknown to creatures but known to Him.
RAZI-FULL:v30p183#2/r2.anchor: وثانيها : وما يعلم جنود ربك لفرط كثرتها إلا هو ، فلا يعز عليه تتميم الخزنة عشرين ولكن له في هذا العدد حكمة

RAZI-FULL:v30p183#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p183#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p183#2/r3.claim: God does not need keepers to punish: He Himself creates their pains, and even a hair turned in an eye or pain in one vein would suffice. His armies are unlimited because His possible acts are unlimited, so the number of keepers does not limit torment.
RAZI-FULL:v30p183#2/r3.anchor: وثالثها : أنه لا حاجة بالله سبحانه في تعذيب الكفار والفساق إلى هؤلاء الخزنة ، فإنه هو الذي يعذبهم في الحقيقة ، وهو الذي يخلق الآلام فيهم

RAZI-FULL:v30p183#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p183#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p183#3/r1.claim: One view takes the pronoun “it” to refer to Saqar: Saqar and its description are a reminder to humanity.
RAZI-FULL:v30p183#3/r1.anchor: الأول : أنه عائد إلى سقر ، والمعنى وما سقر وصفتها إلا تذكرة للبشر

RAZI-FULL:v30p183#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p183#3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p183#3/r2.claim: A second view takes “it” as the verses containing these ambiguous matters: they remind all humanity, though only believers benefit from them.
RAZI-FULL:v30p183#3/r2.anchor: والثاني : أنه عائد إلى هذه الآيات المشتملة على هذه المتشابهات ، وهي ذكرى لجميع العالمية

STUDYQURAN:74:31/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:74:31/r1.speaker: Abū Jahl
STUDYQURAN:74:31/r1.claim: After hearing there were only nineteen guardians, Abū Jahl reportedly boasted that they would be easy to overcome.
STUDYQURAN:74:31/r1.anchor: Upon hearing that there were only nineteen over it, Abū Jahl, one of the leaders of the Quraysh, is reported to have boasted that there would be no problem in overcoming them

STUDYQURAN:74:31/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:74:31/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:74:31/r2.claim: The verse clarifies that the Fire’s wardens are angels rather than human beings.
STUDYQURAN:74:31/r2.anchor: this verse clarifies that they are angels, not human beings

STUDYQURAN:74:31/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:74:31/r3.speaker: JJ
STUDYQURAN:74:31/r3.claim: The nineteen may be a trial because some ask why the number is nineteen and thereby go astray.
STUDYQURAN:74:31/r3.anchor: they are something that will lead some people astray when they ask why there are nineteen

STUDYQURAN:74:31/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:74:31/r4.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:74:31/r4.claim: Alternatively, the nineteen are a source of punishment in the Hereafter.
STUDYQURAN:74:31/r4.anchor: or that they are a source of punishment in the Hereafter

STUDYQURAN:74:31/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:74:31/r5.speaker: Bg, IK, Q, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:74:31/r5.claim: Most say nineteen was already known to Jews and Christians, so Quranic agreement confirms Muhammad’s prophethood for the People of the Book.
STUDYQURAN:74:31/r5.anchor: understood by most to mean that nineteen was also the number known to the Jews and Christians; therefore, the similar enumeration in the Quran should give them greater certainty

STUDYQURAN:74:31/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:74:31/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:74:31/r6.claim: The appointment of the number is also said to increase believers’ faith and certainty.
STUDYQURAN:74:31/r6.anchor: the believers and the People of the Book are said to increase in faith and certainty

STUDYQURAN:74:31/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:74:31/r7.speaker: Q, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:74:31/r7.claim: Those with sickness in their hearts may be hypocrites.
STUDYQURAN:74:31/r7.anchor: Those in whose hearts is a disease indicates those who have hypocrisy in their hearts

STUDYQURAN:74:31/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:74:31/r8.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:74:31/r8.claim: Alternatively, the diseased-hearted are those who opposed the Prophet.
STUDYQURAN:74:31/r8.anchor: or those who opposed the Prophet

STUDYQURAN:74:31/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:74:31/r9.speaker: Q, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:74:31/r9.claim: The disbelievers likely ask what God means by this particular number, nineteen.
STUDYQURAN:74:31/r9.anchor: likely refers to the meaning behind this particular number, nineteen

STUDYQURAN:74:31/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:74:31/r10.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:74:31/r10.claim: Revelation’s questions lead some to faith and certainty and others to greater disbelief.
STUDYQURAN:74:31/r10.anchor: the manner in which the questions posed by revelation lead some to certainty and faith and others to greater disbelief

STUDYQURAN:74:31/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:74:31/r11.speaker: Q, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:74:31/r11.claim: No one knows the hosts’ true number; the nineteen guards are only their leaders.
STUDYQURAN:74:31/r11.anchor: None knows the hosts means that none knows their true number (Q, Ṭ), for although

STUDYQURAN:74:31/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:74:31/r12.speaker: Prophet
STUDYQURAN:74:31/r12.claim: A hadith describes Hell arriving on Judgment Day with 70,000 bridles, each held by 70,000 angels.
STUDYQURAN:74:31/r12.anchor: Hell will be brought on that Day [the Day of Judgment] with seventy thousand bridles

STUDYQURAN:74:31/r13.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:74:31/r13.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:74:31/r13.claim: “It is but a reminder” most likely refers to the hosts of God, though it may refer to Saqar or the Quran.
STUDYQURAN:74:31/r13.anchor: It is but a reminder most likely refers to the hosts of thy Lord, but may instead refer to Saqar or the Quran

STUDYQURAN:74:31/r14.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:74:31/r14.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:74:31/r14.claim: If “it” means Saqar, dhikrā can be rendered “admonition.”
STUDYQURAN:74:31/r14.anchor: If taken as a reference to Saqar

TAB-FULL:v23p436/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p436/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v23p436/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that Abū Jahl mocked the count and urged Quraysh to overpower the keepers; God sent the Prophet to confront him, and Abū Jahl was disgraced at Badr.
TAB-FULL:v23p436/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، {عليها تسعة عشر} [المدثر: 30] إلى قوله: {ويزداد الذين آمنوا إيمانا} [المدثر: 31] فلما سمع

TAB-FULL:v23p437/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p437/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p437/r1.claim: The keepers of the Fire are angels, so Abū Jahl’s challenge to overpower one keeper per ten men cannot apply.
TAB-FULL:v23p437/r1.anchor: قال: ثنا ابن زيد، في قوله: {وما جعلنا أصحاب النار إلا ملائكة} [المدثر: 31] قال: ما جعلناهم رجالا

TAB-FULL:v23p437/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p437/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v23p437/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd says they were not men whom one could pair off and overpower as Abū Jahl proposed.
TAB-FULL:v23p437/r2.anchor: قال: ثنا ابن زيد، في قوله: {وما جعلنا أصحاب النار إلا ملائكة} [المدثر: 31] قال: ما جعلناهم رجالا

TAB-FULL:v23p438/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p438/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p438/r1.claim: The count was a trial for the Quraysh polytheists, exposing their denial and boast that they could handle the keepers.
TAB-FULL:v23p438/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، {وما جعلنا عدتهم إلا فتنة للذين كفروا} [المدثر: 31] إلا بلاء

TAB-FULL:v23p438/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p438/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v23p438/r2.claim: Qatāda glosses the count as a trial and says disbelievers mocked it, each boasting that he could deal with the keepers.
TAB-FULL:v23p438/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، {وما جعلنا عدتهم إلا فتنة للذين كفروا} [المدثر: 31] إلا بلاء وإنما جعل الله الخبر عن عدة خزنة جهنم فتنة

TAB-FULL:v23p438/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p438/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v23p438/r3.claim: Mujāhid says the nineteen were made a trial; Abū al-Ashadd al-Jumaḥī boasted none could reach his strength before he drove them from Hell.
TAB-FULL:v23p438/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: {تسعة عشر} [المدثر: 30] قال: جعلوا فتنة، قال أبو الأشد بن الجمحي

TAB-FULL:v23p439/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p439/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p439/r1.claim: The count confirms the Torah and Gospel report about Hell’s keepers, making the People of the Book certain because revelation to Muhammad agrees with their scriptures.
TAB-FULL:v23p439/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {ليستيقن الذين أوتوا الكتاب ويزداد الذين آمنوا إيمانا} [المدثر: 31] قال: وإنها في التوراة والإنجيل تسعة عشر

TAB-FULL:v23p439/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p439/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v23p439/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the Torah and Gospel give the number as nineteen, confirming the People of the Book and increasing believers’ faith.
TAB-FULL:v23p439/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {ليستيقن الذين أوتوا الكتاب ويزداد الذين آمنوا إيمانا} [المدثر: 31] قال: وإنها في التوراة والإنجيل تسعة عشر

TAB-FULL:v23p439/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p439/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v23p439/r3.claim: Mujāhid says they find the number of Hell’s keepers written in their books.
TAB-FULL:v23p439/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: {ليستيقن الذين أوتوا الكتاب} [المدثر: 31] قال: يجدونه مكتوبا عندهم عدة خزنة أهل النار

TAB-FULL:v23p439/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p439/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v23p439/r4.claim: Qatāda says the Qur’an confirms the earlier Torah and Gospel, which give the keepers’ count as nineteen.
TAB-FULL:v23p439/r4.anchor: عن قتادة، {ليستيقن الذين أوتوا الكتاب} [المدثر: 31] يصدق القرآن الكتب التي كانت قبله فيها كلها

TAB-FULL:v23p439/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p439/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v23p439/r5.claim: Qatāda also says the People of the Book become certain when the number agrees with their scriptures.
TAB-FULL:v23p439/r5.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله: {ليستيقن الذين أوتوا الكتاب} [المدثر: 31] قال: ليستيقن أهل الكتاب حين وافق عدة خزنة النار ما في كتبهم

TAB-FULL:v23p439/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p439/r6.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v23p439/r6.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says the Torah and Gospel state that Hell has nineteen keepers.
TAB-FULL:v23p439/r6.anchor: سمعت الضحاك، يقول في قوله: {ليستيقن الذين أوتوا الكتاب} [المدثر: 31] قال: عدة خزنة جهنم

TAB-FULL:v23p439/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p439/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v23p439/r7.claim: Ibn Zayd says the agreement makes the People of the Book certain that Muhammad is God’s Messenger.
TAB-FULL:v23p439/r7.anchor: قال ابن زيد في قوله: {ليستيقن الذين أوتوا الكتاب} [المدثر: 31] أنك رسول الله

TAB-FULL:v23p440/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p440/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p440/r1.claim: Believers increase in faith by affirming that Hell’s keepers number nineteen.
TAB-FULL:v23p440/r1.anchor: وقوله: {ويزداد الذين آمنوا إيمانا} [المدثر: 31] يقول تعالى ذكره: وليزداد الذين آمنوا بالله تصديقا

TAB-FULL:v23p440#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p440#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p440#2/r1.claim: Those with hypocrisy in their hearts and the Quraysh polytheists ask what God intended by this example; they mean the nineteen keepers.
TAB-FULL:v23p440#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {وليقول الذين في قلوبهم مرض والكافرون ماذا أراد الله بهذا مثلا} [المدثر: 31] يقول: حتى يخوفنا

TAB-FULL:v23p440#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p440#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v23p440#2/r2.claim: Qatāda says the disease in their hearts is hypocrisy.
TAB-FULL:v23p440#2/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، {وليقول الذين في قلوبهم مرض} [المدثر: 31] أي نفاق

TAB-FULL:v23p440#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p440#2/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v23p440#2/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd says they ask this because God is frightening them with the nineteen keepers.
TAB-FULL:v23p440#2/r3.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {وليقول الذين في قلوبهم مرض والكافرون ماذا أراد الله بهذا مثلا} [المدثر: 31] يقول: حتى يخوفنا بهؤلاء التسعة عشر

TAB-FULL:v23p440#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p440#3/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p440#3/r1.claim: God leaves the mocking hypocrites and polytheists astray, while guiding believers to the truth and increasing their faith.
TAB-FULL:v23p440#3/r1.anchor: من خلقه فيخذله عن إصابة الحق {ويهدي من يشاء} [يونس: 25] منهم، فيوفقه لإصابة الصواب

TAB-FULL:v23p440#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p440#3/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p440#3/r2.claim: God abandons whom He wills from attaining truth and enables whom He wills to reach what is right.
TAB-FULL:v23p440#3/r2.anchor: من خلقه فيخذله عن إصابة الحق

TAB-FULL:v23p440#3/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p440#3/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p440#3/r3.claim: Only God knows the number and multitude of His forces.
TAB-FULL:v23p440#3/r3.anchor: وما يعلم جنود ربك} [المدثر: 31] من كثرتهم {إلا هو} [البقرة: 163] يعني الله

TAB-FULL:v23p440#3/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p440#3/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v23p440#3/r4.claim: Qatāda explains that only God knows how numerous His forces are.
TAB-FULL:v23p440#3/r4.anchor: عن قتادة، {وما يعلم جنود ربك إلا هو} [المدثر: 31] أي من كثرتهم

TAB-FULL:v23p441/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p441/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p441/r1.claim: The fire described is an admonition for human beings, the descendants of Adam.
TAB-FULL:v23p441/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {وما هي إلا ذكرى للبشر} [المدثر: 31] يعني النار

TAB-FULL:v23p441/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p441/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v23p441/r2.claim: Qatāda identifies the admonition as the Fire.
TAB-FULL:v23p441/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {وما هي إلا ذكرى للبشر} [المدثر: 31] يعني النار

TAB-FULL:v23p441/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p441/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v23p441/r3.claim: Mujāhid also says the phrase refers to the Fire.
TAB-FULL:v23p441/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد، {وما هي إلا ذكرى للبشر} [المدثر: 31] قال: النار

TABATABAI:74:31/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:74:31/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:74:31/r1.claim: The context indicates that people debated the stated number of the keepers and this verse answered them; reports on the occasion follow below.
TABATABAI:74:31/r1.anchor: سياق الآية يشهد على أنهم تكلموا فيما ذكر في الآية من عدد خزان النار فنزلت هذه الآية

TABATABAI:74:31/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:74:31/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:74:31/r2.claim: The companions of the Fire are its keepers, charged with overseeing it and punishing its criminals, as indicated by the preceding count of nineteen.
TABATABAI:74:31/r2.anchor: المراد بأصحاب النار خزنتها الموكلون عليها المتولون لتعذيب المجرمين فيها

TABATABAI:74:31/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:74:31/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:74:31/r3.claim: They are angels able to carry out their charge; criminals cannot hope to resist or overpower them as they could humans.
TABATABAI:74:31/r3.anchor: فليسوا من البشر حتى يرجو المجرمون أن يقاوموهم ويطيقوهم

TABATABAI:74:31/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:74:31/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:74:31/r4.claim: Fitna means a trial or test.
TABATABAI:74:31/r4.anchor: وقوله { وما جعلنا عدتهم إلا فتنة للذين كفروا } الفتنة المحنة والاختبار

TABATABAI:74:31/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:74:31/r5.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:74:31/r5.claim: Some take ‘making’ their number as communicating it, not creating it: God informed people that the keepers numbered nineteen to test disbelievers.
TABATABAI:74:31/r5.anchor: ذكروا أن المراد بالجعل الجعل بحسب الإخبار دون الجعل بحسب التكوين

TABATABAI:74:31/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:74:31/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:74:31/r6.claim: People of the Book become certain the revelation is true when its count matches what their scripture says.
TABATABAI:74:31/r6.anchor: ليوقن أهل الكتاب بأن القرآن النازل عليك حق حيث يجدون ما أخبرنا به من عدة أصحاب النار موافقا لما ذكر فيما عندهم من الكتاب

TABATABAI:74:31/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:74:31/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:74:31/r7.claim: Believers increase in faith when they see the People of the Book confirm the count.
TABATABAI:74:31/r7.anchor: أي بسبب ما يجدون من تصديق أهل الكتاب ذلك

TABATABAI:74:31/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:74:31/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:74:31/r8.claim: The confirmation leaves the People of the Book and believers free of doubt about the revealed report.
TABATABAI:74:31/r8.anchor: ليوقن أهل الكتاب بأن القرآن النازل عليك حق حيث يجدون ما أخبرنا به من عدة أصحاب النار موافقا لما ذكر فيما عندهم من الكتاب

TABATABAI:74:31/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:74:31/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:74:31/r9.claim: The lam introducing mockery marks an outcome, unlike the purposive lam for certainty; the second lam is repeated because mockery is not a divine end except incidentally.
TABATABAI:74:31/r9.anchor: اللام في { ليقول } للعاقبة بخلاف اللام في { ليستيقن } فللتعليل بالغاية

TABATABAI:74:31/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:74:31/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:74:31/r10.claim: Those with sickness in their hearts are hypocrites marked by doubt and rejection; disbelievers are those openly displaying unbelief, including polytheists.
TABATABAI:74:31/r10.anchor: وقد فسروا { الذين في قلوبهم مرض } بالشك والجحود بالمنافقين وفسروا الكافرين بالمتظاهرين بالكفر

TABATABAI:74:31/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:74:31/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:74:31/r11.claim: Their question mocks the description ‘nineteen’; mithal means a description, and they ask how so few could punish most humans and jinn.
TABATABAI:74:31/r11.anchor: وقولهم { ماذا أراد الله بهذا مثلا } أرادوا به التحقير والتهكم يشيرون بهذا إلى قوله تعالى { عليها تسعة عشر } والمثل الوصف

TABATABAI:74:31/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:74:31/r12.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:74:31/r12.claim: Some argue that, if the whole sura is Meccan and hypocrisy began in Medina, the verse foretells later events.
TABATABAI:74:31/r12.anchor: ذكر بعضهم أن قوله تعالى { وليقول الذين في قلوبهم مرض } الآية - بناء على أن السورة بتمامها مكية، وأن النفاق إنما حدث بالمدينة

TABATABAI:74:31/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:74:31/r13.speaker: author
TABATABAI:74:31/r13.claim: The sura’s Meccan origin is established by transmission and claimed consensus; Muqatil’s report that this verse is Medinan is unproven, and its reasoning assumes hypocrisy began in Medina.
TABATABAI:74:31/r13.anchor: أما كون السورة بتمامها مكية فهو المتعين من طريق النقل. وقد ادعي عليه اجماع المفسرين

TABATABAI:74:8-31/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:74:8-31/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:74:8-31/r1.claim: The claim that hypocrisy could arise only from fear or immediate gain is incomplete: motives also include hoped-for future benefit, group loyalty, habit, and other causes.
TABATABAI:74:8-31/r1.anchor: فإن علل النفاق ليست تنحصر في المخافة والإتقاء أو الاستدرار من خير معجل فمن علله الطمع ولو في نفع مؤجل ومنها العصبية والحمية

TABATABAI:74:8-31/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:74:8-31/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:74:8-31/r2.claim: There is no proof that every motive for hypocrisy was absent among Meccan converts; some reportedly believed and recanted, or first believed doubtfully and later became sound.
TABATABAI:74:8-31/r2.anchor: ولا دليل على انتفاء جميع هذه العلل عن جميع من آمن بالنبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم بمكة قبل الهجرة وقد نقل عن بعضهم أنه آمن ثم رجع

TABATABAI:74:8-31/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:74:8-31/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:74:8-31/r3.claim: Meccan 29:10–11 describes people claiming faith, yielding to persecution, and later claiming alliance when God’s support arrives.
TABATABAI:74:8-31/r3.anchor: على أنه تعالى يقول ومن الناس من يقول آمنا بالله فإذا أوذي في الله جعل فتنة الناس كعذاب الله

TABATABAI:74:8-31/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:74:8-31/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:74:8-31/r4.claim: The persecution and trial in 29:10–11 indicate a Meccan setting; promised support need not mean an immediate conquest.
TABATABAI:74:8-31/r4.anchor: والآيتان في سورة مكية وهي سورة العنكبوت، وهما ناطقتان بوجود النفاق فيها

TABATABAI:74:8-31/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:74:8-31/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:74:8-31/r5.claim: Even if the trial refers to persecution in Mecca after the Hijra, those tested had already believed before migrating.
TABATABAI:74:8-31/r5.anchor: واحتمال أن يكون المراد بالفتنة ما وقعت بمكة بعد الهجرة غير ضائر فإن هؤلاء المفتونين بمكة بعد الهجرة إنما كانوا من الذين آمنوا

TABATABAI:74:8-31/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:74:8-31/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:74:8-31/r6.claim: The same reasoning applies to 22:11 if fitna there means punishment, despite that sura’s Medinan origin.
TABATABAI:74:8-31/r6.anchor: وعلى مثل ذلك ينبغي أن يحمل قوله تعالى ومن الناس من يعبد الله على حرف فإن أصابه خير اطمأن به وإن أصابته فتنة انقلب على وجهه

TABATABAI:74:31#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:74:31#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:74:31#2/r1.claim: ‘In this way’ points back to the account of the keepers’ number serving as a trial for disbelievers and a source of certainty and faith for others.
TABATABAI:74:31#2/r1.anchor: الإشارة بذلك إلى مضمون قوله { وما جعلنا عدتهم إلا فتنة } الخ

TABATABAI:74:31#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:74:31#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:74:31#2/r2.claim: The troops are massive hosts created as intermediaries for carrying out God’s commands; God alone knows their reality, nature, number, works, and wisdom.
TABATABAI:74:31#2/r2.anchor: فأفاد بإطلاقه أن العلم بحقيقتهم وخصوصيات خلقتهم وعدتهم وما يعملونه من عمل

TABATABAI:74:31#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:74:31#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:74:31#2/r3.claim: No one may call the troops too few or too many, or criticize their qualities, while ignorant of what they are.
TABATABAI:74:31#2/r3.anchor: فليس لأحد أن يستقل عدتهم أو يستكثر أو يطعن في شيء مما يرجع إلى صفاتهم وهو جاهل بها

TABATABAI:74:31#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:74:31#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:74:31#2/r4.claim: The feminine pronoun returns to the earlier statement that the keepers number nineteen; it is feminine because its predicate is feminine.
TABATABAI:74:31#2/r4.anchor: الضمير راجع إلى ما تقدم من قوله { عليها تسعة عشر } وتأنيثه لتأنيث الخبر

TABATABAI:74:31#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:74:31#2/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:74:31#2/r5.claim: Humans cannot know God’s troops; the disclosed count of the keepers is a reminder for people to take heed.
TABATABAI:74:31#2/r5.anchor: أن البشر لا سبيل لهم إلى العلم بجنود ربك وإنما أخبرنا عن خزنة النار إن عدتهم تسعة عشر ليكون ذكرى لهم يتعظون بها

TABATABAI:74:8-31#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:74:8-31#2/r1.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:74:8-31#2/r1.claim: Other readings take the pronoun to refer to the troops, Saqar, the sura, or worldly fire; the author calls the last the weakest view.
TABATABAI:74:8-31#2/r1.anchor: وقيل الضمير للجنود، وقيل لسقر، وقيل للسورة

TABATABAI:74:8-31#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:74:8-31#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:74:8-31#2/r2.claim: The verse indicates Qur’anic addresses are directed to all humanity.
TABATABAI:74:8-31#2/r2.anchor: وفي الآية دلالة على أن الخطابات القرآنية لعامة البشر.

BURSEVI:v10p180/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p180/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p180/r1.claim: The creatures are described with spear-like fangs, palm-like height, red eyes, and a broad mouth that swallows people and animals; the passage links 99 dragons in the grave to disbelief in God and His 99 names, not necessarily 99 in Hell.
BURSEVI:v10p180/r1.anchor: في فمه أنياب مثل اسنة الرماح وهو طويل كالنخلة السحوق أحمر العينين مثل الدم

BURSEVI:v10p180/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p180/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p180/r2.claim: Nine signifies domination, confinement, and extinction: mercy’s supply ceases for Hell’s inhabitants.

BURSEVI:v10p180/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p180/r3.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v10p180/r3.claim: The Najmī allusion maps corruption of the human soul through deed and knowledge, and its hell of distance, expulsion, curse, and veiling, onto nine causes.
BURSEVI:v10p180/r3.anchor: ومنها ما في التأويلات النجمية : من أن اختلال النفوس البشرية بحسب العمل والعلم

BURSEVI:v10p180/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p180/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p180/r4.claim: The nine causes are seven bodily limbs named in the prostration report plus animal nature, or anger and desire instead of nature, totaling nineteen.
BURSEVI:v10p180/r4.anchor: بقوله عليه السلام أمرت أن أسجد عى سبعة أعضاء وآراب

BURSEVI:v10p180/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p180/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p180/r5.claim: Aṣḥāb al-nār here are managers of Hell and punishers, unlike the phrase in 59:20; Kashf al-asrār instead supplies an omitted word for “keepers of the people of Hell,” which Bursevī calls remote.
BURSEVI:v10p180/r5.anchor: أي المدبرين لأمرها القائمين بتعذيب أهلها فأصحاب النار هنا غير أصحاب النار في قوله تعالى

BURSEVI:v10p180/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p180/r6.speaker: كشف الأسرار
BURSEVI:v10p180/r6.claim: Kashf al-asrār reads an omitted muḍāf, “keepers of the people of the Fire”; Bursevī objects that the angels keep the Fire, not its people.
BURSEVI:v10p180/r6.anchor: وفي كشف الأسرار وما جعلنا خزنة أصحاب النار

BURSEVI:v10p180/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p180/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p180/r7.claim: The keepers are angels, unlike the humans and jinn they punish, so they do not pity them; angels are exceptionally strong and resolute in enforcing God’s command.
BURSEVI:v10p180/r7.anchor: ليخالفوا جنس المعذبين من الثقلين فلا يرقوا لهم ولا يميلوا إليهم

BURSEVI:v10p180/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p180/r8.speaker: النبي
BURSEVI:v10p180/r8.claim: The Prophet is cited as saying each angel’s strength equals that of both heavy species; one can drive a community into the Fire with a mountain on his neck and cast it over them.
BURSEVI:v10p180/r8.anchor: وعن النبي عليه السلام لقوة أحدهم مثل قوة الثقلين يسوق أحدهم الأمة

BURSEVI:v10p180/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p180/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p180/r9.claim: A report says Abū Jahl challenged Quraysh to overpower the keepers when the nineteen was revealed; Abū al-Aswad claimed he could handle seventeen if they dealt with two.
BURSEVI:v10p180/r9.anchor: ويروى إنه لما نزل قوله تعالى

BURSEVI:v10p180/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p180/r10.speaker: أبو الأسود ابن أسيد بن كلدة
BURSEVI:v10p180/r10.claim: Abū al-Aswad boasted he could resist seventeen angels, after groups failed to pull his feet off a hide without tearing it.
BURSEVI:v10p180/r10.anchor: أنا أكفيكم سبعة عشر منهم فاكفوني أنتم

BURSEVI:v10p180/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p180/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p180/r11.claim: The different species means human messengers are sent from our kind to show mercy, while angels are the strongest creatures and most resolute in God’s right.
BURSEVI:v10p180/r11.anchor: فلذا بعث الرسول من جنسنا ليرحم بنا ولأنهم أقوى الخلق وأقومهم بحق الله

BURSEVI:v10p180#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p180#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p180#2/r1.claim: Nineteen is called a fitna because it causes unbelievers to stumble into disbelief; the effect is named for its cause to show their inseparability.
BURSEVI:v10p180#2/r1.anchor: وما جعلنا عددهم إلا العدد الذي تسبب لافتتانهم ووقوعهم في الكفر

BURSEVI:v10p180#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p180#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p180#2/r2.claim: Since jaʿala takes subject and predicate, its second object must match the first; the unbelievers’ being tempted cannot literally be the number, hence the causal reading.
BURSEVI:v10p180#2/r2.anchor: لأن جعل من دواخل المبتدأ والخبر فوجب حمل مفعوله الثاني على الأول

BURSEVI:v10p180#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p180#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p180#2/r3.claim: The trial is not just the angels’ actual number: stating nineteen in the Quran prompts mockery at its smallness against a vast host and sets up the following effects.
BURSEVI:v10p180#2/r3.anchor: بل جعله في القرآن أيضا كذلك وهو الحكم بأن عليها تسعة عشر

BURSEVI:v10p180#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p180#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p180#2/r4.claim: The purpose clause attaches to “making” in the causal sense, and the sīn indicates seeking to attain certainty.
BURSEVI:v10p180#2/r4.anchor: متعلق بالجعل على المعنى المذكور والسين للطلب

BURSEVI:v10p180#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p180#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p180#2/r5.claim: Scripture recipients become certain of the Prophet’s mission and the Quran’s truth by seeing it agree with their scripture.
BURSEVI:v10p180#2/r5.anchor: ليكتسبوا اليقين بنبوته عليه السلام وصدق القرآن لما شاهدوا ما فيه موافقا لما في كتابهم

BURSEVI:v10p180#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p180#2/r6.speaker: عين المعاني
BURSEVI:v10p180#2/r6.claim: ʿAyn al-maʿānī says Jews asked the Prophet about Hell’s keepers and their number, and he replied that there were nineteen.
BURSEVI:v10p180#2/r6.anchor: وفي عين المعاني سأل اليهود رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن خزنة النار

BURSEVI:v10p180#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p180#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p180#3/r1.claim: Believers increase in faith’s quality by seeing the People of the Book affirm the number, or in quantity by adding this belief to belief in the rest of revelation.
BURSEVI:v10p180#3/r1.anchor: أي بزداد إيمانهم كيفية بما رأوا من تسليم أهل الكتاب وتصديقهم إنه كذلك

BURSEVI:v10p180#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p180#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p180#3/r2.claim: Denying doubt after affirming certainty and increased faith intensifies the affirmation and prevents later misgivings from weakening conviction.
BURSEVI:v10p180#3/r2.anchor: تأكيد لما قبله من الاستيقان وازدياد الإيمان فإن نفي ضد الشيء بعد إثبات وقوعه

BURSEVI:v10p180#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p180#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p180#3/r3.claim: The groups’ lack of doubt accompanies different states: denial for the People of the Book, faith for believers; the active participle signals the believers’ constancy.
BURSEVI:v10p180#3/r3.anchor: فإن انتفاء الارتياب من أهل الكتاب مقارن لما ينافيه من الجحود

BURSEVI:v10p180#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p180#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p180#3/r4.claim: The heart’s disease means doubt or hypocrisy; this predicts Medinan hypocrites after the Hijra, since Meccans had been believers, deniers, or doubters.
BURSEVI:v10p180#3/r4.anchor: شك أو نفاق فإن كلا منهما من الأمراض الباطنة

BURSEVI:v10p180#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p180#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p180#3/r5.claim: The unbelievers are those who persist in denial.
BURSEVI:v10p180#3/r5.anchor: المصرون على التكذيب فإن قلت كيف يجوز أن يكون قولهم هذا مقصود الله تعالى

BURSEVI:v10p180#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p180#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p180#3/r6.claim: The lām is consequential rather than a true purpose marker, resolving how God could intend their objectionable speech.
BURSEVI:v10p180#3/r6.anchor: اللام ليست على حقيقتها بل للعاقبة فلا إشكال

BURSEVI:v10p180#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p180#3/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p180#3/r7.claim: Mathalan parses either as a specification of hādhā or its circumstantial accusative, meaning “as an example.”
BURSEVI:v10p180#3/r7.anchor: تمييز لهذا أو حال منه بمعنى ممثلا به كقوله هذه ناقة الله لكم آية

BURSEVI:v10p180#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p180#3/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p180#3/r8.claim: They metaphorically call the strange nineteen an “example,” like an oddly incomplete proverb rather than a round number; their question rejects divine authorship on that basis.
BURSEVI:v10p180#3/r8.anchor: فإطلاق المثل على هذا العدد على سبيل الاستعارة حيث شبهوه بالمثل المضروب

BURSEVI:v10p180#3/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p180#3/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p180#3/r9.claim: This objection is singled out for its special offensiveness although it belongs to the same trial as their other reactions.
BURSEVI:v10p180#3/r9.anchor: وأفراد قولهم هذا بالتعليل مع كونه من باب فتنتهم

BURSEVI:v10p180#3/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p180#3/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p180#3/r10.claim: “Thus” points to the preceding misguidance: God misguides Abū Jahl and companions who reject the keepers and their number.
BURSEVI:v10p180#3/r10.anchor: ذلك إشارة إلى ما قبله من معنى الضلال أي يضل الله من يشاء إضلاله كأبي جهل

BURSEVI:v10p180#3/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p180#3/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p180#3/r11.claim: Their misguidance is not imposed against choice: on seeing the signs they turn their own choice toward error, in keeping with their pre-eternal fixed essences.
BURSEVI:v10p180#3/r11.anchor: لصرف اختياره إلى جنب الضلال عند مشاهدته لآيات الله الناطقة بالحق

BURSEVI:v10p181/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p181/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p181/r1.claim: God guides whom He wills, such as Muhammad’s Companions, as they choose guidance upon seeing the signs.
BURSEVI:v10p181/r1.anchor: هدايته كأصحاب محمد عليه السلام هدايته كائنة

BURSEVI:v10p181/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p181/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p181/r2.claim: In reality, God guides according to pre-eternal disposition; guidance and choosing its direction are eternal states that cannot be otherwise.
BURSEVI:v10p181/r2.anchor: وحقيقته إن الله لا يهي إلا بموجب الهداية الأزلية

BURSEVI:v10p181/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p181/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p181/r3.claim: God’s jund are His hosts of creatures, including angels; jund means army, group, or distinct class of beings.
BURSEVI:v10p181/r3.anchor: الجنود جمع جند بالضم وهو العسكر

BURSEVI:v10p181/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p181/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p181/r4.claim: A hadith states that God has hosts, including honey.
BURSEVI:v10p181/r4.anchor: وفي الحديث إن الله جنودا منها العسل

BURSEVI:v10p181/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p181/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p181/r5.claim: A report says Moses asked how many inhabitants heaven had; God answered twelve tribes, each as numerous as dust.
BURSEVI:v10p181/r5.anchor: سأل ربه عن عدد أهل السماء فقال تعالى اثنا عشر سبطا

BURSEVI:v10p181/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p181/r6.speaker: الأسرار المحمدية
BURSEVI:v10p181/r6.claim: Al-Asrār al-Muḥammadiyya says every place and corner is inhabited by creatures known only to God, citing commands to cover oneself privately and not have intercourse naked.
BURSEVI:v10p181/r6.anchor: ليس في العالم موضع بيت ولا زاوية إلا وهو معمور بما لا يعلمه إلا الله

BURSEVI:v10p181/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p181/r7.speaker: القاشاني
BURSEVI:v10p181/r7.claim: Al-Qāshānī says only God knows the hosts’ number, quantity, quality, and reality because His knowledge encompasses all essences and states.
BURSEVI:v10p181/r7.anchor: وما يعلم عدد الجنود وكميتها وكيفيتها وحقيقتها إلا هو

BURSEVI:v10p181/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p181/r8.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v10p181/r8.claim: The Najmī allusion takes “He alone” as the all-encompassing divine identity, gathering infinitely many determinations of particular names and named particulars.
BURSEVI:v10p181/r8.anchor: وفي التأويلات النجمية : إلا هويته الجامعة لجميع جنود

BURSEVI:v10p181/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p181/r9.speaker: بعض العارفين
BURSEVI:v10p181/r9.claim: Some gnostics distinguish absorbed spirits devoted to glorifying God, spirits governing human and animal bodies, and many task-specific spirits serving worldly and religious needs.
BURSEVI:v10p181/r9.anchor: قال بعض العارفين خلقت الملائكة على مراتب فأرواح ليس لهم عقل إلا تعظيم جناب الله
