BURSEVI:v10p181/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p181/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p181/r10.claim: The passage ranks Gabriel above Azrael, Michael above Gabriel, and Israfil above Michael.
BURSEVI:v10p181/r10.anchor: وإما مراتبهم وتفاوتهم ففيهم الأكبر والكبير فجبريل أكبر من عزرائيل

BURSEVI:v10p181/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p181/r11.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v10p181/r11.claim: Another view says the hosts arrange the upper and lower worlds rather than fight, since creation serves one another.
BURSEVI:v10p181/r11.anchor: وقال بعضهم : هذه الجنود ليست معدة للمحاربة بل هي لترتيب المملكة

BURSEVI:v10p182#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p182#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p182#2/r1.claim: Angels seek forgiveness, bring revelation and law, take souls, inspire hearts, shape and ensoul fetuses, and provide sustenance and rain; every worldly event is effected by appointed angels under angelic governors.
BURSEVI:v10p182#2/r1.anchor: المستغفرين لمن في الأرض ومنهم الموكلون بإيصال الشرائع

BURSEVI:v10p182#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p182#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p182#2/r2.claim: Ordinary people see angels’ stations as celestial bodies, not the angels themselves; people of unveiling witness angels directly at their stations.
BURSEVI:v10p182#2/r2.anchor: ثم إن العامة ما تشهد من هؤلاء الملائكة إلا منازلهم التي هي أجرام الكواكب

BURSEVI:v10p182#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p182#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p182#2/r3.claim: Earthly rulers parallel heavenly rulers; refined correspondences reach them according to preparedness, yielding a just ruler from sound disposition and a tyrant from corrupt disposition, for which they must blame themselves.
BURSEVI:v10p182#2/r3.anchor: ثم اعلم أن الله قد جعل في هذا العالم العنصري خلقا من جنسهم ولاة عليهم نظير العالم العلوي

BURSEVI:v10p182#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p182#2/r4.speaker: الإمام الشعراني
BURSEVI:v10p182#2/r4.claim: Al-Shaʿrānī’s Jawāhir says subjects are beyond counting; some angels on earth never ascend and some in heaven never descend, each knowing its prayer and glorification through God’s inspiration.
BURSEVI:v10p182#2/r4.anchor: ولله تعالى في الأرض ملائكة لا يصعدون إلى السماء أبدا

BURSEVI:v10p182#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p182#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p182#2/r5.claim: The pronoun refers to Saqar, whose description warns people of disbelief’s end; humans are singled out because they are the primary addressees, though jinn are also warned.
BURSEVI:v10p182#2/r5.anchor: إلا تذكرة وعظة وإنذار لهم بسوء عاقبة الكفر والضلال

BURSEVI:v10p182#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p182#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p182#2/r6.claim: Alternatively, it means the keepers’ number: God can punish an uncountable multitude with few angels and needs no helpers; assigning number and hosts reflects wisdom, not need.
BURSEVI:v10p182#2/r6.anchor: ليتذكروا ويعلموا أن الله قادر على أن يعذب الكثير الغير المحصور

BURSEVI:v10p182#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p182#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p182#2/r7.claim: God needs no helpers: turning one hair in the eye or causing pain in one vein would suffice as torment; He appoints hosts for a purpose.
BURSEVI:v10p182#2/r7.anchor: فإنه لو قلب شعرة واحدة في عين ابن آدم أو سلط الألم على عرق واحد

BURSEVI:v10p182#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p182#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p182#2/r8.claim: A further possibility is that the pronoun refers to the verses describing Saqar, which remind people because they contain a warning.
BURSEVI:v10p182#2/r8.anchor: ويجوز أن يعود الضمير إلى الآيات الناطقة بأحوال سقر فإنها تذكرة

TABRISI:74:25-31/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:74:25-31/r15.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة والضحاك
TABRISI:74:25-31/r15.claim: They report that Abu Jahl mocked the nineteen keepers, and Abū al-Asad al-Jumaḥī boasted he could handle seventeen while Quraysh dealt with two; the verse followed.
TABRISI:74:25-31/r15.anchor: فنزل { وما جعلنا أصحاب النار إلا ملائكة } الآية عن ابن عباس وقتادة والضحاك

TABRISI:74:25-31/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:74:25-31/r16.speaker: author
TABRISI:74:25-31/r16.claim: The keepers entrusted with Hell's administration are angels, whose drive is to punish its inhabitants, rather than humans whom people might imagine they could overpower.
TABRISI:74:25-31/r16.anchor: وما جعلنا الموكلين بالنار المتولين تدبيرها إلا ملائكة جعلنا شهوتهم في تعذيب أهل النار

TABRISI:74:25-31/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:74:25-31/r17.speaker: author
TABRISI:74:25-31/r17.claim: The number tests and burdens disbelievers, who should reflect that God is wise and could strengthen even one angel to punish all creatures.
TABRISI:74:25-31/r17.anchor: محنة وتشديدا في التكليف للذين كفروا نعم الله وجحدوا وحدانيته حتى يتفكروا فيعلموا أن الله سبحانه حكيم

TABRISI:74:25-31/r18.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:74:25-31/r18.speaker: author
TABRISI:74:25-31/r18.claim: A further proof of God's power is that a single angel can be assigned to take the souls of all humanity, so nineteen can drive some people to Hell.
TABRISI:74:25-31/r18.anchor: من سلط ملكا واحدا على كافة بني آدم لقبض أرواحهم فلا يغلبونه قادر على سوق بعضهم إلى النار

TABRISI:74:31/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:74:31/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:74:31/r1.claim: Jews and Christians can confirm the report and Muḥammad's truthfulness because it matches their scriptures, though he neither read them nor learned from them.
TABRISI:74:31/r1.anchor: من اليهود والنصارى أنه حق وأن محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم صادق من حيث أخبر بما هو في كتبهم من غير قراءة لها

TABRISI:74:31/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:74:31/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:74:31/r2.claim: Believers grow in faith in the number and in Muḥammad's prophethood when the People of the Book confirm it.
TABRISI:74:31/r2.anchor: إذا أخبرهم أهل الكتاب أنه مثل ما في كتابهم

TABRISI:74:31/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:74:31/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:74:31/r3.claim: The purpose is that both believers and those not yet believing in Muḥammad become certain of his prophethood and do not doubt the keepers' number through reflection.
TABRISI:74:31/r3.anchor: وليستيقن من لم يؤمن بمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ومن آمن به صحة نبوته إذا تدبروا وتفكروا

TABRISI:74:31/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:74:31/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:74:31/r4.claim: The lām marks an eventual outcome: hypocrites and unbelievers end up asking what God intended by this description and number.
TABRISI:74:31/r4.anchor: اللام هنا لام العاقبة أي عاقبة أمر هؤلاء أن يقولوا هذا يعني المنافقين والكافرين

TABRISI:74:31/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:74:31/r5.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:74:31/r5.claim: Alternatively, the lām expresses purpose: they ask what it means, reflect, and their reflection leads them to faith.
TABRISI:74:31/r5.anchor: وقيل: معناه ولأن يقولوا ماذا أراد الله بهذا الوصف والعدد ويتدبروه فيؤدي بهم التدبر

TABRISI:74:31/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:74:31/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:74:31/r6.claim: As with the angels and their number, the test brings error or guidance to light; God is named as its source because the testing obligation comes from Him.
TABRISI:74:31/r6.anchor: تكلف الخلق ليظهر الضلال والهدى وأضافهما إلى نفسه لأن سبب ذلك التكليف وهو من جهته

TABRISI:74:31/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:74:31/r7.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:74:31/r7.claim: Alternatively, God misleads whom He wills away from the path to Paradise and reward, and guides whom He wills to it.
TABRISI:74:31/r7.anchor: وقيل: يضل عن طريق الجنة والثواب من يشاء ويهدي من يشاء إليه

TABRISI:74:31/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:74:31/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:74:31/r8.claim: Only God knows the innumerable forces He commands; the nineteen were selected by wisdom, not because His forces are few.
TABRISI:74:31/r8.anchor: ما يعلم جنود ربك من كثرتها أحد إلا هو ولم يجعل خزنة النار تسعة عشر لقلة جنوده

TABRISI:74:31/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:74:31/r9.speaker: مقاتل
TABRISI:74:31/r9.claim: Miqātil says this answers Abū Jahl's taunt that Muḥammad had only nineteen helpers.
TABRISI:74:31/r9.anchor: وقيل: هذا جواب أبي جهل حين قال ما لمحمد أعوان إلا تسعة عشر عن مقاتل

TABRISI:74:31/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:74:31/r10.speaker: عطاء
TABRISI:74:31/r10.claim: ʿAṭāʾ says only God knows the number of angels made to torment Hell's inhabitants; the nineteen keepers have further forces known only to Him.
TABRISI:74:31/r10.anchor: وما يعلم عدة الملائكة الذين خلقهم الله لتعذيب أهل النار إلا الله عن عطاء

TABRISI:74:31/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:74:31/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:74:31/r11.claim: Saqar is a reminder and admonition for people to avoid what would merit it.
TABRISI:74:31/r11.anchor: تذكرة وموعظة للعالم ليتذكروا فيتجنبوا ما يستوجبون به ذلك

TABRISI:74:31/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:74:31/r12.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:74:31/r12.claim: Alternatively, the earthly fire is a reminder of the afterlife's fire, prompting people to beware it.
TABRISI:74:31/r12.anchor: وقيل: معناه وما هذه النار في الدنيا إلا تذكرة للبشر من نار الآخرة

TABRISI:74:31/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:74:31/r13.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:74:31/r13.claim: Another view takes the reminder to be this sūra itself.
TABRISI:74:31/r13.anchor: وقيل: ما هذه السورة إلا تذكرة للناس

TABRISI:74:31/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:74:31/r14.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:74:31/r14.claim: Another view says the nineteen angels are a lesson in God's complete power and a warning against sins.
TABRISI:74:31/r14.anchor: وقيل: وما هذه الملائكة التسعة عشر إلا عبرة للخلق يستدلون بذلك على كمال قدرة الله

THALABI:v10p74/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p74/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p74/r1.claim: The guardians of the Fire are angels, not men; no one could overpower the angels.
THALABI:v10p74/r1.anchor: فأنزل الله سبحانه وتعالى وما جعلنا أصحاب النار إلا ملائكة لا رجالا إذ من فمن ذا يغلب الملائكة

THALABI:v10p74/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p74/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p74/r2.claim: The number nineteen tests disbelievers, who reject it and boast that they can deal with the guardians.
THALABI:v10p74/r2.anchor: وما جعلنا عدتهم عددهم إلا فتنة للذين كفروا لتكذيبهم بذلك وقول بعضهم أنا أكفيكموه

THALABI:v10p74/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p74/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p74/r3.claim: The number confirms the People of the Book because the Torah and Gospel state that the guardians number nineteen.
THALABI:v10p74/r3.anchor: ليستيقن الذين أوتوا الكتاب لأنه مكتوب في التوراة والإنجيل أنهم تسعة عشر

THALABI:v10p74/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p74/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p74/r4.claim: The disclosure strengthens believers' faith and leaves the People of the Book and believers without doubt.
THALABI:v10p74/r4.anchor: ويزداد الذين آمنوا إيمانا ولا يرتاب يشك الذين أوتوا الكتاب والمؤمنون

THALABI:v10p74/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p74/r5.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
THALABI:v10p74/r5.claim: Most commentators take the sickness in hearts as doubt and hypocrisy.
THALABI:v10p74/r5.anchor: قاله أكثر المفسرين، وقال الحسين بن الفضل: السورة مكية

THALABI:v10p74/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p74/r6.speaker: الحسين بن الفضل
THALABI:v10p74/r6.claim: Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl says the sickness means opposition, not hypocrisy, since the sura is Meccan and there was no hypocrisy in Mecca.
THALABI:v10p74/r6.anchor: وقال الحسين بن الفضل: السورة مكية ولم يكن بمكة البتة نفاق فالمرض في هذه الخلاف لا النفاق.

THALABI:v10p74/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p74/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p74/r7.claim: The Meccan polytheists are the ones who asked what God meant by this example.
THALABI:v10p74/r7.anchor: ماذا أراد الله بهذا مثلا إنما قاله مشركو مكة

THALABI:v10p74/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p74/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p74/r8.claim: Only God knows the full number of His hosts.
THALABI:v10p74/r8.anchor: وما يعلم جنود ربك جموع ربك إلا هو

THALABI:v10p74/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p74/r9.speaker: مقاتل
THALABI:v10p74/r9.claim: Mujahid says this answers Abu Jahl's taunt asking whether Muhammad had no helpers beyond nineteen.
THALABI:v10p74/r9.anchor: قال مقاتل: هذا جواب أبي جهل حين قال: أما لمحمد أعوان إلا تسعة عشر.

THALABI:v10p74/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p74/r10.speaker: النبي
THALABI:v10p74/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas reports that at Hunayn an angel brought God's command; the Prophet asked Gabriel if he knew him, and Gabriel said he did not know every angel.
THALABI:v10p74/r10.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقسم غنائم حنين وجبرئيل إلى جنبه

THALABI:v10p74/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p74/r11.speaker: موسى
THALABI:v10p74/r11.claim: Al-Awzaʿi transmits Moses asking about the heavenly angels: God says there are twelve tribes, each as numerous as grains of sand.
THALABI:v10p74/r11.anchor: سمعت الأوزاعي يقول: قال موسى عليه السلام: يا رب من معك في السماء؟ قال: ملائكتي

THALABI:v10p74/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p74/r12.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p74/r12.claim: The Fire is an admonition for humankind.
THALABI:v10p74/r12.anchor: وما هي يعني النار إلا ذكرى للبشر عضة للناس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p435/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p435/r4.speaker: أبو بكر بن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p435/r4.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says the angels are the Fire’s keepers; Muslims described them as jailers, and ḥaddād means a jailer who confines people.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p435/r4.anchor: قال (أبو بكر) (¬7) بن الأنباري: لما أنزل الله تعالى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p435/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p435/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p435/r5.claim: The term ḥaddād means a jailer; the angels are keepers of the Fire.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p435/r5.anchor: والمعنى: عس (¬1) الملائكة إلى السجانين من النار

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p435/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p435/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p435/r6.claim: The phrase means that no one can endure or overcome the angels.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p438/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p438/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p438/r1.claim: Their count is small; Muqatil glosses it as their fewness.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p438/r1.anchor: أي: عددهم في القلة، وقال مقاتل: قلتهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p438/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p438/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p438/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the number was a trial that led the disbelievers astray into making their taunts.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p438/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد ضلاله لهم حتى قالوا ما قالوا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p438/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p438/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p438/r3.claim: Abu Ishaq interprets fitna as a test, since some claimed they could handle the keepers.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p438/r3.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: أي محنة؛ لأن بعضهم قال: أنا أكفي هؤلاء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p438/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p438/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p438/r4.claim: God made the number a trial so disbelievers would expose the denial within them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p438/r4.anchor: والمعنى: جعلنا هذه العدة محنة لهم؟ ليظهروا ما عندهم من التكذيب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p438/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p438/r5.speaker: ابن الأنباري، الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p438/r5.claim: Ibn al-Anbari and al-Zajjaj say the number is in the People of the Book’s scripture, confirming Muhammad’s truth because he reported it without reading a book.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p438/r5.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري (¬7)، والزجاج (¬8)؛ لأن عدد الخزنة في كتابهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p438/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p438/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p438/r6.claim: The purpose-lām in “so that they may be certain” attaches to the statement that there are nineteen keepers.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p438/r6.anchor: واللام في قوله: {ليستيقن} تتعلق بقوله: {عليها تسعة عشر}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p438/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p438/r7.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p438/r7.claim: Al-Kalbi says the number nineteen was already in the scriptures of the People of the Book.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p438/r7.anchor: قال الكلبي: كان ذلك في كتب أهل الكتاب: تسعة عشر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p438/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p438/r8.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p438/r8.claim: Al-Farra reads this as certainty added to their existing certainty, since their scripture also gives nineteen keepers.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p438/r8.anchor: وقال الفراء: {ليستيقن الذين أوتوا الكتاب} يقينا إلى يقينهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p438/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p438/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p438/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas says this refers to the believers among the People of the Book.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p438/r9.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يعني الذين آمنوا منهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p439/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p439/r1.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p439/r1.claim: Al-Farra says the count was likewise in the People of the Book’s scriptures, so believing scripturalists gain confidence in Muhammad when his report matches theirs.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p439/r1.anchor: قال الفراء: لأنهما (¬6) في كتاب أهل الكتاب كذلك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p439/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p439/r2.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p439/r2.claim: Abu Ishaq says believers increase in faith whenever they affirm what comes in God’s Book, including Muhammad’s report of the keepers’ number.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p439/r2.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: لأنهم كلما صدقوا بما يأتي في كتاب الله زاد إيمانهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p439/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p439/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p439/r3.claim: The purpose is that the People of the Book and believers not doubt that Hell’s keepers number nineteen.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p439/r3.anchor: أي لكيلا (¬1) يشك هؤلاء في أن خزنة جهنم تسعة عشر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p439/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p439/r4.speaker: الكلبي، مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p439/r4.claim: Al-Kalbi and Muqatil identify those with diseased hearts as the doubting hypocrites of Medina.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p439/r4.anchor: أي: شك ونفاق من منافقي المدينة (¬2)، (هذا قول ... (¬3)، والكلبي (¬4)، ومقاتل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p439/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p439/r5.speaker: الحسين بن الفضل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p439/r5.claim: Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl rejects hypocrisy as the meaning because the sura is Meccan and there was no hypocrisy in Mecca.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p439/r5.anchor: وذكر عن الحسين بن الفضل أنه (¬7) قال: هذه السورة مكية، ولم يكن بمكة نفاق

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p439/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p439/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p439/r6.claim: He defends the exegetes: God knew hypocrisy would arise and foretold what would happen.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p439/r6.anchor: وقول المفسرين صحيح وإن أنكره؛ لأنه كان في معلوم الله تعالى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p440/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p440/r1.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p440/r1.claim: Muqatil identifies the disbelievers as the Arab polytheists.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p440/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p440/r2.speaker: عطاء، الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p440/r2.claim: Ata and al-Kalbi identify them as Jews and Christians; the author prefers Muqatil because they believe their scripture and would not deny the count.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p440/r2.anchor: وقال عطاء (¬1)، (والكلبي (¬2)) (¬3): يعني الكفار من اليهود

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p440/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p440/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p440/r3.claim: Here mathal means the account itself; unlike 2:26, no parable is explicitly cited, so the disbelievers ask what God intends by this account.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p440/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p440/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p440/r4.claim: In the examples from al-Raʿd and al-Fatḥ, mathal also means an account, report, or story.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p440/r4.anchor: ومنه قوله: {مثل الجنة التي وعد المتقون} [الرعد: 35]، أي: حديثها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p442/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p442/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p442/r1.claim: God misleads those who deny the keepers’ number and guides those who affirm and believe it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p442/r1.anchor: أي كما أضل من أنكر عدد الخزنة، ولم يؤمن به

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p442/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p442/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p442/r2.claim: The statement answers Abu Jahl’s claim that Muhammad had only nineteen troops, emphasizing that God’s forces are too numerous to count.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p442/r2.anchor: وأنزل في قول أبي جهل: أما لمحمد من الجنود إلا تسعة عشر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p442/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p442/r3.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p442/r3.claim: Muqatil explains the reference to God’s troops as emphasizing their vast number.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p442/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p442/r4.speaker: عطاء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p442/r4.claim: Ata says God’s troops are angels created to punish Hell’s inhabitants, whose number only God knows; the nineteen keepers have innumerable angelic auxiliaries.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p442/r4.anchor: وقال عطاء: "جنود ربك" يعني: من الملائكة الذين خلقهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p442/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p442/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p442/r5.claim: The passage returns to mention Saqar as a reminder for humankind.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p442/r5.anchor: ثم رجع إلى ذكر سقر فقال: {وما هي إلا ذكرى للبشر}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p442/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p442/r6.speaker: ابن عباس، مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p442/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas and Muqatil gloss it as admonition and reminder for the world.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p442/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس (¬3)، (ومقاتل (¬4)) (¬5)، أي: موعظة وتذكرة للعالم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p442/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p442/r7.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p442/r7.claim: Abu Ishaq says the Fire in this world reminds people of the Fire in the afterlife.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p442/r7.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: جاء في التفسير أن النار في الدنيا تذكر النار في

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:29-31/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:29-31/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:29-31/r4.claim: The keepers of the Fire are angels, not men, so no one can overpower them.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:29-31/r4.anchor: { وما جعلنا أصحاب النار إلا ملائكة } لا رجالا، فمن ذا يغلب الملائكة؟

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:29-31/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:29-31/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:29-31/r5.claim: The small number tests disbelievers, who scoff that Muhammad has only nineteen helpers.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:29-31/r5.anchor: { وما جعلنا عدتهم } عددهم في القلة { إلا فتنة للذين كفروا } لأنهم قالوا: ما أعوان محمد إلا تسعة عشر

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:29-31/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:29-31/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:29-31/r6.claim: People given scripture gain certainty because Muhammad’s message agrees with their books.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:29-31/r6.anchor: { ليستيقن الذين أوتوا الكتاب } ليعلموا أن ما أتى به النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم موافق لما في كتبهم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:29-31/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:29-31/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:29-31/r7.claim: Believers grow in faith by affirming the Messenger and the reported number of Hell’s keepers.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:29-31/r7.anchor: { ويزداد الذين آمنوا } لأنهم يصدقون بما أتى به الرسول عليه السلام، وبعدد خزنة النار

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:29-31/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:29-31/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:29-31/r8.claim: People of scripture and believers do not doubt the number Muhammad reported.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:29-31/r8.anchor: { ولا يرتاب الذين أوتوا الكتاب والمؤمنون } أي: لا يشكون في أن عددهم على ما أخبر به محمد عليه السلام

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:29-31/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:29-31/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:29-31/r9.claim: The sickness in their hearts is doubt; they and the disbelievers ask what God intends by this number as an example.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:29-31/r9.anchor: { وليقول الذين في قلوبهم مرض } شك { والكافرون ماذا أراد الله بهذا مثلا } أي: شيء أراد الله بهذا العدد وتخصيصه؟

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:29-31/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:29-31/r10.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:29-31/r10.claim: God misguides and guides whom He wills, as He has led the deniers astray for their rejection.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:29-31/r10.anchor: { كذلك } كما أضلهم الله بتكذيبهم { يضل الله من يشاء ويهدي من يشاء

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:29-31/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:29-31/r11.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:29-31/r11.claim: This answers those who asked why Muhammad’s helpers number only nineteen: only God knows His forces.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:29-31/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:29-31/r12.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:29-31/r12.claim: The Fire reminds people in this life of the Fire awaiting them in the Hereafter.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:29-31/r12.anchor: { وما هي } أي: النار { إلا ذكرى للبشر } أي: إنها تذكرهم في الدنيا النار في الآخرة.

QASHANI:74:29-31/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:74:29-31/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:74:29-31/r3.claim: Angelic keepers can overpower the people of the fire because the sensible realm is under the dominion and service of the malakut realm.
QASHANI:74:29-31/r3.anchor: لتغلبهم وتقهرهم فإن عالم الملك في قهر عالم الملكوت وتسخيره

QASHANI:74:29-31/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:74:29-31/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:74:29-31/r4.claim: The number tests those veiled from truth, increasing their veiling and doubt.
QASHANI:74:29-31/r4.anchor: لابتلاء المحجوبين وتعذيبهم وزيادة احتجابهم وارتيابهم

QASHANI:74:29-31/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:74:29-31/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:74:29-31/r5.claim: Those given the discriminating intellect become certain, while believers with intellectual certainty increase in faith through unveiling and direct witnessing and do not doubt.
QASHANI:74:29-31/r5.anchor: ويزداد الذين آمنوا } الإيمان اليقيني العلمي { إيمانا } بالكشف والعيان فلا يرتابوا

QASHANI:74:29-31/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:74:29-31/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:74:29-31/r6.claim: Alternatively, imitators who received scripture gain certainty, realized people deepen realization, and the ignorant with neither verified nor imitative belief doubt.
QASHANI:74:29-31/r6.anchor: أو ليستيقن الذين اوتوا الكتاب من المقلدين ويزداد المحققون تحقيقهم ولا يرتابوا كما ارتاب الجاهلون

QASHANI:74:29-31/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:74:29-31/r7.speaker: author
QASHANI:74:29-31/r7.claim: The sick-hearted are hypocrites and doubters in simple ignorance; disbelievers are veiled by false beliefs in compounded ignorance.
QASHANI:74:29-31/r7.anchor: نفاق وشك من الجاهلين بالجهل البسيط

QASHANI:74:29-31/r8.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:74:29-31/r8.speaker: author
QASHANI:74:29-31/r8.claim: They call the number a strange, astonishing example; it is among the causes by which God manifests the deviation of the deviant and guidance of the guided.
QASHANI:74:29-31/r8.anchor: أي: شيئا عجيبا كالمثل المستغرب المتعجب منه

QASHANI:74:29-31/r9.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:74:29-31/r9.speaker: author
QASHANI:74:29-31/r9.claim: God guides people of primordial felicity and misguides those of primordial wretchedness.
QASHANI:74:29-31/r9.anchor: يضل الله من يشاء } من أهل الشقاوة الأصلية

QASHANI:74:29-31/r10.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:74:29-31/r10.speaker: author
QASHANI:74:29-31/r10.claim: Only God knows the number, quantity, quality, and reality of His forces, since His knowledge encompasses essences and their states.
QASHANI:74:29-31/r10.anchor: عددها وكميتها وكيفيتها وحقيقتها إلا هو لإحاطة علمه بالماهيات وأحوالها

QASHANI:74:29-31/r11.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:74:29-31/r11.speaker: author
QASHANI:74:29-31/r11.claim: The pronoun in “it is only a reminder” refers to Saqar, continuing the description begun by “I shall roast him in Saqar.”
QASHANI:74:29-31/r11.anchor: وما سقر متصل بقوله: سأصليه سقر من تتمة أوصافه

QASHANI:74:31/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:74:31/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:74:31/r1.claim: The clause from “We made” through “except Him” is an explanatory parenthesis about the keepers of Hell.
QASHANI:74:31/r1.anchor: { إلا هو } اعتراض لبيان حال الزبانية

QASHANI:74:31/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:74:31/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:74:31/r2.claim: The passage concludes that it is only a reminder for humankind.

ELMALILI:74:26-31/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:74:26-31/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:74:26-31/r11.claim: God has powers and forces humans cannot yet understand, whose reality He alone knows; believers should accept the revealed report unconditionally.
ELMALILI:74:26-31/r11.anchor: Allah teâlâ’nın şimdi sizin tamamen bilip anlayamayacağınız ve ileride tezahür edecek öyle kuvvet ve kudretleri vardır ki onların hakikatini ancak kendisi bilir

ELMALILI:74:26-31/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:74:26-31/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:74:26-31/r12.claim: Ashab al-nar means the fire's keepers or guardians, not its eternal inhabitants; these are the angelic keepers of Hell, led by Malik.
ELMALILI:74:26-31/r12.anchor: ebediyen o ateş içinde kalıp yanacak

ELMALILI:74:26-31/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:74:26-31/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:74:26-31/r13.claim: The keepers are the stern angels described in al-Tahrim, called the keepers of Hell and led by Malik.
ELMALILI:74:26-31/r13.anchor: ve reisleri Mâlik olan zebâni meleklerdir

ELMALILI:74:26-31/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:74:26-31/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:74:26-31/r14.claim: Their number means the nineteen just mentioned.
ELMALILI:74:26-31/r14.anchor: yani adetlerinden murad da zikrolunan تِسْعَةَ عَشَرَ adedi olduğu vâzıhtır

ELMALILI:74:26-31/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:74:26-31/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:74:26-31/r15.claim: Making the number nineteen, while leaving unclear whether it counts individuals or kinds, is a trial for unbelievers.
ELMALILI:74:26-31/r15.anchor: sayılarının on dokuz yapılması veya şahısları mı nevileri mi ne olduğu tâyin edilmeyerek sade on dokuz adediyle muammâ hâlinde ifade ve ihbar olunması mücerred kâfirlere bir mihnet ve imtihan içindir

ELMALILI:74:26-31/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:74:26-31/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:74:26-31/r16.claim: Those who know scripture and the limits of present human judgment have doubts dispelled, while receptive believers gain faith and are guided toward success and salvation.
ELMALILI:74:26-31/r16.anchor: kitap ve peygamberin ne demek olduğunu ve istikbal işinin bugünkü kıyaslarla bilinemeyeceğini bilenlerin işkillerini kesecek ve iman kābiliyeti olanların imanlarını artırarak muvaffakiyet ve halâslarına bâ‘is olacak

ELMALILI:74:26-31/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:74:26-31/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:74:26-31/r17.claim: People without faith or with diseased hearts may treat the report as a puzzling riddle and use it to ridicule and deny revelation.
ELMALILI:74:26-31/r17.anchor: alay ve inkâra sapmalarına sebep olabilirse de

ELMALILI:74:26-31/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:74:26-31/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:74:26-31/r18.claim: One occasion report says Abu Jahl mocked the nineteen guardians and challenged Quraysh's strong men; Abu al-Ashadd claimed he could defeat seventeen while others handled two, after which the verse identified them as angels.
ELMALILI:74:26-31/r18.anchor: Ebû Cehil Kureyş’e şöyle demişti: “Analarınız ağlasın, [^7] Ebû Kebşe’nin oğlunu işitiyorum

ELMALILI:74:26-31/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:74:26-31/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:74:26-31/r19.claim: The report says the clarification that the keepers were angels was revealed in response to the boast that men could overpower them.
ELMALILI:74:26-31/r19.anchor: nâzil oldu. “Onlar sizin tâkat getireceğiniz adamlar değil, melâikedir” diye haber verildi

ELMALILI:74:26-31/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:74:26-31/r20.speaker: author
ELMALILI:74:26-31/r20.claim: The account also says verses from Surat al-Qiyama were revealed concerning Abu Jahl.
ELMALILI:74:26-31/r20.anchor: Ve Ebû Cehil hakkında da Sûre-i Kıyâme’deki

ELMALILI:74:26-31/r21.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:74:26-31/r21.speaker: author
ELMALILI:74:26-31/r21.claim: Tirmidhi and Ibn Mardawayh report from Jabir that Jews asked companions whether their Prophet knew the keepers' number; the Prophet indicated ten and then nine with his fingers.
ELMALILI:74:26-31/r21.anchor: Tirmizî ve İbn Merdûye’nin Hazret-i Câbir’den bir rivayetlerine göre: Yahudîlerden bazı kimseler Peygamber’in ashabından bazılarına

ELMALILI:74:26-31/r22.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:74:26-31/r22.speaker: author
ELMALILI:74:26-31/r22.claim: Some infer a Medinan date because Jews lived in Medina, but Elmalılı considers the inference weak: companions could visit Medina or Jews could visit Mecca, and the story may be explanatory rather than an occasion of revelation.
ELMALILI:74:26-31/r22.anchor: ashabdan bazılarının Medine’ye veya Yahudîlerden bazılarının Mekke’ye gitmiş olmaları melhuz bulunduğundan bu istidlâlin zayıf olduğu derkârdır

ELMALILI:74:26-31/r23.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:74:26-31/r23.speaker: author
ELMALILI:74:26-31/r23.claim: Junud is the plural of jund, meaning soldiers, helpers, troops, or armies; it is associated with military strength and harshness and derives from jund, rocky hard terrain.
ELMALILI:74:26-31/r23.anchor: cem‘idir ki asker ve bir adamın a‘vân u ensârı, alay ve ordu mânalarına gelir

ELMALILI:74:26-31/r24.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:74:26-31/r24.speaker: author
ELMALILI:74:26-31/r24.claim: Only God knows His forces; the incomprehensible number is meant to establish unconditional belief in this truth.
ELMALILI:74:26-31/r24.anchor: İşte o muammânın asıl sırrı ve fâidesi bu hakikate mutlak bir imanı temin etmektir

ELMALILI:74:26-31/r25.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:74:26-31/r25.speaker: author
ELMALILI:74:26-31/r25.claim: It may refer either to Saqar or to these verses; in either case it is a reminder and benefit for humanity.
ELMALILI:74:26-31/r25.anchor: ancak beşer için, beşerin menfaati için bir öğüt, bir muhtıradır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:31/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:31/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:31/r1.claim: When the previous verse was revealed, mockers claimed that their large crowd could overpower the nineteen guards and keep them from casting people into Hell.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:31/r1.anchor: Bir önceki âyet indiğinde müşrikler, alay yollu sözlerle kendilerinin kalabalık bir topluluk olduğunu, dolayısıyla on dokuz bekçinin güç yetirip onları cehenneme atamayacağını söylemişlerdi.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:31/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:31/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:31/r2.claim: The verse answers that angels manage Hell’s affairs and cannot be overpowered by the mockers.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:31/r2.anchor: cehennem işlerine bakmakla meleklerin görevlendirildiği bildirilerek onların meleklere güç yetirmelerinin mümkün olmadığına dikkat çekilmiştir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:31/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:31/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:31/r3.claim: The number nineteen is presented as a means of testing people.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:31/r3.anchor: Âyette on dokuz sayısının verilmesi sadece bir imtihan vesilesi olarak gösterilmiştir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:31/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:31/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:31/r4.claim: Some People of the Book recognized the information as consonant with the spirit of the Torah and Gospel; Jews and Christians, like Muslims, believe in the afterlife, unlike polytheists.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:31/r4.anchor: “Kendilerine kitap verilenler iyiden iyiye öğrensinler” şeklinde çevirdiğimiz cümle bazı Ehl-i kitap mensuplarının, bu âyetlerde verilen bilgileri Tevrat ve İncil’in ruhuna uygun bulduklarını gösterir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:31/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:31/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:31/r5.claim: One view identifies those with diseased hearts as hypocrites; although there were no hypocrites in Mecca, the verse foretells their later emergence in Medina.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:31/r5.anchor: Bunlar münafıklardır; her ne kadar Mekke döneminde münafık yok idiyse de âyet ileride böyle bir grubun ortaya çıkacağını haber vermiştir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:31/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:31/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:31/r6.claim: Another view identifies them as polytheists uncertain whether to believe in the Prophet.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:31/r6.anchor: “Kalplerinde hastalık bulunanlar” Hz. Peygamber’e iman edip etmeme hususunda tereddütte kalan müşriklerdir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:31/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:31/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:31/r7.claim: The “parable” in the polytheists’ question refers to the verse 30 account of the nineteen guardians of Hell.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:31/r7.anchor: Müşriklerin “Allah bu sayı misaliyle ne demek istemiş olabilir?” anlamındaki sorusunda geçen misalden maksat, cehennemin on dokuz görevlisiyle ilgili 30. âyetteki anlatımdır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:31/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:31/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:31/r8.claim: The commentary reports Ibn Ashur’s view that mathal can also mean “report,” “speech,” or “information.”

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:31/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:31/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:31/r9.claim: Since polytheists disbelieved the Qur’an, they could not be sincerely asking about information they considered true; their question denies that God would say such a thing.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:31/r9.anchor: Zira onlar Kur’an’a inanmadıkları için Kur’an’ın verdiği bilgiyi doğru sayarak bu bilgiye dayalı samimi soru sormaları da mümkün değildir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:31/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:31/r10.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:31/r10.claim: God guides through scriptures and prophets; those who accept His direction are saved, while those who freely disobey and follow their desires fail to benefit from it and persist in error.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:31/r10.anchor: O’nun irşad ve yardımlarından yararlananlar doğru yolu bularak kurtuluşa ererler; kendi iradeleriyle Allah’ın emrine karşı geldikleri ve nefislerine uydukları için

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:31/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:31/r11.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:31/r11.claim: “The armies of your Lord” generally means all visible and invisible beings who submit to God’s will and execute His commands; here it specifically means Hell’s attendants.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:31/r11.anchor: “Rabbinin orduları”ndan maksat genel anlamda Allah’ın iradesine teslim olup buyruklarını icra eden görünür ve görünmez varlıklar; özel olarak bu bağlamda cehennemdeki hizmetleri yerine getiren görevlilerdir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:31/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:31/r12.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:31/r12.claim: Only God knows the angels’ number, strength, and other qualities, which belong to the unseen; this answers those mocking the guards’ count.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:31/r12.anchor: gayb âleminden olan meleklerin sayılarını, güçlerini ve diğer özelliklerini Allah’tan başka kimsenin bilemeyeceği ifade edilmektedir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:31/r13.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:31/r13.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:31/r13.claim: The phrase also signals the Prophet’s exalted status and that some of God’s armies will aid his victory.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:31/r13.anchor: “Rabbinin orduları” tamlaması aynı zamanda Hz. Peygamber’in şanının yüceliğine, bu ordulardan bir kısmının onun zaferi için yardımcı olacaklarına işaret eder.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:31/r14.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:31/r14.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:31/r14.claim: The final statement presents the descriptions of Hell’s guardians as a reminder of God’s power meant to lead people to obey Him.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:31/r14.anchor: Âyetin son cümlesi, cehennem bekçileri, onların sayıları ve diğer anlatılanların tümünün insanlara Allah’ın gücünü hatırlatmak ve O’na itaat etmelerini sağlamak için bir öğüt ve nasihat olduğunu ifade etmektedir.

BURHAN:v3p268#2/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p268#2/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p268#2/r3.claim: The order of the People of the Book and believers is also cited among examples of progression.
BURHAN:v3p268#2/r3.anchor: وكقوله ﴿ ولا يرتاب الذين أوتوا الكتاب والمؤمنون ﴾ 8 الآية وبهذا يتبين فساد استدلال المعتزلة

BURHAN:v1p108/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p108/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p108/r4.claim: Aṣḥāb al-nār normally means the people of the Fire; in this verse it refers to the Fire's keepers.
BURHAN:v1p108/r4.anchor: وكل ما فى القرآن من أصحاب النار فهم اهل النار إلا قوله ﴿ وما جعلنا أصحاب النار إلا ملائكة ﴾

BURHAN:v3p16/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p16/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p16/r6.claim: The phrase is listed among examples in the section on repetition used for magnification and awe.

ITQAN:v2p418/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p418/r6.speaker: ابن فارس
ITQAN:v2p418/r6.claim: Aṣḥāb al-nār generally means Hell's inhabitants, but in 74:31 it refers to the angels who keep Hell.
ITQAN:v2p418/r6.anchor: وكل ما فيه من أصحاب النار فأهلها إلا ﴿ وما جعلنا أصحاب النار إلا ملائكة ﴾ فالمراد خزنتها

SULAMI:v2p359#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p359#2/r1.speaker: القاسم
SULAMI:v2p359#2/r1.claim: God tells Muhammad that people cannot grasp created beings, so how could they grasp the divine names and attributes?
SULAMI:v2p359#2/r1.anchor: قال القاسم : قال الله تعالى : لمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم : إنكم لا تقفون على المخلوقات فكيف تقفون على الاسامي والصفات

ITQAN:v1p194/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p194/r1.speaker: ابن حجر
ITQAN:v1p194/r1.claim: Ibn Hajar calls most explanations of the report about four Khazraj memorizers strained and proposes it refers only to a comparison with the Aws, not to emigrants.
ITQAN:v1p194/r1.anchor: قال ابن حجر وفي غالب هذه الاحتمالات تكلف ولا سيما الأخير قال وقد ظهر لي احتمال آخر وهو أن المراد إثبات ذلك للخزرج دون الأوس فقط

ITQAN:v1p194/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p194/r2.speaker: أنس
ITQAN:v1p194/r2.claim: Anas reports a contest between Aws and Khazraj: Aws listed four distinguished companions, while Khazraj claimed four had collected the Qur’an.
ITQAN:v1p194/r2.anchor: كما أخرجه ابن جرير من طريق سعيد بن أبي عروبة عن قتادة عن أنس قال افتخر الحيان الأوس والخزرج فقال الأوس منا أربعة

ITQAN:v1p194/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p194/r3.speaker: ابن حجر
ITQAN:v1p194/r3.claim: Ibn Hajar says reports show Abu Bakr memorized the Qur’an during the Prophet’s life; a report of his recitation refers to what had been revealed by then.
ITQAN:v1p194/r3.anchor: والذي يظهر من كثير من الأحاديث أن أبا بكر كان يحفظ القرآن في حياة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ففي الصحيح أنه بنى مسجدا بفناء داره

ITQAN:v1p194/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p194/r4.speaker: ابن حجر
ITQAN:v1p194/r4.claim: Abu Bakr’s memorization is supported by his zeal, free time, closeness to the Prophet, and the Prophet’s frequent visits to his household.
ITQAN:v1p194/r4.anchor: وهذا مما لا يرتاب فيه مع شدة حرص أبي بكر على تلقي القرآن من النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وفراغ باله له وهما بمكة

ITQAN:v1p194/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p194/r5.speaker: ابن حجر
ITQAN:v1p194/r5.claim: The Prophet’s instruction to appoint the best reciter as imam and his choosing Abu Bakr during illness indicate Abu Bakr was the most proficient reciter; Ibn Kathir said this earlier.
ITQAN:v1p194/r5.anchor: وقد صح حديث يؤم القوم أقرؤهم لكتاب الله وقد قدمه صلى الله عليه وسلم في مرضه إماما للمهاجرين والأنصار فدل على أنه كان أقرأهم

ITQAN:v1p194/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p194/r6.speaker: محمد بن سيرين
ITQAN:v1p194/r6.claim: A sound report says Abu Bakr died without collecting the Qur’an and ʿUmar was killed without collecting it; interpreters differ whether this means memorizing it all or compiling manuscripts.
ITQAN:v1p194/r6.anchor: أخرج ابن اشته في المصاحف بسند صحيح عن محمد بن سيرين قال مات أبو بكر ولم يجمع القرآن وقتل عمر ولم يجمع القرآن

ITQAN:v1p194/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p194/r7.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
ITQAN:v1p194/r7.claim: A report says ʿAli collected the Qur’an in revelation order after the Prophet’s death.
ITQAN:v1p194/r7.anchor: قال ابن حجر وقد ورد عن علي أنه جمع القرآن على ترتيب النزول عقب موت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أخرجه ابن أبي داود

ITQAN:v1p194/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p194/r8.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
ITQAN:v1p194/r8.claim: A sound report says Ibn ʿUmar had collected the Qur’an and read it nightly; the Prophet instructed him to complete it in a month.
ITQAN:v1p194/r8.anchor: وأخرج النسائي بسند صحيح عن عبد الله بن عمر قال جمعت القرآن فقرأت به كل ليلة فبلغ النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال أقرأه في شهر

ITQAN:v2p461/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p461/r1.speaker: الزجاج
ITQAN:v2p461/r1.claim: Al-Zajjaj considers iyyā an overt noun, while most grammarians consider it a pronoun.
ITQAN:v2p461/r1.anchor: زعم الزجاج أنها اسم ظاهر والجمهور ضمير ثم اختلفوا فيه على أقوال

ITQAN:v2p461/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p461/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p461/r2.claim: One analysis treats iyyā plus its attachment as a pronoun; another treats only iyyā as the pronoun and the following noun as specifying person, absence, or address.
ITQAN:v2p461/r2.anchor: أحدها أنه كلمة ضمير هو وما اتصل به والثاني أنه وحده ضمير وما بعده اسم مضاف له يفسر ما يراد به

ITQAN:v2p461/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p461/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p461/r3.claim: Other analyses treat only iyyā as pronoun with following explanatory particles, or treat iyyā as support and the next element as pronoun.
ITQAN:v2p461/r3.anchor: والثالث أنه وحده ضمير وما بعده حروف تفسر المراد والرابع أنه عماد وما بعده هو الضمير

ITQAN:v2p461/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p461/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p461/r4.claim: The derivation of iyyā is rejected; several dialectal readings vary the yāʾ and replace the hamza with a hāʾ.
ITQAN:v2p461/r4.anchor: وقد غلط من زعم أنه مشتق وفيه سبع لغات قرئ بها بتشديد الياء وتخفيفها مع الهمزة وإبدالها هاء مكسورة ومفتوحة

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p146/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p146/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p146/r1.claim: In the Khansa example, the definite predicate places mourning a slain person among an unmistakably recognized kind of goodness; it neither denies goodness to other mourning nor restricts goodness to that case.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p146/r1.anchor: الحسن الظاهر الذي لا ينكره أح د

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p146/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p146/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p146/r2.claim: Hassan ibn Thabit uses والدك العبد to affirm enslavement as an evident, established condition; saying والدك عبد would not give it the same recognized force.

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p146/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p146/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p146/r3.claim: The line about being lions in war and rain-bringing clouds in other times is another example of stating a recognized quality through a definite predicate.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p146/r3.anchor: أسود إذا ما أبدت الحرب نابها وفي سائر الدهر الغيوث المواطر

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p146/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p146/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p146/r4.claim: A definite predicate such as البطل المحامي introduces an ideal quality for the listener to picture, then identifies the subject as that very ideal rather than merely asserting or restricting the attribute.

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p273/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p273/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p273/r1.claim: Attributing speech to its author concerns the author's particular arrangement of syntactic meanings within words, not the words or language forms by themselves.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p273/r1.anchor: من حيث توخي فيها النظم الذي بينا أنه عبارة عن توخي معاني النحو في معاني الكلم

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p273/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p273/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p273/r2.claim: The relation resembles a weaver's brocade or a jeweler's ornament: authorship attaches to the craft and ordering, not to the raw silk, silver, or gold.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p273/r2.anchor: حال الإبريسم مع الذي ينسج منه الديباج وحال الفضة والذهب مع من يصوغ منهما الحلي

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p273/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p273/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p273/r3.claim: If uttering the words in the poet's arrangement made someone their author, the narrator who repeats the same words from memory would also count as the poet, which is untenable.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p273/r3.anchor: فإنه ينطق بها ويخرجها من فيه على الهيئة والصورة التي نطق بها الشاعر

DAMGHANI:v1p274/r6.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p274/r6.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p274/r6.claim: The companions of Hell are its keepers, the angels assigned to guard it.
DAMGHANI:v1p274/r6.anchor: وما جعلنا اصحاب النار الا ملائكة يعني خزنة النار ولا نظير له

DAMGHANI:v1p316/r2.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p316/r2.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p316/r2.claim: ʿAdad here means the small number of Hell’s keepers, made a trial for the unbelievers.
DAMGHANI:v1p316/r2.anchor: فوجه منها العدة القلة قوله سبحانه في سورة المدثر وما جعلنا عدتهم الا فتنة للذين كفروا يعني قلة خزان جهنم

DAMGHANI:v1p316/r12.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p316/r12.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p316/r12.claim: The following entry begins by listing transgression as a sense of ʿadā, but the excerpt ends before elaboration.
DAMGHANI:v1p316/r12.anchor: ع د ا على وجهين التعدي عما

DAMGHANI:v1p106/r1.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p106/r1.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p106/r1.claim: Jaʿala can mean to describe or characterize, as when people ascribe partners or daughters to God.
DAMGHANI:v1p106/r1.anchor: فوجه منها جعلوا يعني وصفوا قوله تعالى في سورة الأنعام وجعلوا لله شركاء الجن

DAMGHANI:v1p106/r22.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p106/r22.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p106/r22.claim: Junūd here means God’s angels, identified as the keepers of Hell.
DAMGHANI:v1p106/r22.anchor: فوجه منها الجنود بمعنى الملائكة قوله تعالى في سورة المدثر

DAMGHANI:v1p106/r24.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p106/r24.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p106/r24.claim: The entry’s heading also lists progeny of Iblis, crowds, and supporters as further senses of jund, without elaboration in this excerpt.
DAMGHANI:v1p106/r24.anchor: ج ن د على خمسة اوجه الملائكة الرسل والمؤمنون ذرية إبليس الجموع الأنصار أو النصراء

DAMGHANI:v1p413/r12.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p413/r12.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p413/r12.claim: The next entry lists eight senses of laʿn: transformation, tribute, anger, grave punishment, legal penalty, supplication or expulsion, fire, and drowning; it gives no examples here.
DAMGHANI:v1p413/r12.anchor: ل ع ن على ثمانية أوجه المسخ ضرب الجزية السخط

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p392/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p392/r10.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p392/r10.claim: Ashab means the keepers of Hell in 74:31.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p392/r10.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن الصاحب في القرآن على تسعة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p233/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p233/r2.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p233/r2.claim: One Qur'anic sense is angels generally; another reported view restricts the phrase to the keepers of Hell.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p233/r2.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن الجنود في القرآن على خمسة أوجه

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p497/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p497/r1.speaker: رجل من المشركين
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p497/r1.claim: A polytheist reportedly challenged the count, saying he could handle seventeen keepers if others handled two; God answered that the keepers are angels, whom no one could overcome.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p497/r1.anchor: روي: أن رجلا (1) من المشركين - قال: أنا أكفيكم سبعة عشر، واكفوني اثنين: فأنزل الله: {وما جعلنا أصحاب النار إلا ملائكة} فمن يطيقهم؟.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p497/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p497/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p497/r2.claim: The small number is a trial because the deniers ask what nineteen could amount to and whether they could manage all creation.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p497/r2.anchor: {وما جعلنا عدتهم} في هذه القلة {إلا فتنة} ؛ لأنهم قالوا

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p497/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p497/r3.speaker: قتادة
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p497/r3.claim: Qatāda says the People of the Book become certain because the number of Hell’s keepers agrees with the number in their scripture.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p497/r3.anchor: {ليستيقن الذين أوتوا الكتاب} حين وافقت عدة خزنة أهل النار ما في كتابهم. هذا قول قتادة (2) .

SAMIN-DURR:74:31/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:74:31/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:74:31/r1.claim: فتنة is a second object with an omitted genitive سبب; للذين modifies فتنة and is not causal.
SAMIN-DURR:74:31/r1.anchor: قوله: { إلا فتنة }: مفعول ثان على حذف مضاف، أي: إلا سبب فتنة

SAMIN-DURR:74:31/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:74:31/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:74:31/r2.claim: ليستيقن attaches to جعلنا, not فتنة; alternatively it depends on an omitted فعلنا ذلك. The author says al-Zamakhsharī's parsing serves his Muʿtazilite purpose.
SAMIN-DURR:74:31/r2.anchor: قوله: { ليستيقن الذين } متعلق ب " جعلنا " لا ب " فتنة ". وقيل: بفعل مضمر

SAMIN-DURR:74:31/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:74:31/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:74:31/r3.claim: كذلك modifies or circumstantially qualifies an omitted verbal noun; ذلك points to preceding misguidance and guidance, meaning God guides and misguides in that manner.
SAMIN-DURR:74:31/r3.anchor: قوله: { كذلك } نعت لمصدر أو حال منه على ما عرف غير مرة. و " ذلك " إشارة

SAMIN-DURR:74:31/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:74:31/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:74:31/r4.claim: مثلا may be specification or circumstantial; calling it an example is metaphorical because it is strange.
SAMIN-DURR:74:31/r4.anchor: و " مثلا " تمييزا أو حال. وتسمية هذا مثلا على سبيل الاستعارة لغرابته

SAMIN-DURR:74:31/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:74:31/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:74:31/r5.claim: جنود ربك must be fronted as object to restrict its subject, with a pronoun referring back to material attached to it.
SAMIN-DURR:74:31/r5.anchor: قوله: { جنود ربك } مفعول واجب التقديم لحصر فاعله، ولعود الضمير على ما اتصل بالمفعول

SAMIN-DURR:74:31/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:74:31/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:74:31/r6.claim: هي may refer to Saqar, the signs mentioned about it, Fire, worldly fire, the angel count, or the angelic hosts.
SAMIN-DURR:74:31/r6.anchor: قوله: { وما هي } يجوز أن يعود الضمير على " سقر " ، أي: وما سقر إلا تذكرة

SAMIN-DURR:74:31/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:74:31/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:74:31/r7.claim: للبشر is governed by ذكرى, and its lām is extra.
SAMIN-DURR:74:31/r7.anchor: و " للبشر " مفعول ب " ذكرى " واللام فيه مزيدة

ZAJJAJ:v5p248/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p248/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p248/r2.claim: The number of the guardians is a test for the unbelievers, some of whom say that some of them would suffice to deal with those guardians.
ZAJJAJ:v5p248/r2.anchor: (وما جعلنا عدتهم إلا فتنة للذين كفروا). أي محنة، لأن بعضهم قال

ZAJJAJ:v5p248/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p248/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p248/r3.claim: The People of the Book become certain because what the Prophet brought agrees with what is in their scriptures.
ZAJJAJ:v5p248/r3.anchor: أي يعلمون أن ما أتى به النبي عليه السلام موافقا لما في كتبهم

ZAJJAJ:v5p248/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p248/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p248/r4.claim: Believers increase in faith whenever they affirm what comes in God's Book.
ZAJJAJ:v5p248/r4.anchor: لأنهم كلما صدقوا بما يأتي في كتاب الله عز وجل زاد إيمانهم

ZAJJAJ:v5p248/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p248/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p248/r5.claim: The phrase means that the People of the Book and believers will not doubt.

ASAD-NOTES:74:31/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:74:31/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:74:31/r1.claim: Asad renders the keepers over hell as angelic powers.
ASAD-NOTES:74:31/r1.anchor: For We have caused none but angelic powers to lord over the fire

ASAD-NOTES:74:31/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:74:31/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:74:31/r2.claim: Their number is a trial for deniers, while it convinces earlier revelation recipients, strengthens believers, and frees both groups from doubt.
ASAD-NOTES:74:31/r2.anchor: their number to be aught but a trial for those who are bent on denying the truth

ASAD-NOTES:74:31/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:74:31/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:74:31/r3.claim: Those with diseased hearts and outright deniers ask what God intends by the parable.
ASAD-NOTES:74:31/r3.anchor: they in whose hearts is disease

ASAD-NOTES:74:31/r4.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:74:31/r4.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:74:31/r4.claim: God lets astray those who will to go astray and guides those who will to be guided.
ASAD-NOTES:74:31/r4.anchor: In this way God lets go astray him that wills

ASAD-NOTES:74:31/r5.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:74:31/r5.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:74:31/r5.claim: Only God comprehends the forces of the Sustainer.
ASAD-NOTES:74:31/r5.anchor: thy Sustaine rs forces save Him alone

ASAD-NOTES:74:31/r6.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:74:31/r6.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:74:31/r6.claim: The passage is a reminder to mortal humanity.

ASAD-NOTES:74:31#n16/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:74:31#n16/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:74:31#n16/r1.claim: Human conscious perception and conceptual thinking are called angelic powers because they enable discrimination between good and evil and spiritual ascent.
ASAD-NOTES:74:31#n16/r1.anchor: by virtue of his powers of conscious perception and conceptual thinking that man can arrive at a discriminating cognition of good and evil

ASAD-NOTES:74:31#n16/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:74:31#n16/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:74:31#n16/r2.claim: Because neglect or deliberate misuse of those powers causes sin and afterlife suffering, they are called lords of the fire; this complements “over it” in the preceding verse.
ASAD-NOTES:74:31#n16/r2.anchor: a neglect or a deliberately wrong use of these angelic powers is at the root of all sinning on the part of man

ASAD-NOTES:74:31#n17/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:74:31#n17/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:74:31#n17/r1.claim: Asad takes the number as part of an allegory: deniers wrongly insist on literalizing it and so miss the passage's point.
ASAD-NOTES:74:31#n17/r1.anchor: take the allegory in a literal sense, thus missing its point entirely

ASAD-NOTES:74:31#n17/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:74:31#n17/r2.speaker: Those who deny the truth
ASAD-NOTES:74:31#n17/r2.claim: Deniers speculate about why Muhammad, whom they regard as the Qur'an's author, singled out one number.
ASAD-NOTES:74:31#n17/r2.anchor: "those who are bent on denying the truth" are unwilling to recognize as such

ASAD-NOTES:74:31#n18/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:74:31#n18/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:74:31#n18/r1.claim: Understanding the allegory lets earlier revelation recipients recognize the Qur'an's rational approach to faith; this is the earliest statement of continuity in humanity's religious experience.
ASAD-NOTES:74:31#n18/r1.anchor: the earliest statement outlining the principle of continuity in mankind's religious experience

ASAD-NOTES:74:31#n19/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:74:31#n19/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:74:31#n19/r1.claim: Those with diseased hearts are half-hearted people able to discern right from wrong but inclined toward unbelief.
ASAD-NOTES:74:31#n19/r1.anchor: the half-hearted ones who, despite their ability to discern between right and wrong, incline towards unbelief

ASAD-NOTES:74:31#n20/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:74:31#n20/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:74:31#n20/r1.claim: Asad notes the phrase also occurs at 2:26 and supplies “your” because unbelievers, rather than the Prophet, ask the question.
ASAD-NOTES:74:31#n20/r1.anchor: the identical phrase in 2:26, together with the corresponding note 18

ASAD-NOTES:74:31#n21/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:74:31#n21/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:74:31#n21/r1.claim: Asad also allows “whomever He wills” as a rendering; the allegorical parable warns Qur'an followers against literal readings of eschatological descriptions.
ASAD-NOTES:74:31#n21/r1.anchor: prevent the followers of the Qur'an from attaching a literal meaning to its eschatological descriptions

ASAD-NOTES:74:31#n21/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:74:31#n21/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:74:31#n21/r2.claim: The closing reminder sentence makes explicit the parable's purpose, as at 2:26.
ASAD-NOTES:74:31#n21/r2.anchor: a purpose that is unmistakably expressed in the concluding sentence of this passage

ASAD-NOTES:74:31#n22/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:74:31#n22/r1.speaker: Tabari, Zamakhshari, Baghawi, Ibn Kathir
ASAD-NOTES:74:31#n22/r1.claim: These commentators take hiya as singular, referring to the feminine noun saqar, hell-fire.
ASAD-NOTES:74:31#n22/r1.anchor: the feminine noun saqar, "hell-fire" (Tabari, Zamakhshari, Baghawi, Ibn Kathir)

ASAD-NOTES:74:31#n22/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:74:31#n22/r2.speaker: Razi
ASAD-NOTES:74:31#n22/r2.claim: Razi takes hiya as plural, referring to the Qur'anic verses about these allegories.
ASAD-NOTES:74:31#n22/r2.anchor: Razi pinpoints as "those [Qur'anic] verses dealing with these allegories

ASAD-NOTES:74:31#n22/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:74:31#n22/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:74:31#n22/r3.claim: Asad compromises between the readings with the rendering “all this.”

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p579/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p579/r1.speaker: الراغب
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p579/r1.claim: Al-Raghib extends heart disease to moral vices such as ignorance, cowardice, miserliness, and hypocrisy.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p579/r1.anchor: عم الراغب مرض القلب فى الرذائل الخلقية كالجهل والجبن والبخل والنفاق

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p579/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p579/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p579/r2.claim: She rejects treating every instance of ignorance, cowardice, or miserliness as heart disease warranting punishment; Quranic heart disease concerns inward acts such as hypocrisy, doubt, rancor, satanic temptation, and lust.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p579/r2.anchor: إنما يتعلق مرض فى القلب بما هو من أفعال القلوب: يكون نفاقا كما فى آية البقرة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p782/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p782/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p782/r1.claim: Al-Baqara mentions mercy and Jewish sins less than al-Maida, so mercy appears more often in al-Baqara: 19 occurrences against five.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p782/r1.anchor: سورة البقرة جاءت أقل غضباً وذكراً لمعاصي اليهود لذا جاءت الرحمة فقد وردت الرحمة ومشتقاتها في سورة البقرة 19 مرة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p782/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p782/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p782/r2.claim: The reward is proportionate to deeds; the passage means People of the Book who truly believed before distortion must also believe in the Hereafter.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p782/r2.anchor: الأجر يكون على قدر العمل فالنسبة للذين آمنوا من أهل الكتاب قبل تحريفه وهم مؤمنون بالله تعالى عليهم أن يؤمنوا إيماناً آخر باليوم الآخر

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p782/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p782/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p782/r3.claim: He counts 10 kinds of good deeds in al-Maida versus 30 or 33 in al-Baqara; al-Baqara includes the former except ablution and many additional acts, warranting greater reward.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p782/r3.anchor: في سورة المائدة ورد ذكر 10 أنواع من العمل الصالح (الوفاء بالعقود، الوضوء، الزكاة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p782/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p782/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p782/r4.claim: He compares phrase-word frequencies: al-Baqara/al-Maida counts are fa 260/180, لهم 29/15, أجرهم 5/1, عند 19/1, and ربهم 10/2.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p782/r4.anchor: (الفاء) وردت في البقرة 260 مرة ووردت في المائدة 180 مرة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p782/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p782/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p782/r5.claim: The full phrase about their reward, absence of fear, and absence of grief appears in this form only in al-Baqara, where it recurs five times.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p782/r5.anchor: هذه العبارة (فلهم أجرهم عند ربهم ولا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون) لم ترد إلا في سورة البقرة بهذا الشكل وقد وردت في البقرة 5 مرات

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p782/r6.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p782/r6.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p782/r6.claim: Quranic word repetition follows context; parallel verses should be compared by attending to their differing words.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p782/r6.anchor: وتردد الكلمات في القرآن تأتي حسب سياق الآيات وفي الآيات المتشابهة يجب أن نرى الكلمات المختلفة فيها

NASHR:v2p108/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p108/r1.speaker: آخرون
NASHR:v2p108/r1.claim: Other authorities argue that rāʾ has no inherent heaviness or lightness: its vowel and articulation determine the quality, and a kasra favors tip articulation and lightness.
NASHR:v2p108/r1.anchor: وقال آخرون: ليس للراء أصل في التفخيم، ولا في الترقيق، وإنما يعرض لها ذلك بحسب حركتها

NASHR:v2p108/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p108/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p108/r2.claim: The author finds no proof that rāʾ is intrinsically heavy: a quiescent rāʾ is light after permanent kasra unless followed by an emphatic letter, and heavy otherwise; apparent cases after incidental kasra may reflect the verb's relation to its imperfect form.
NASHR:v2p108/r2.anchor: فظهر أن تفخيم الراء وترقيقها مرتبط بأسباب كالمتحركة، ولم يثبت في ذلك دلالة على حكمها في نفسها

IBNHISHAM:v1p313#3/r1.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p313#3/r1.speaker: أبو جهل
IBNHISHAM:v1p313#3/r1.claim: Abu Jahl mocks the claim that Hell has nineteen keepers, asking whether each hundred Quraysh could overcome one; the passage says the verse was revealed in response.
IBNHISHAM:v1p313#3/r1.anchor: فقال أبو جهل يوما وهو يهزأ برسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وما جاء به من الحق

IBNHISHAM:v1p313#3/r2.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p313#3/r2.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNHISHAM:v1p313#3/r2.claim: After the mockery, Quraysh avoid listening when the Prophet recites aloud; individual listeners secretly lean in but stop if they fear being noticed or harmed.
IBNHISHAM:v1p313#3/r2.anchor: جعلوا إذا جهر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بالقرآن وهو يصلي، يتفرقون عنه، ويأبون أن يستمعوا له

IBNHISHAM:v1p403/r1.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p403/r1.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
IBNHISHAM:v1p403/r1.claim: Abu Sa'id al-Khudri reports the Prophet's night journey: at the heaven's Gate of the Keepers, angel Isma'il stood over twelve thousand angels, each over twelve thousand more; the Prophet cited the verse that only God knows His hosts.
IBNHISHAM:v1p403/r1.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري رضي الله عنه أنه قال: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: لما فرغت مما كان في بيت المقدس

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p329#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p329#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p329#2/r1.claim: Qatāda says the People of the Book become certain because the number of the Fire's keepers agrees with the number in their scripture.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p329#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ ليستيقن الذين أوتوا الكتاب ﴾ قال ليستيقن أهل الكتاب حين وافق عدة خزنة أهل النار ما في كتابهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p332/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p332/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p332/r8.claim: The keepers are angels made as creatures no human can withstand.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p332/r8.anchor: وما جعلنا أصحاب النار إلا ملائكة: أي جعلناهم خلقا لا قبل لأحد من الناس بهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p332/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p332/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p332/r9.claim: فتنة is the second object of جعلنا, meaning a cause of trial, not a purpose-object; unbelievers mock their ability to overpower keepers despite denying resurrection and Hell.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p332/r9.anchor: وما جعلنا عدتهم إلا فتنة للذين كفروا: أي سبب فتنة، وفتنة مفعول ثان لجعلنا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p332/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p332/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p332/r10.claim: ليستيقن is a purpose-object attached to جعلنا, not فتنة: the number serves to establish certainty among the People of the Book.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p332/r10.anchor: ليستيقن: هذا مفعول من أجله، وهو متعلق بجعلنا لا بفتنة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p332/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p332/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p332/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas and Mujahid say Jews and Christians recognize the Quran as from God because its count matches their revealed books, which the unlettered Messenger had not read.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p332/r11.anchor: وهم اليهود والنصارى. أن هذا القرآن هو من عند الله، إذ هم يجدون هذه العدة في كتبهم المنزلة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p332/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p332/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p332/r12.claim: When truths come from God, every believer's faith increases and doubt disappears from sincere People of the Book and believers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p332/r12.anchor: وبورود الحقائق من عند الله تعالى يزداد كل ذي إيمان إيمانا، ويزول الريب عن المصدقين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p332/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p332/r13.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p332/r13.claim: Another explanation is that the number tests unbelievers because they mockingly ask why the keepers are not twenty and what warrants this count.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p332/r13.anchor: وقيل: إنما صار جعلها فتنة لأنهم يستهزئون ويقولون: لم لم يكونوا عشرين؟ وما المقتضى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p333/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p333/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p333/r1.claim: The mockers ask how such a small number could torture most of all jinn and humankind from creation until the Resurrection.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p333/r1.anchor: ويقولون هذا العدد القليل، يقوون بتعذيب أكثر العالم من الجن والإنس من أول ما خلق الله تعالى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p333/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p333/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p333/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the count itself is the trial: nineteen, one short of twenty, unsettles those who reject God's wisdom while spurring believers' certainty. Abu Hayyan rejects this as a distortion that substitutes words and meaning absent from the verse.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p333/r2.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: فإن قلت: قد جعل افتتان الكافرين بعدة الزبانية سببا لاستيقان أهل الكتاب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p333/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p333/r3.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p333/r3.claim: An alternative syntax attaches ليستيقن to an unexpressed verb: We did this so they would become certain.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p333/r3.anchor: وقيل: ليستيقن متعلق بفعل مضمر، أي فعلنا ذلك ليستيقن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p333/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p333/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p333/r4.claim: Negating doubt reinforces the affirmation of certainty and describes a soul completely at rest.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p333/r4.anchor: ولا يرتاب: توكيد لقوله ليستيقن، إذ إثبات اليقين ونفي الارتياب أبلغ وآكد في الوصف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p333/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p333/r5.speaker: الحسين بن الفضل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p333/r5.claim: Husayn ibn al-Fadl notes that the sura is Meccan and there was no hypocrisy in Mecca; disease here means instability and weakness of faith.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p333/r5.anchor: قال الحسين بن الفضل: السورة مكية، ولم يكن بمكة نفاق، وإنما المرض في الآية: الاضطراب وضعف الإيمان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p333/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p333/r6.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p333/r6.claim: Another view treats this as a prediction of hypocrites who would arise in Medina after the Hijra and ask what God intended by the strange number; calling it a parable expresses rejection of its divine origin.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p333/r6.anchor: وقيل: هو إخبار بالغيب، أي وليقول المنافقون الذين ينجمون في مستقبل الزمان بالمدينة بعد الهجرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p333/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p333/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p333/r7.claim: They call the number a parable metaphorically because it is strange; their question intends to deny that it is from God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p333/r7.anchor: وسموه مثلا استعارة من المثل المضروب استغرابا منهم لهذا العدد، والمعنى: أي شيء أراد الله بهذا العدد العجيب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p333/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p333/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p333/r8.claim: The author points to his earlier grammatical analysis of a similar phrase at the beginning of al-Baqara.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p333/r8.anchor: وتقدم إعراب مثل هذه الجملة في أوائل البقرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p334/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p334/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p334/r1.claim: The kaf is accusative and points to the preceding account of misguidance and guidance: God increases disbelievers' doubt and believers' faith.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p334/r1.anchor: الكاف في محل نصب، وذلك إشارة إلى ما قبله من معنى الإضلال والهدى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p334/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p334/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p334/r2.claim: God's forces exceed what people imagine; punishment is only a portion of His power, and the heavens teem with kinds of angels.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p334/r2.anchor: وما يعلم جنود ربك إلا هو: إعلام بأن الأمر فوق ما يتوهم، وأن الجزاء إنما هو عن بعض القدرة لا عن كلها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p334/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p334/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p334/r3.claim: A Prophetic report says the sky groans, as it should: no space the size of a foot is empty of an angel prostrating before God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p334/r3.anchor: وفي الحديث: «أطت السماء وحق لها أن تئط ما فيها موضع قدم إلا وملك واضع جبهته لله ساجدا»

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p334/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p334/r4.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p334/r4.claim: Mujahid says هي refers to the fire.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p334/r4.anchor: وما هي: أي النار، قاله مجاهد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p334/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p334/r5.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p334/r5.claim: Other proposed referents for هي are the address and warning.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p334/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p334/r6.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p334/r6.claim: Other proposed referents are the fire of this world, the signs just mentioned, the number nineteen, and God's forces.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p334/r6.anchor: أو نار الدنيا، أو الآيات التي ذكرت، أو العدة التسعة عشر، أو الجنود

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p334/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p334/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p334/r7.claim: The author prefers Hell, specifically Saqar, as the referent: its mention is a reminder that should make people fear and obey.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p334/r7.anchor: أقوال راجحها الأول وهي سقر، ذكر بها البشر ليخافوا ويطيعوا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p334/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p334/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p334/r8.claim: The reminder benefits people capable of reflection and taking heed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p334/r8.anchor: إلا ذكرى للبشر: أي الذين أهلوا للتذكر والاعتبار

ALUSI-FULL:v29p126/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p126/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p126/r1.claim: The guardians of the Fire are angels rather than humans, who could not endure them; the verse is also linked to a warning revealed about Abū Jahl.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p126/r1.anchor: وما جعلنا أصحاب النار إلا ملائكة أي ما جعلناهم رجالا من جنسكم يطاقون وأنزل سبحانه في أبي جهل أولي لك فأولى

ALUSI-FULL:v29p126/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p126/r2.speaker: الجمهور
ALUSI-FULL:v29p126/r2.claim: The majority identify the guardians as the nineteen chiefs who administer the Fire and direct its gatekeepers; the explicit noun replaces a pronoun to emphasize their role.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p126/r2.anchor: والظاهر أن المراد بأصحاب النار هم التسعة عشر ففيه وضع الظاهر موضع الضمير وكأن ذلك لما في هذا الظاهر من الإشارة إلى أنهم المدبرون لأمرها

ALUSI-FULL:v29p126/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p126/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p126/r3.claim: A hadith says Hell will be brought with seventy thousand reins, each drawn by seventy thousand angels, indicating that the nineteen are not every angel involved.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p126/r3.anchor: يؤتى بجهنم يومئذ لها سبعون ألف زمام مع كل زمام سبعون ألف ملك

ALUSI-FULL:v29p126/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p126/r4.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v29p126/r4.claim: Some supply an omitted classifier, making the nineteen groups or ranks; al-Ālūsī considers this unlikely given the transmitted report and the verse’s point about mockery of their number.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p126/r4.anchor: وذهب بعضهم إلى التمييز المحذوف صف وقيل صف والأصل عليها تسعة عشر صنفا أو عليها تسعة عشر صفا ويبعده ما تقدم

ALUSI-FULL:v29p126/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p126/r5.speaker: غير واحد
ALUSI-FULL:v29p126/r5.claim: Several commentators explain that angels do not pity the condemned and are the strongest creatures, wholly devoted to God and fierce in defending His right.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p126/r5.anchor: وقال غير واحد في تعليل جعلهم ملائكة ليخافوا جنس المعذبين فلا يرقوا لهم ولا يستروحوا إليهم ولأنهم أقوى الخلق

ALUSI-FULL:v29p126/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p126/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p126/r6.claim: A hadith describes their eyes like lightning, their mouths like hooks, and their strength as that of humans and jinn; one can carry a whole nation and a mountain before casting them into the Fire.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p126/r6.anchor: وفي الحديث كأن أعينهم البرق وكأن أقوالهم الصياصي يجرون أشعارهم لهم مثل قوة الثقلين يقبل أحدهم بالأمة من الناس

ALUSI-FULL:v29p126/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p126/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p126/r7.claim: The indefinite form may signal the immense magnitude of these angels.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p126/r7.anchor: ولا يبعد أن يكون في التنوين إشعار إلى عظم أمرهم

ALUSI-FULL:v29p126/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p126/r8.speaker: بعض الأجلة
ALUSI-FULL:v29p126/r8.claim: One interpretation says God set the number at nineteen precisely because disbelievers would be tested by seeing so few guardians and ridiculing the number.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p126/r8.anchor: ومعنى قوله تعالى وما جعلنا عدتهم إلا آخره على ما اختاره بعض الأجلة وما جعلنا عدد أصحاب النار إلا العدد الذي اقتضى فتنة الذين كفروا بالاستقلال والاستهزاء

ALUSI-FULL:v29p126/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p126/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p126/r9.claim: On this analysis, “a trial for disbelievers” names the effect in place of the particular cause—the number nineteen; making a number means declaring the count, not creating the guardians.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p126/r9.anchor: فكاءن الأصل وما جعلنا عدتهم إلا تسعة عشر فعبر بالأثر وهو فتنة الذين كفروا عن المؤخر وهو خصوص التسعة

ALUSI-FULL:v29p126#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p126#2/r1.speaker: author
