ALUSI-FULL:v29p126#2/r1.claim: The intended cause is the number itself, not the unbelievers’ reaction: its agreement with the number in earlier scriptures lets scripture-holders become certain of the Prophet and Qurʾān.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p126#2/r1.anchor: ليستيقن الذين أوتوا الكتاب أي ليكتسبوا اليقين بنبوته صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم وصدق القرآن لأجل موافقة المذكورين ذكرهم في القرآن بهذا العدد

ALUSI-FULL:v29p126#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p126#2/r2.speaker: البحر
ALUSI-FULL:v29p126#2/r2.claim: Al-Baḥr treats “so that they may become certain” as a purpose clause attached to “We made,” not to “a trial”; the trial is not caused by their certainty.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p126#2/r2.anchor: وفي البحر ليستيقن مفعول من أجله وهو متعلق بجملنا لا بفتنة فليست الفتنة معلولة للاستيقان

ALUSI-FULL:v29p126#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p126#2/r3.speaker: الانتصاف
ALUSI-FULL:v29p126#2/r3.claim: Al-Intiṣāf allows the purpose clause to reach back across the exception: the number was made a trial for disbelievers and a source of certainty for believers.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p126#2/r3.anchor: وفي الانتصاف يجوز أن يرجع قوله تعالى ليستسقن إلى ما قبل الإستثناء أي جعلنا عدتهم سببا لفتنة الكفار ويقين المؤمنين

ALUSI-FULL:v29p126#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p126#2/r4.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v29p126#2/r4.claim: Al-Rāzī gives two explanations: one has God set the count to test disbelievers and bring certainty to scripture-holders; the other is the earlier effect-for-cause account.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p126#2/r4.anchor: وذكر الإمام في ذلك وجهين الثاني ما قدمناهم ما اختاره بعض الأجلة والأول أن التقدير وما جعلنا عدتهم إلا فتنة للكافرين

ALUSI-FULL:v29p126#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p126#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p126#2/r5.claim: “Those given scripture” most likely includes both Jews and Christians, though some restrict it to Jews.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p126#2/r5.anchor: وقيل المراد بهم اليهود فقد أخرج ابن أبي حاتم وابن مردويه والبيهقي

ALUSI-FULL:v29p126#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p126#2/r6.speaker: البراء
ALUSI-FULL:v29p126#2/r6.claim: Al-Barāʾ reports that a group of Jews asked a Companion about Hell’s keepers; after he deferred to God and the Messenger, “nineteen” was revealed.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p126#2/r6.anchor: أخرج ابن أبي حاتم وابن مردويه والبيهقي في البعث عن البراء أن رهطا من اليهود سألوا رجلا من أصحاب النبي

ALUSI-FULL:v29p126#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p126#2/r7.speaker: جابر
ALUSI-FULL:v29p126#2/r7.claim: Jābir reports that Jews asked whether the Prophet knew the number; he gestured ten once and nine another time.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p126#2/r7.anchor: وأخرج الترمذي وابن مردويه عن جابر قال قال ناس من اليهود

ALUSI-FULL:v29p126#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p126#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p126#2/r8.claim: Those reports may suggest a Medinan revelation, but the inference is weak: a Companion may have been travelling, and Jews could also come to Mecca; neither report proves the verse means Jews alone.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p126#2/r8.anchor: واستشعر من هذا أن الآية مدنية لأن اليهود إنما كانوا فيها وهو استشعار ضعيف لأن السؤال لصحابي فلعله كان مسافر

ALUSI-FULL:v29p126#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p126#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p126#2/r9.claim: Believers may increase in the quality of faith by seeing scripture-holders confirm the number, or in its quantity by adding belief in this detail to what they already believe.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p126#2/r9.anchor: ويزداد الذين آمنوا إيمانا أي يزداد إيمانهم كيفية بما رأوا من تسليمهم أهل الكتاب وتصديقهم أنه كذلك أو كمية بانضمام إيمانهم بذلك إلى إيمانهم بسائر ما أنزل

ALUSI-FULL:v29p126#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p126#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p126#2/r10.claim: The statement that scripture-holders and believers do not doubt reinforces certainty and increased faith, excluding doubts from overlooked premises or apparent counterevidence.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p126#2/r10.anchor: ولا يرتاب الذين أوتوا الكتاب والمؤمنون تأكيد لما قبله من الاستيقان

ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r1.claim: The distinct negations mark different states: the People of the Book do not doubt despite their denial, while believers do not doubt in a way consonant with faith.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r1.anchor: للتنبيه على تباين النفيين حالا فإن انتفاء الإرتياب من أهل الكتاب مقارن لما ينافيه من الجحود ومن المؤمنين مقارن لما يقتضيهمن الإيمان

ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r2.claim: The wording repeats the negation to emphasize both groups, since a pronoun might otherwise be understood to refer only to believers.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r2.anchor: للتنصيص على تأكيد الأمرين لاحتمال عود الضمير في ذلك على المؤمنين فقط

ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r3.claim: Calling believers by an active participle after describing them with a relative clause signals that their faith remains firm as it increases.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r3.anchor: والتعبير عن المؤمنين باسم الفاعل بعد ذكرهم بالموصول والصلة الفعلية المنبئة عن الحدوث للإيذان بثباتهم على الإيمان بعد ازديادهم

ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r4.claim: The heart sickness means doubt or hypocrisy; if the whole sūra is Meccan, the reference predicts hypocrisy that would arise after the Hijra.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r4.anchor: أي شك أو نفاق فيكون بناء على أن السورة بتمامها مكية والنفاق إنما حدث بالمدينة إخبارا عما سيحدث من المغيبات بعد الهجرة

ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r5.claim: The disbelievers here are those persistent in denial.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r6.claim: On one parsing, ماذا is a single interrogative noun in the accusative as the object of أراد.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r6.anchor: وعلى الأول ماذا منزلة اسم واحد للإستفهام في موضع نصب بأراد

ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r7.claim: Alternatively, ما is an interrogative subject and ذا a relative predicate, with an omitted relative pronoun in the following clause.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r7.anchor: وعلى الثاني هي مؤلفة من كلمة ما اسم استفهام مبتدأ وذا اسم موصول خبره والجملة بعد صلة والعائد فيها محذوف

ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r8.claim: The question can mean what God intended by this startling number, which they found so strange it seemed like a proverbial example.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r8.anchor: ما الذي أراده الله تعالى بهذاالعدد المستغرب استغراب المثل

ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r9.claim: Their wording is reported speech used contemptuously: they deny that the number came from God rather than sincerely asking about its wisdom.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r9.anchor: والظاهر أن ألفاظ هذه الجملة من المحكي وعنوا بالإشارة التحقير وغرضهم نفى أن يكون ذلك من عند الله عز وجل على أبلغ وجه لا الإستفهام حقيقة

ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r10.claim: One possible reading takes the phrase as God recounting their words, such as their saying, “What did I intend?”
ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r10.anchor: وجوز أن يكون أراد الله تعالى من الحكاية وهم قالوا ماذا أريد ونحوه

ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r11.speaker: قائلون
ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r11.claim: Another view takes مثل as a parable: they treated the strange number as a proverbial comparison and mockingly attributed it to God.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r11.anchor: وقيل يجوز أن يكون المثل بمعناه الآخر وهو ما شبه مضربه بأن يكونوا قد عدوه لاستغرابه مثلا مضروبا ونسبوه إليه عز وجل استهزاء وتهكما

ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r12.claim: The separate explanation of this lām marks misguidance as an incidental result of the deniers’ bad conduct, unlike guidance intended for its own sake; both lām clauses may instead indicate consequence.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r12.anchor: إنما أعيد اللام فيه للفرق بين العلتين إذ مرجح الأولى الهداية المقصودة بالذات ومرجح هذه الضلال المقصود بالعرض الناشيء من سوء صنيع الضالين

ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r13.speaker: المحققون
ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r13.claim: The verifying scholars allow divine acts to be explained through wisdoms and purposes.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r13.anchor: وتعليل أفعاله بالحكم والمصالح جائز عند المحققين

ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r14.claim: Both lām clauses may also be construed as lām of consequence rather than purpose.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r14.anchor: وجوز في هذه اللام وكذا الأولى كونها للعاقبة

ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r15.claim: “Thus” points back to the preceding pattern of misguidance and guidance.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r15.anchor: ذلك إشارة إلى ما قبله من معنى الإضلال والهداية

ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r16.claim: The comparison originally qualifies an omitted verbal noun; moving it before the verb gives the construction an exclusive emphasis.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r16.anchor: ومحل الكاف في الأصل على أنها صفة لمصدر محذوف وأصل التقدير يضل الله من يشاء ويهدي من يشاء إضلالا وهداية كائنين مثل ما ذكر

ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r17.claim: God turns each person’s choice toward misguidance or guidance according to their bad or good preparedness when they witness the signs; the wording excludes lesser forms of either.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r17.anchor: لصرف اختياره حسب استعداده السيء إلى جانب الضلال عند مشاهدته لآيات الله تعالى الناطقة بالهدى ويهدي من يشاء هدايته لصرف اختياره حسب استعداده الحسن

ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r18.claim: Alternatively, “thus” may point forward, as in the wording “Thus We made you a middle community.”
ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r18.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون الإشارة إلى ما بعد كما في قوله تعالى وكذلك جعلناكم أمة وسطا

ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r19.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r19.claim: Jund is the plural of jund, commonly used for an army because of its dense, rough mass; it can refer to any group.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r19.anchor: جمع جند اشتهر في العسكر اعتبارا بالغلظة من الجند أي الأرض الغليظة التي فيها حجارة ويقال لكل جمع

ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r20.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r20.claim: Only God knows the hosts’ full nature and number, including the angels: no one can enumerate possibilities or grasp their detailed qualities; this rebuts mockery of the nineteen keepers.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p127/r20.anchor: إذ لا سبيل لأحد إلى حصر الممكنات والوقوف على حقائقها وصفاتها

ALUSI-FULL:v29p128/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p128/r1.speaker: مقاتل
ALUSI-FULL:v29p128/r1.claim: Muqatil says this answers Abu Jahl’s taunt asking whether Muhammad’s Lord had helpers besides nineteen: only nineteen are assigned to Hell, not all God’s countless hosts.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p128/r1.anchor: وقال مقاتل هو جواب لقول أبي جهل أما لرب محمد أعوان إلا تسعة عشر وحاصله أنه لما قلل الأعوان أجيب بأنهم لا يحصون كثرة

ALUSI-FULL:v29p128/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p128/r2.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v29p128/r2.claim: Al-Tibi reads the verse as saying only God knows the angels’ striking power, but al-Alusi says the wording does not clearly support that meaning.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p128/r2.anchor: لا أن المعنى ما يعلم بقوة بطش الملائكة إلا هو خلافا للطيبي فإن اللفظ غير ظاهر الدلالة على هذا المعنى

ALUSI-FULL:v29p128/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p128/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p128/r3.claim: Some reports describe the angels as the most numerous hosts, citing the heavens’ groaning because every space contains an angel standing, bowing, or prostrating.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p128/r3.anchor: فقيل الملائكة لخير أطت السماء وحق لها أن تئط ما فيها موضع قدم إلا وفيه ملك قائم أو راكع أو ساجد

ALUSI-FULL:v29p128/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p128/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p128/r4.claim: Other reports make each class of earthly, marine, and celestial creatures ten times the prior class, through the angels to the Throne, yet all remain few beside what God alone knows.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p128/r4.anchor: وفي بعض الأخبار أن مخلوقات البر عشر مخلوقات البحر والمجموع عشر مخلوقات الجو والمجموع عشر مخلوقات ملائكة السماء الدنيا

ALUSI-FULL:v29p128/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p128/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p128/r5.claim: A further opinion says even all angels are few beside the bewildered angels, who do not know God created anyone, and those too are few beside all creation.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p128/r5.anchor: وقيل المجموع أقل قليل بالنسبة إلى الملائكة المهيمين الذين لا يعلم أحدهم أن الله تعالى خلق أحدا سواء والمجموع أقل قليل بالنسبة إلى ما يعلمه سبحانه من مخلوقاته

ALUSI-FULL:v29p128/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p128/r6.speaker: الأوزاعي
ALUSI-FULL:v29p128/r6.claim: Al-Awza‘i relates Moses asking who inhabits heaven and how many there are; God answers that they are angels, twelve tribes, each as numerous as grains of earth.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p128/r6.anchor: وعن الأوزاعي قال قال موسى عليه السلام يا رب من مهك في السماء قال ملائكتي قال كم عدتهم قال اثنا عشر سبطا قال كم عدة السبط قال عدد التراب

ALUSI-FULL:v29p128/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p128/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p128/r7.claim: Al-Alusi does not affirm the reported ranking as sound or assert which host is greatest, though he considers angels most likely to be the largest group.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p128/r7.anchor: وفي صحة هذا روي إن صح فصدره من المتشابه وأنا لا أجزم بأكثرية صف فما يعلم جنود ربك إلا هو ولم يصح عندي في ذلك بيد أنه يغلب على الظن أن الأكثر الملائكة

ALUSI-FULL:v29p128/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p128/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p128/r8.claim: These verses and reports make it reasonable that unknown hosts exist in celestial bodies; God’s dominion exceeds thought’s capacity to encompass.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p128/r8.anchor: هذه الآية وأمثالها من الآيات والأخبار تشجع على القول باحتمال أن يكون في الأجرام العلوية جنود من جنود الله تعالى لا يعلم حقائقها وأحوالها إلا هو

ALUSI-FULL:v29p128/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p128/r9.speaker: قائلون
ALUSI-FULL:v29p128/r9.claim: One proposed explanation derives nineteen from twelve animal faculties and seven natural powers, but al-Alusi says this philosophical account hardly withstands scrutiny.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p128/r9.anchor: فقيل أن اختلاف النفوس البشرية في النظر والعمل بسبب القوى الحيوانية الأثنتي عشرة يعني الحواس الخمسة الباطنة والحواس الخمسة الظاهرة والقوة الباعثة

ALUSI-FULL:v29p128/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p128/r10.speaker: قائلون
ALUSI-FULL:v29p128/r10.claim: One scheme assigns six levels to disbeliever classes, each punished for failures of belief, confession, and action, producing eighteen overseers, plus one for sinful Muslims.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p128/r10.anchor: وقيل أن لجهنم سبع دركات ست منها لأصناف الكفار وكل صنف يعذب بترك الإعتقاد والأقرار والعمل أنواعا من العذاب تناسبها

ALUSI-FULL:v29p128/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p128/r11.speaker: قائلون
ALUSI-FULL:v29p128/r11.claim: A related proposal says if disbelievers occupy five levels, two are left for major and minor sinners among the Muslim community, or for male and female sinners.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p128/r11.anchor: ولم يجعل تعذيب الكفار في خمس منها فيبق للمؤمنين اثنتان أحدهما لأهل الكبائر

ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r1.speaker: قائلون
ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r1.claim: In the seven-level scheme, Hell was first prepared for disbelievers across its levels, then one level was set apart when God willed to punish this community there.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r1.anchor: لما تعلقت إرادته سبحانه بتعذيب الأمة بها أفرزت واحدة منها لهم

ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r2.speaker: قائلون
ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r2.claim: Another proposal subtracts five prayer hours from the day’s twenty-four, leaving nineteen; prayer’s blessing means no keepers were created for those hours.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r2.anchor: وقيل أن الساعات أربع وعشرون خمسة منها مصروفة للصلاة فلم يخلق في مقابلتها زبانية لبركة الصلاة الشاملة لمن لم يصل فيبقي تسعة عشر

ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r3.speaker: قائلون
ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r3.claim: A further seven-level scheme places six disbeliever classes under three overseers each, totaling eighteen, and one overseer over sinful believers.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r3.anchor: وقيل أن لجهنم سبع دركات ست منها لأصناف الكفار وللأعتناء بأمر عذابهم واستمراره ناسب أن يقوم عليه ثلاثة واحد في الوسط واثنان في الطرفين

ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r4.speaker: قائلون
ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r4.claim: One symbolic explanation combines the endpoint of the small numbers, nine, with the beginning of the large numbers, ten.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r4.anchor: وقيل أن العدد على وجهين قليل وهو من الواحد إلى التسعة وكثير وهو من العشرة إلا ما لا نهاية له فجمع بين نهاية القليل وبداية الكثير

ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r5.claim: Most scholars, in al-Alusi’s preferred account, say the number’s precise wisdom is unknowable; it is a mutashabih matter to affirm while consigning its knowledge to God, and the proposed rationales are unreliable.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r5.anchor: والذي مال إليه أكثر العلماء أن ذلك مما لا يعلم حكمته على التحقيق إلا الله عز وجل وهو كالمتشابه يؤمن به ويفوض علمه إلى الله تعالى وكل ما ذكر مما لا يعول عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r6.speaker: أبو جعفر
ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r6.claim: Abu Ja‘far reads the compound with a quiescent ع, avoiding a sequence of moving vowels in what functions as one name.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r6.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر وطلحة ابن سليمان تسعة عشر بإسكان العين وهو لغة فيه كراهة توالي الحركات فيما هو كاسم واحد

ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r7.speaker: طلحة ابن سليمان
ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r7.claim: Talha ibn Sulayman shares the reading تسعة عشر with a quiescent ع, a dialect form avoiding consecutive vowels.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r7.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر وطلحة ابن سليمان تسعة عشر بإسكان العين وهو لغة فيه كراهة توالي الحركات فيما هو كاسم واحد

ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r8.speaker: أنس بن مالك
ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r8.claim: Anas, Ibn Abbas, Ibn Qutb, and Ibrahim ibn Qutta are reported to read تسعة with a damma on ت as a built form, avoiding five successive fatḥas.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r8.anchor: وقرأ أنس بن مالك وابن عباس وابن قطب وابراهيم بن قتة تسعة بضم التاء وهي حركة بناء عدل إليها عن الفتح لتوالي خمس فتحات

ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas is among those reported to read تسعة with a built damma on ت to avoid a run of five fatḥas.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r9.anchor: وقرأ أنس بن مالك وابن عباس وابن قطب وابراهيم بن قتة تسعة بضم التاء وهي حركة بناء عدل إليها عن الفتح لتوالي خمس فتحات

ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r10.speaker: ابن قطب
ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r10.claim: Ibn Qutb is among those reported to read تسعة with a built damma on ت to avoid a run of five fatḥas.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r10.anchor: وقرأ أنس بن مالك وابن عباس وابن قطب وابراهيم بن قتة تسعة بضم التاء وهي حركة بناء عدل إليها عن الفتح لتوالي خمس فتحات

ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r11.speaker: إبراهيم بن قتة
ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r11.claim: Ibrahim ibn Qutta is among those reported to read تسعة with a built damma on ت to avoid a run of five fatḥas.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r11.anchor: وقرأ أنس بن مالك وابن عباس وابن قطب وابراهيم بن قتة تسعة بضم التاء وهي حركة بناء عدل إليها عن الفتح لتوالي خمس فتحات

ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r12.speaker: أنس بن مالك
ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r12.claim: Anas also reads تسعةُ أعشرَ, which the author of al-Lawāmi‘ suggests treats أعشر as a plural of ten assimilated to the compound form.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r12.anchor: أنس أيضا تسعة بالضم أعشر بالفتح قال صاحب اللوامح

ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r13.speaker: صاحب اللوامح
ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r13.claim: The author of al-Lawāmi‘ explains Anas’s أعشر as a plural of عشرة treated like the second element of تسعة عشر.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r13.anchor: قال صاحب اللوامح فيجوز أنه جمع العشرة على أعشر ثم أجراه مجرى تسعة عشر

ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r14.speaker: أنس بن مالك
ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r14.claim: Anas is also reported to read تسعة وعشر with damma and to turn the hamza into a pure wāw for ease, keeping the initial damma as a built vowel.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r14.anchor: وعنه أيضا تسعة وعشر بالضم وقلب الهمزة واوا خالصة تخفيفا والتاء فيهما مضمومة ضمة بناء لما سمعت آنفا

ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r15.speaker: سليمان بن قتة
ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r15.claim: Sulayman ibn Qutta reads تسعة أعشر with an inflectional damma and genitive annexation; al-Lawāmi‘ calls أعشر a plural of ten and says the reading denotes ninety angels.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r15.anchor: وعن سليمان بن قتة وهو أخو إبراهيم أنه قرأ تسعة أعشر بضم التاء ضمة إعراب والأضافة إلى أعشر وجره منونا

ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r16.speaker: صاحب اللوامح
ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r16.claim: Al-Lawāmi‘ says the plural reading, whether inflected or built, explicitly means ninety angels.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r16.anchor: وقد صرح بأن الملائكة على القراءة بهذا الجمع معربا أو مبنيا تسعون ملكا

ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r17.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r17.claim: Al-Zamakhshari calls أعشر a plural of عشير, like يمين and أيمن, and explains the reading as nine angels, each a عشير with his followers, totaling ninety.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r17.anchor: وقال الزمخشري جمع عشير مثل يمين وأيمن وروي عنه أنه قال تسعة من الملائكة كل واحد منهم عشير فهم مع أشياعهم تسعون

ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r18.speaker: ابن جني
ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r18.claim: Ibn Jinni says the reading otherwise lacks a clear basis, unless it means nine groups of عشير, “companions.”
ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r18.anchor: ولهذا قال ابن جني لا وجه لتلك القراءة إلا أن يعني تسعة عشر جمع العشير وهم الأصدقاء

ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r19.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r19.claim: Mujahid takes the pronoun هي to refer to Saqar.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r19.anchor: وما هي أي سقر كما يقتضيه كلام مجاهد

ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r20.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r20.claim: Other suggested antecedents for هي are the verses describing Saqar, the number of its keepers, the divine hosts, or earthly fire; the strongest is the prior interpretation.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r20.anchor: وقيل الضمير للآيات الناطقة بأحوال سقر وقيل لعد خزنتها والتذكير والعظة فيها

ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r21.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r21.claim: The clause may coordinate with “I shall roast him in Saqar”; the intervening account of the keepers is a parenthesis magnifying Hell’s power and severity.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r21.anchor: والعطف قيل على قوله تعالى سأصليه سقر وما جعلنا أصحاب النار إلى هنا اعتراض ووجهه أنه قيل عليها تسعة عشر وزيادة في تهويل أمر جهنم

ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r22.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r22.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r22.claim: The reminder lies in God’s creation of beings so mighty that a few can torment and destroy innumerable creatures, demonstrating His incomprehensible greatness.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r22.anchor: في خلقه تعالى ما هو في غاية العظمة حتى يكون القليل منهم معذبا ومهلكا لما لا يحصى دلالة على أنه عز وجل لا يقدر حق قدره

ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r23.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r23.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r23.claim: The two occurrences of البشر—in this verse and “scorching the البشر”—form complete verbal and written paronomasia.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p129/r23.anchor: وبين البشر ههنا والبشر فيما سبق أعني قوله تعالى لواحة للبشر على تفسير الجمهور تجنيس تام لفظي وخطي

ALUSI-FULL:v1p13#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p13#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p13#2/r1.claim: Al-Alusi distinguishes God's eternal speech, an attribute of the speaker, from recited letters on created sound, which image it; mutawatir usage establishes the latter as God's speech by religious convention, figurative only as an image.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p13#2/r1.anchor: بل هو صورة من صور كلامه القديم القائم به تعالى ومظهر تنزلاته فهو دال على الحقيقي القائم فسمى كلاما حقيقة شرعية لذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v1p13#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p13#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p13#2/r2.claim: Al-Alusi says this reading is what al-Taftazani indicates, avoids the feared consequences, and shows that al-Mawaqif's objection rests on an assumption.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p13#2/r2.anchor: وإلى هذا يشير كلام التفتازاني فلا يلزم شيء من المفاسد وإعتراض صاحب المواقف مبني على ظنه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p13#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p13#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p13#2/r3.claim: In his fifth reply, Al-Alusi says al-Mawaqif's pronoun may refer to the uttered content rather than the act of utterance; inner speech lacks sequence mentally, while external utterance orders it.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p13#2/r3.anchor: أن كلام صاحب المواقف ليس نصافي أن الضمير راجع إلى التلفظ بل يحتمل أن يكون راجعا إلى الملفوظ

ALUSI-FULL:v1p13#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p13#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p13#2/r4.claim: Thus, the statement that it is created can refer to the externally uttered image, so proofs of createdness concern that image rather than inward speech and the objection falls away.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p13#2/r4.anchor: وهو الذي هو حادث أي الملفوظ بالتلفظ الخارجي الذي هو الصورة حادث لا اللفظ النفسي

ALUSI-FULL:v1p13#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p13#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p13#2/r5.claim: The miracle objection assumes verbal Quran cannot be eternal divine speech; Al-Alusi answers that its descent into genuine Arabic wording is miraculous, while the eternal Quran is inner wording joined to meaning.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p13#2/r5.anchor: المعجزة هو القرآن في مرتبة تنزله إلى الألفاظ الحقيقة العربية فكونه لفظا حقيقيا عربيا مجعول بالنص

ALUSI-FULL:v1p13#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p13#2/r6.speaker: عفيف الدين الإيجي
ALUSI-FULL:v1p13#2/r6.claim: Al-Iji analyzes a statement into its wording, intended sense, the speaker's knowledge of the relation, and the relation's actual truth; the last two are not speech by consensus, and Ashʿarīs exclude the wording, leaving its meaning.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p13#2/r6.anchor: قال تلميذ مولانا الدواني عفيف الدين الإيجي ما حاصله أن هذا الذي تدعيه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p13#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p13#2/r7.speaker: عفيف الدين الإيجي
ALUSI-FULL:v1p13#2/r7.claim: For command and prohibition, Iji likewise counts will or aversion, spoken wording, and its meaning; excluding the first and second under the Ashʿarī account leaves the concept as their inner speech.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p13#2/r7.anchor: قال تلميذ مولانا الدواني عفيف الدين الإيجي ما حاصله أن هذا الذي تدعيه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p13#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p13#2/r8.speaker: عفيف الدين الإيجي
ALUSI-FULL:v1p13#2/r8.claim: Iji argues that defining inner speech as a meaning without letters conflicts with ordinary language and Arabic usage, where speech consists only of a combination of letters.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p13#2/r8.anchor: قال تلميذ مولانا الدواني عفيف الدين الإيجي ما حاصله أن هذا الذي تدعيه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p13#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p13#2/r9.speaker: عفيف الدين الإيجي
ALUSI-FULL:v1p13#2/r9.claim: Iji argues that scripture repeatedly says God calls His servants and authentic reports specify a voice; treating over 100,000 explicit texts as metaphor is unreasonable.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p13#2/r9.anchor: قال تلميذ مولانا الدواني عفيف الدين الإيجي ما حاصله أن هذا الذي تدعيه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p13#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p13#2/r10.speaker: عفيف الدين الإيجي
ALUSI-FULL:v1p13#2/r10.claim: Iji argues that one inner meaning cannot cover distinct commands, prohibitions, reports, and individual utterances; otherwise all scriptures would contain identical content, and speech would be both truth-apt and not truth-apt.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p13#2/r10.anchor: قال تلميذ مولانا الدواني عفيف الدين الإيجي ما حاصله أن هذا الذي تدعيه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p271/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p271/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p271/r1.claim: An unnamed preceding boast says the least among them would enter the Fire and then they would pass into Paradise; the verse was revealed in response.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p271/r1.anchor: الأيسر في النار ونمضي فندخل الجنة. فأنزل الله عز وجل

BAYDAWI-FULL:74:31/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:31/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:31/r1.claim: The keepers are angels so they differ in kind from the punished, will not pity them or comfort them, and are the strongest and most wrathful servants of God.
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:31/r1.anchor: ليخالفوا جنس المعذبين فلا يرقون لهم ولا يستروحون إليهم، ولأنهم أقوى الخلق بأسا وأشدهم غضبا لله

BAYDAWI-FULL:74:31/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:31/r2.speaker: أبو جهل
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:31/r2.claim: After hearing that nineteen guarded the Fire, Abū Jahl challenged Quraysh to see whether ten of them could overpower one guardian; the verse was revealed.
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:31/r2.anchor: روي أن أبا جهل لما سمع عليها تسعة عشر قال لقريش

BAYDAWI-FULL:74:31/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:31/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:31/r3.claim: The number nineteen tests unbelievers, provoking scorn, mockery, and disbelief that so few could punish most humans and jinn.
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:31/r3.anchor: وما جعلنا عددهم إلا العدد الذي اقتضى فتنتهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:74:31/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:31/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:31/r4.claim: The intended act of making the number may be its announcement, which makes the following explanation of its purposes apt.
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:31/r4.anchor: ولعل المراد الجعل بالقول ليحسن تعليله بقوله

BAYDAWI-FULL:74:31#2/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:31#2/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:31#2/r1.claim: People of the Book gain certainty about Muhammad's prophethood and the Qurʾān's truth because the number matches their scripture.
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:31#2/r1.anchor: أي في ذلك وهو تأكيد للاستيقان وزيادة الإيمان ونفي لما يعرض للمتيقن

BAYDAWI-FULL:74:31#2/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:31#2/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:31#2/r2.claim: Believers increase their faith through belief in the Qurʾān and by affirming the People of the Book's testimony to it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:31#2/r2.anchor: بالإيمان به وبتصديق أهل الكتاب به

BAYDAWI-FULL:74:31#2/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:31#2/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:31#2/r3.claim: The absence of doubt reinforces certainty and increased faith, removing doubts that might otherwise arise even in the certain.
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:31#2/r3.anchor: أي في ذلك وهو تأكيد للاستيقان وزيادة الإيمان ونفي لما يعرض للمتيقن حيثما عراه شبهة

BAYDAWI-FULL:74:31#2/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:31#2/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:31#2/r4.claim: Those with sickness in their hearts are people of doubt or hypocrisy; the verse predicts in Mecca what would occur in Medina after the migration.
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:31#2/r4.anchor: شك أو نفاق، فيكون إخبارا بمكة عما سيكون في المدينة

BAYDAWI-FULL:74:31#2/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:31#2/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:31#2/r5.claim: The unbelievers here are those resolute in denial.

BAYDAWI-FULL:74:31#2/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:31#2/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:31#2/r6.claim: They ask what God intends by this strange number, treating it as an astonishing parable; some assumed it was a parable.
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:31#2/r6.anchor: أي شيء أراد بهذا العدد المستغرب استغراب المثل، وقيل لما استبعدوه حسبوا أنه مثل مضروب

BAYDAWI-FULL:74:31#2/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:31#2/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:31#2/r7.claim: In this manner God misguides unbelievers and guides believers.
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:31#2/r7.anchor: مثل ذلك المذكور من الإضلال والهدى يضل الكافرين ويهدي المؤمنين

BAYDAWI-FULL:74:31#2/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:31#2/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:31#2/r8.claim: Only God knows His hosts as they truly are: no one else can enumerate possible beings, comprehend their realities and attributes, or grasp why each has its specific qualities and relations.
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:31#2/r8.anchor: إذ لا سبيل لأحد إلى حصر الممكنات والاطلاع على حقائقها وصفاتها وما يوجب اختصاص كل منها بما يخصه من كم وكيف واعتبار ونسبة

BAYDAWI-FULL:74:31#2/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:31#2/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:31#2/r9.claim: “It” may refer to Saqar, the number of its keepers, or the sūra; each serves as a reminder to humanity.
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:31#2/r9.anchor: وما سقر أو عدة الخزنة أو السورة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p231/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p231/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p231/r1.claim: The companions of the Fire are its keepers, not its human inmates; their angelic nature makes them powerful and prevents pity, weakness, or the inmates’ ability to overpower or rest with them.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p231/r1.anchor: أصحاب النار } أي خزنتها { إلا ملائكتة } أي إنهم ليسوا من جنس المعذبين

BIQAI-FULL:v8p231/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p231/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p231/r2.claim: The angels are far stronger than human beings: a single angel’s cry can destroy an entire city, as happened to Thamud, and each keeper commands forces only God can count.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p231/r2.anchor: بل الواحد منم يصيح صيحة واحدة فيهلك مدينة كاملة كما وقع لثمود

BIQAI-FULL:v8p231/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p231/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p231/r3.claim: The number is a trial because its wisdom is obscure and the scoffing disbeliever treats nineteen as too few, turning the count into an occasion for mockery and further unbelief.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p231/r3.anchor: وكانت الحكمة في تعيين هذا العد غير ظاهر , وكان هذا العدد مما يستقله المتعنت فيزيده كفرا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p231/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p231/r4.speaker: أبو جهل
BIQAI-FULL:v8p231/r4.claim: Abu Jahl mocks the reported count, asking whether ten Quraysh men cannot overpower one keeper.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p231/r4.anchor: أبو جهل , قال : ثكلتكم أمهاتكم , أسمع ابن أبي كبشة يقول كذا وأنتم أدلهم

BIQAI-FULL:v8p231/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p231/r5.speaker: أبو الأشد بن أسيد بن كلدة الجمحي
BIQAI-FULL:v8p231/r5.claim: Abu al-Ashadd boasts that he can handle seventeen angels himself while the others take two, in mockery of the warning.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p231/r5.anchor: فقال أبو الأشد بن أسيد بن كلدة الجمحي - وكان شديد البطش : أنا أكفيكم سبعة عشر

BIQAI-FULL:v8p231/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p231/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p231/r6.claim: Their taunting stems from denying resurrection and treating this description of its consequences as a target for obstinate challenge.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p231/r6.anchor: وهذا كله على سبيل الاستهزاء , فإنهم مكذبون بالبعث الذي هذا من آثاره

BIQAI-FULL:v8p231/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p231/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p231/r7.claim: Scripture’s people already know this number from their books, and hearing it confirms their certainty.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p231/r7.anchor: وكان في علم أهل الكتاب أن هذه العدة عدتهم

BIQAI-FULL:v8p231/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p231/r8.speaker: البغوي
BIQAI-FULL:v8p231/r8.claim: Al-Baghawi says the number nineteen is written in the Torah and Gospel.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p231/r8.anchor: قال البغوي : مكتوب في التوراة والإنجيل أنهم تسعة عشر

BIQAI-FULL:v8p231/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p231/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p231/r9.claim: The passive wording “those given the Book” needs no named giver because the act of giving suffices and God is already understood as the giver.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p231/r9.anchor: بناه للمفعول لأن مطلق الإيتاء كاف في ذلك من غير احتياج إلى تعيين المؤتي

BIQAI-FULL:v8p231/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p231/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p231/r10.claim: Believers grow in faith by affirming what they had not understood, especially when they see others tested by it; faith in such matters is greater.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r1.claim: The scriptural People of the Book do not develop deliberate, cultivated doubt because their knowledge already matches the truth of the number.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r1.anchor: أي يشك شكا يحصل بتعمد وتكسب

BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r2.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r2.claim: Ibn Burjān reports from Jābir that some People of the Book asked the Prophet about Hell’s keepers; he indicated ten, then nine, and they affirmed him. Asked about Paradise’s keepers, they answered, “a loaf.”
BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r2.anchor: قال ابن برجان : وروى جابر بن عبد الله رضي الله عنهما

BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r3.claim: Believers whose faith is firmly rooted do not doubt because the proofs have made the matter as clear to them as daylight.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r3.anchor: لا يرتاب الذين رسخ الإيمان عندهم لما رأوا من الدلائل التي جعلتهم في مثل ضوء النهار

BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r4.claim: The heart’s illness means doubt or even a small measure of hypocrisy.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r4.anchor: أي شك أو نفاق وإن قل

BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r5.claim: The sūra’s prediction of people with hypocrisy before hypocrites existed is a sign of prophethood.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r5.anchor: ونزول هذه السورة قبل وجود المنافقين علم من أعلام النبوة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r6.claim: God may intend one result as His primary purpose and arrange another as a secondary purpose; leaving a town to oppose most people illustrates the distinction.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r6.anchor: ولا ينكر جعل الله تعالى بعض الأمور مقصودة لشيء

BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r7.claim: These are people settled in disbelief, certain and open in their denial, who conceal the truth shown by the proofs.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r7.anchor: أي ويقول الراسخون في الكفر الجازمون بالتكذيب

BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r8.claim: One possible sense of “a likeness” is something so startling that the small number seems astonishing beside God’s greatness.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r8.anchor: من جهة أنه صار بذلك مستغربا استغراب المثل

BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r9.claim: Alternatively, “likeness” signals that the number is not meant literally but represents something they failed to understand.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r9.anchor: أو أن ذلك إشارة إلى أنه ليس المراد به ظاهره بل مثل لشيء لم يفهموه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r10.claim: They wrongly take the small count to conflict with divine majesty; few in number can be stronger than many and better demonstrate comprehensive power.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r10.anchor: وما علموا أن القليل من حيث العدد قد يكون أعظم

BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r11.claim: God guides or misguides whomever He wills, through whatever words He wills, by this very statement or by another means.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r11.anchor: أي الذي له مجامع العظمة ومعاقد العز

BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r12.claim: The deliberately obscure count of nineteen tests temperaments: the deviant demand an explanation, then reject or doubt what they cannot fathom, while the sound-natured submit and affirm that all is from their Lord.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r12.anchor: لأن المنحرف الطباع يبحث عن عللها بحثا متعنتا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r13.claim: Only God knows the number and qualities of His troops, including the keepers of Hell; their count says nothing about the limit of His forces.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r13.anchor: أي المحسن إليك بأنواع الإحسان المدبر لأمرك

BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r14.claim: A report says seventy thousand angels enter the Frequented House each day and never return for another turn.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r14.anchor: فقد روي أن البيت المعمور يدخله كل يوم سبعون ألفا من الملائكة لا تعود إليهم نوبة أخرى

BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r15.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r15.claim: A report compares the earth within heaven to a ring cast in a desert, and each heaven to the one above it in the same way.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r15.anchor: وقد ورد أن الأرض في السماء كحلقة ملقاة في فلاة وكل سماء في التي فوقها كذلك

BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r16.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r16.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r16.claim: A report says heaven groans, as it should, because every space the size of a foot contains a standing angel at prayer.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r16.anchor: ورد في الخبر : أطت السماء وحق لها أن تئط

BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r17.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r17.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r17.claim: The angels once included those who uprooted the seven towns of Lot’s people and lifted them to the sky.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r17.anchor: فقد كان في الملائكة من اقتلع مدائن قوم لوط وهي سبع ورفعها إلى عنان السماء

BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r18.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r18.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r18.claim: Every substance and accident in a human is among God’s troops: disrupting a still vein, stopping a moving one, or blocking or opening a cavity could kill a person.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r18.anchor: لو تحرك عرق ساكن أو سكن متحرك أو انسد مجوف

BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r19.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r19.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r19.claim: Hellfire is a powerful reminder for all people; embodied humans already know its effects, though God can create something more painful and severe than anything creatures know.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r19.anchor: أي تذكرة عظيمة لكل من هو ظاهر البشرة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r20.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r20.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r20.claim: The obscure description of God’s forces mercifully opens a path to surrender to divine wisdom; emphasis suits most hearers’ crooked temperaments and tendency to reject.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p232/r20.anchor: وكان ذلك من رحمة العباد ليفتح لهم بابا إلى التسليم لما يغمض

DURR-FULL:v8p332/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p332/r9.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v8p332/r9.claim: Al-Suddi says Qurayshi Abu al-Ashaddayn boasted he could fend off the nineteen keepers, after which the verse clarified that they are angels.
DURR-FULL:v8p332/r9.anchor: عن السدي قال: لما نزلت {عليها تسعة عشر} قال رجل من قريش يدعى أبا الأشدين

DURR-FULL:v8p333/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p333/r1.speaker: أبو العوام
DURR-FULL:v8p333/r1.claim: Abu al-Awwam asks if the keepers are nineteen angels or nineteen thousand; the narrator argues they are angels because their number is a test, and Abu al-Awwam agrees.
DURR-FULL:v8p333/r1.anchor: أبي العوام فقرأ هذه الآية {عليها تسعة عشر} فقال: ما تقولون أتسعة عشر ملكا أو تسعة عشر ألفا قلت: لا بل تسعة عشر ملكا

DURR-FULL:v8p333/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p333/r2.speaker: أبو العوام
DURR-FULL:v8p333/r2.claim: Abu al-Awwam says each keeper carries an iron two-pronged hammer whose blow sends seventy thousand people into Hell.
DURR-FULL:v8p333/r2.anchor: كنا عند أبي العوام فقرأ هذه الآية {عليها تسعة عشر} فقال: ما تقولون

DURR-FULL:v8p333/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p333/r3.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p333/r3.claim: Mujahid says the keepers were made a test for disbelievers.
DURR-FULL:v8p333/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله: {عليها تسعة عشر} قال: جعلوا فتنة

DURR-FULL:v8p333/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p333/r4.speaker: أبو الأشدين الجمحي
DURR-FULL:v8p333/r4.claim: Abu al-Ashaddayn al-Jumahi boasts that the keepers could not reach his strength before he drove them from Hell.
DURR-FULL:v8p333/r4.anchor: قال أبو الأشدين الجمحي: لا يبلغون رتوتي حتى أجهضهم عن جهنم

DURR-FULL:v8p333/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p333/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p333/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas reports Abu al-Ashaddayn challenged others to leave him alone with Hell’s keepers, saying he would handle them.
DURR-FULL:v8p333/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس {وما جعلنا عدتهم إلا فتنة للذين كفروا} قال: قال أبو الأشدين: خلوا بيني وبين خزنة جهنم

DURR-FULL:v8p333/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p333/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p333/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas transmits the Prophet’s description of the keepers: lightning-like eyes, spike-like mouths, power exceeding humans and jinn, and the ability to carry a crowd beneath a mountain into the Fire.
DURR-FULL:v8p333/r6.anchor: وحدثت أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وصف خزان جهنم فقال: كأن أعينهم البرق

DURR-FULL:v8p333/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p333/r7.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v8p333/r7.claim: Ibn Jurayj says the People of the Book find the keepers’ number, nineteen, in their scripture, while agreement strengthens believers’ faith.
DURR-FULL:v8p333/r7.anchor: عن ابن جريج {ليستيقن الذين أوتوا الكتاب} أنهم يجدون عدتهم في كتابهم تسعة عشر

DURR-FULL:v8p333/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p333/r8.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p333/r8.claim: Qatadah says the People of the Book become certain because the keepers’ number matches their scripture.
DURR-FULL:v8p333/r8.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله: {ليستيقن الذين أوتوا الكتاب} قال: يستيقن أهل الكتاب حين وافق عدد خزنة النار

DURR-FULL:v8p333/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p333/r9.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p333/r9.claim: Mujahid says the keepers’ number is written in the People of the Book’s scripture.
DURR-FULL:v8p333/r9.anchor: عن مجاهد {ليستيقن الذين أوتوا الكتاب} قال: يجدونه مكتوبا عندهم عدة خزنة النار

DURR-FULL:v8p333/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p333/r10.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p333/r10.claim: Qatadah says the Qur’an confirms the earlier Torah and Gospel on the nineteen keepers.
DURR-FULL:v8p333/r10.anchor: عن قتادة {ليستيقن الذين أوتوا الكتاب ويزداد الذين آمنوا إيمانا} قال: صدق القرآن الكتب التي خلت قبله التوراة والإنجيل أن خزنة جهنم تسعة عشر

DURR-FULL:v8p333/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p333/r11.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p333/r11.claim: Qatadah identifies those with sickness in their hearts as hypocrites.
DURR-FULL:v8p333/r11.anchor: عن قتادة {ليستيقن الذين أوتوا الكتاب ويزداد الذين آمنوا إيمانا} قال: صدق القرآن الكتب التي خلت قبله التوراة والإنجيل أن خزنة جهنم تسعة عشر

DURR-FULL:v8p334/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p334/r1.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p334/r1.claim: Qatadah says only God knows the vast number of His hosts.
DURR-FULL:v8p334/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله: {وما يعلم جنود ربك إلا هو} قال: من كثرتهم

DURR-FULL:v8p334/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p334/r2.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v8p334/r2.claim: Ibn Jurayj gives the same explanation: God alone knows the great multitude of His hosts.
DURR-FULL:v8p334/r2.anchor: وأخرج ابن المنذر عن ابن جريج مثله

DURR-FULL:v8p334/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p334/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص
DURR-FULL:v8p334/r3.claim: Abdullah ibn Amr says angels are the greatest created beings, made from the light of forearms and chest; their multitude is described as two thousand thousand.
DURR-FULL:v8p334/r3.anchor: عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص أي الخلق أعظم قال: الملائكة قال: من ماذا خلقت قال: من نور الذراعين والصدر

DURR-FULL:v8p334/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p334/r4.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v8p334/r4.claim: Ibn Jurayj explains “two thousand thousand” as an innumerable multitude.
DURR-FULL:v8p334/r4.anchor: قيل لابن جريج: ما ألفي ألفين قال: ما لا يحصى كثرته

DURR-FULL:v8p334/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p334/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p334/r5.claim: The Prophet says Ismail, keeper of the lowest heaven, has seventy thousand angels before him, each with one hundred thousand troops.
DURR-FULL:v8p334/r5.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حدثهم عن ليلة الإسراء قال: فصعدت أنا وجبريل

DURR-FULL:v8p334/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p334/r6.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p334/r6.claim: Mujahid identifies the reminder to humankind as the Fire.
DURR-FULL:v8p334/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد {وما هي إلا ذكرى للبشر} قال: النار

DURR-FULL:v8p334/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p334/r7.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p334/r7.claim: Qatadah likewise identifies the reminder as the Fire.
DURR-FULL:v8p334/r7.anchor: وأخرج عبد بن حميد وابن المنذر عن قتادة مثله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p291/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p291/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p291/r1.claim: The sūra is called al-Muddaththir in tafsīr works and manuscripts; the title describes the Prophet in the state in which he was addressed, or follows the word used in the sūra, as with al-Muzzammil.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p291/r1.anchor: تسمى في كتب التفسير ( سورة المدثر ) وكذلك سميت

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p291/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p291/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p291/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyyah and al-Qurṭubī report consensus that the sūra is Meccan; al-Itqān does not list it among partly Medinan sūras.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p291/r2.anchor: وهي مكية حكى الاتفاق على ذلك ابن عطية والقرطبي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p291/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p291/r3.speaker: محمد بن النقيب المقدسي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p291/r3.claim: Al-Ālūsī says Muḥammad ibn al-Naqīb al-Maqdisī reported a view, attributed ambiguously to Muqātil or concerning 74:31 onward, that this passage was revealed in Medina; Ibn ʿĀshūr found no chain or corroboration.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p291/r3.anchor: وذكر الآلوسي أن صاحب ( التحرير ) ( محمد بن النقيب المقدسي المتوفى سنة 698

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p291/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p291/r4.speaker: عائشة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p291/r4.claim: The report from ʿĀʾishah in both Ṣaḥīḥs says the first revelation comprised 96:1–5, followed by a pause, without mentioning any intervening revelation; this supports the view that al-Muddaththir was second.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p291/r4.anchor: في حديث عائشة في ( الصحيحين ) في صفة بدء الوحي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p293/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p293/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p293/r2.claim: It answers polytheists who belittled Hell's keepers and claimed their number was small.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p293/r2.anchor: الرد على المشركين الذين استخفوا بها وزعموا قلة عدد حفظتها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p293/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p293/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p293/r3.claim: The passage challenges the People of the Book by saying they did not know the keepers' number.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p293/r3.anchor: وتحدي أهل الكتاب بأنهم جهلوا عدد حفظتها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p293/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p293/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p293/r4.claim: The passage makes the disbelievers despair of escaping punishment.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p293/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p293/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p293/r5.claim: The passage portrays the disbelievers' misguidance in this world.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p293/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p293/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p293/r6.claim: It contrasts their condition with believers characterized by prayer, almsgiving, and belief in the Day of Recompense.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p293/r6.anchor: ومقابلة حالهم بحال المؤمنين أهل الصلاة والزكاة والتصديق بيوم الجزاء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p312/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p312/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p312/r8.claim: The number challenges the People of the Book to affirm the Qur'an, since their scholars possessed this knowledge; the next verse states the outcome.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p312/r8.anchor: وفي ذكر هذا العدد تحد لأهل الكتابين يبعثهم على تصديق القرآن إذ كان ذلك مما استأثر به علماؤهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p313/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p313/r1.speaker: ابن عباس وجابر بن زيد
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p313/r1.claim: Al-Tabari reports from Ibn Abbas and Jabir ibn Zayd that Abu Jahl mocked the nineteen, proposing that each ten Quraysh men could overpower one; God answered that the keepers were angels, whom humans cannot defeat.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p313/r1.anchor: روى الطبري عن ابن عباس وجابر بن زيد : ( أن أبا جهل لما سمع قوله تعالى : { عليها تسعة عشر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p313/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p313/r2.speaker: السدي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p313/r2.claim: Al-Suddi says Abu al-Ashadd ibn Kalda al-Jumahi mocked that he would shove ten keepers with his right shoulder and nine with his left so the others could pass into Paradise.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p313/r2.anchor: وفي ( تفسير القرطبي ) عن السدي : أن أبا الأشد بن كلدة الجمحي قال مستهزئا : لا يهولنكم التسعة عشر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p313/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p313/r3.speaker: قيل
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p313/r3.claim: Another report attributes to al-Harith ibn Kalda the boast that he would handle seventeen keepers and leave the other two to his companions.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p313/r3.anchor: وقيل : قال الحارث بن كلدة : أنا أكفيكم سبعة عشر واكفوني أنتم اثنين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p313/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p313/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p313/r4.claim: Aṣḥāb al-nār means Hell's keepers, previously introduced as being over Saqar in 74:30.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p313/r4.anchor: فالمراد من { أصحاب النار } خزنتها ، وهم المتقدم ذكرهم بقوله : { عليها تسعة عشر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p313/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p313/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p313/r5.claim: The exception ranges over kinds: God made the keepers exclusively from the kind of angels.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p313/r5.anchor: والاستثناء من عموم الأنواع ، أي ما جعلنا خزنة النار من نوع إلا من نوع الملائكة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p313/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p313/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p313/r6.claim: The restriction overturns Abu Jahl's assumption that the nineteen were human men whom he and his companions could overpower.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p313/r6.anchor: وصيغة القصر تفيد قلب اعتقاد أبي جهل وغيره ما توهموه أو تظاهروا بتوهمه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p313/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p313/r7.speaker: أبو الأشد بن أسيد الجمحي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p313/r7.claim: Abu al-Ashadd ibn Asid al-Jumahi is also quoted as boasting that the keepers could not reach his garment before he thrust them away from Hell.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p313/r7.anchor: فقد قال أبو الأشد بن أسيد الجمحي : لا يبلغون ثوبي حتى أجهضهم عن جهنم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p314/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p314/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p314/r1.claim: The number answers why keepers are nineteen rather than thousands for greater terror or one angel, since angels can perform any task God assigns; it exposes how differently people understand the Qur'an.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p314/r1.anchor: وهو كلام جار على تقدير الأسلوب الحكيم إذ الكلام قد أثار في النفوس تساؤلا عن فائدة جعل خزنة جهنم تسعة عشر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p314/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p314/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p314/r2.claim: The trial arose from mentioning the number in the previous verse; God set the keepers' number for another wisdom known to Him, not disclosed here.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p314/r2.anchor: وإنما حصلت الفتنة من ذكر عددهم في الآية السابقة . فقوله : { وما جعلنا عدتهم } تقديره

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p314/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p314/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p314/r3.claim: The exception is emptied into jaʿalnā's second-object position: ‘We made their count nothing but a trial’; fitna is a condition occurring to unbelievers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p314/r3.anchor: والاستثناء مفرغ لمفعول ثان لفعل { جعلنا } تقديره جعلنا عدتهم فتنة لا غير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p314/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p314/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p314/r4.claim: The implied purpose is that mentioning the number serves only as a trial for unbelievers, reversing their belief that it is insignificant.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p314/r4.anchor: والتقدير : ما جعلنا ذكر عدتهم لعلة وغرض إلا لغرض فتنة الذين كفروا ؛

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p315/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p315/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p315/r1.claim: Li-yastaqīna gives a second purpose for making the number a trial; since fitna is jaʿalnā's second object, the phrase is not coordinated to fitna.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p315/r1.anchor: وقوله : { ليستيقن الذين أوتوا الكتاب } الخ . علة ثانية لفعل { وما جعلنا عدتهم إلا فتنة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p315/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p315/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p315/r2.claim: Alternatively, li-lladhīna kafarū may be governed by both jaʿalnā and fitna: the number became a trial for unbelievers who produced corrupt interpretation, while others can defer to God and reflect.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p315/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون للذين كفروا } متعلقا بفعل { جعلنا وب فتنة } ، على وجه التنازع فيه ، أي ما جعلنا عدتهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p315/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p315/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p315/r3.claim: Istīqān is firm certainty; its sin and tāʾ intensify the meaning.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p315/r3.anchor: والاستيقان : قوة اليقين ، فالسين والتاء فيه للمبالغة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p315/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p315/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p315/r4.claim: The People of the Book here are Jews, who could become certain of the Qur'an's truth when they found this number matching their scriptures.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p315/r4.anchor: والمعنى : ليستيقنوا صدق القرآن حيث يجدون هذا العدد مصدقا لما في كتبهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p315/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p315/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p315/r5.claim: Jews traded in Mecca and Meccans went to Khaybar, Qurayza, and Yathrib for supplies; they exchanged reports about Muhammad, and polytheists hoped Jews would refute the Qur'an but did not.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p315/r5.anchor: وكان اليهود يترددون على مكة في التجارة ويتردد عليهم أهل مكة للميرة في خيبر وقريظة ويثرب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p315/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p315/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p315/r6.claim: Certainty may lead to faith when the mind is free of unbelief, as with ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam, or fail through obstinacy, envy, or fear of losing status or wealth; 2:146 says many Jews concealed truth.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p315/r6.anchor: والاستيقان من شأنه أن يعقبه الإيمان إذا صادف عقلا بريئا من عوارض الكفر كما وقع لعبد الله بن سلام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p315/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p315/r7.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p315/r7.claim: Al-Tirmidhi reports from Jabir ibn Abdullah that Jews asked whether the Prophet knew the keepers' number; after the Companions said they did not, he indicated ten, ten, and nine on his fingers, and they affirmed it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p315/r7.anchor: روى الترمذي بسنده إلى جابر بن عبد الله قال : قال ناس من اليهود لأناس من أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p315/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p315/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p315/r8.claim: The hadith does not require a Medinan setting, contrary to Qatada's report, since Quraysh and Jews exchanged Qur'anic information already in Mecca.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p315/r8.anchor: وليس في هذا ما يلجىء إلى اعتبار هذه الآية نازلة بالمدينة كما روي عن قتادة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p316/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p316/r1.speaker: ابن العربي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p316/r1.claim: Ibn al-Arabi says Jabir's hadith is authentic and notes the problem that the keepers' number occurs in a Meccan verse by consensus, while the Jews' exchange with the Prophet seems to occur in Medina.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p316/r1.anchor: قال أبوبكر ابن العربي في ( العارضة ) : حديث جابر صحيح والآية التي فيها { عليها تسعة عشر } ( المدثر : 30 ) مكية بإجماع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p316/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p316/r2.speaker: ابن العربي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p316/r2.claim: Ibn al-Arabi proposes that the Companions may have been Ansar who had not encountered the Meccan sura because it had not spread to them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p316/r2.anchor: فيحتمل أن الصحابة قالوا : لا نعلم ، لأنهم لم يكونوا قرأوا الآية ولا كانت انتشرت عندهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p316/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p316/r3.speaker: ابن العربي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p316/r3.claim: His alternative is that the Companions could not identify the nineteen specifically as keepers until God or the Prophet clarified it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p316/r3.anchor: ويحتمل أن الصحابة لم يمكنهم أن يعينوا أن التسعة عشر هم الخزنة دون أن يعينهم الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p316/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p316/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p316/r4.claim: The hadith thus confirms that the verse's prediction about the People of the Book came true years after its revelation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p316/r4.anchor: فقد ظهر مصداق قوله تعالى : { ليستيقن الذين أوتوا الكتاب } بعد سنين من وقت نزوله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p316/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p316/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p316/r5.claim: Faith increases quantitatively as each unseen fact joins what believers affirm; faith's essence is assent and certainty and does not increase in quality, which is how scriptural statements about increased faith should be understood.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p316/r5.anchor: ومعنى { ويزداد الذين ءامنوا إيمانا } أنهم يؤمنون به في جملة ما يؤمنون به من الغيب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p316#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p316#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p316#2/r1.claim: ‘And so the People of the Book and believers do not doubt’ coordinates with ‘so that the People of the Book become certain,’ eliminating doubt after knowledge grounded in proof.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p316#2/r1.anchor: وقوله : { ولا يرتاب الذين أوتوا الكتاب والمؤمنون } عطف على { ليستيقن الذين أوتوا الكتاب ، }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p316#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p316#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p316#2/r2.claim: The groups differ in practice: believers knew and acted, while the People of the Book knew but resisted, making their knowledge evidence against them and a source of regret.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p316#2/r2.anchor: فالمؤمنون علموا وعملوا ، والذين أوتوا الكتاب علموا وعاندوا فكان علمهم حجة عليهم وحسرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p316#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p316#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p316#2/r3.claim: Mentioning their lack of doubt indirectly prepares for naming the diseased-hearted and disbelievers' bad interpretation: Jews were regarded as sounder in judgment, exposing the others as inferior.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p316#2/r3.anchor: والمقصود من ذكره التمهيد لذكر مكابرة الذين في قلوبهم مرض والكافرين في سوء فهمهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p316#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p316#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p316#2/r4.claim: The lām in ‘so that they say’ marks an outcome, as in Pharaoh's household taking Moses in to become an enemy and grief to them in 28:8.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p316#2/r4.anchor: واللام لام العاقبة مثل التي في قوله تعالى : { فالتقطه آل فرعون ليكون لهم عدوا وحزنا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p316#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p316#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p316#2/r5.claim: The heart's disease is bad intent toward the Qur'an and Messenger; these were wavering Meccans, including al-Akhnas ibn Shurayq and al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, not hypocrites who arose only in Medina.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p316#2/r5.anchor: والمرض في القلوب : هو سوء النية في القرآن والرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم وهؤلاء هم الذين لم يزالوا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p316#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p316#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p316#2/r6.claim: In mādhā, mā is interrogative and dhā, originally a demonstrative, functions as ‘that which’ after an interrogative mā or man.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p316#2/r6.anchor: و { ماذا أراد الله } استفهام إنكاري فإن ( ما ) استفهامية ، و ( ذا ) أصله اسم إشارة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p316#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p316#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p316#2/r7.claim: Their incredulous question asks what God intended by this parable; denying a purpose for the number implies God did not say it and seeks to deny its reality or revelation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p316#2/r7.anchor: والمعنى : لم يرد الله هذا العدد الممثل به ، وقد كني بنفي إرادة الله العدد عن إنكار أن يكون الله قال ذلك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p317/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p317/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p317/r1.claim: The demonstrative ‘this’ points back to the preceding statement that the keepers of Hell are nineteen.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p317/r1.anchor: والإشارة بهذا إلى قوله : { عليها تسعة عشر }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p317/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p317/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p317/r2.claim: مثلا is accusative as a circumstantial qualifier of هذا; المثل means a description, asking why this number rather than another such as twenty.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p317/r2.anchor: و { مثلا } منصوب على الحال من هذا ، والمثل : الوصف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p317/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p317/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p317/r3.claim: Alternatively, المثل describes the extraordinary situation of Hell’s keepers being nineteen, as in the description of Paradise.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p317/r3.anchor: والمثل : وصف الحالة العجيبة ، أي ما وصفه من عدد خزنة النار

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p317/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p317/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p317/r4.claim: كذلك refers to the preceding whole account, from the scripture recipients’ certainty through the question about the example, construed as what was mentioned.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p317/r4.anchor: اسم الإشارة عائد إلى ما تضمنه الكلام المتقدم من قوله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p317/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p317/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p317/r5.claim: Those with diseased hearts and disbelievers are led astray, including scripture recipients who became certain but did not believe; believers are guided and their faith grows.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p317/r5.anchor: مثل ذلك الضلال الحاصل للذين في قلوبهم مرض وللكافرين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p317/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p317/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p317/r6.claim: The comparison brings the abstract divine creation of human circumstances close through a familiar concrete event, teaching Muslims to seek what benefits their souls.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p317/r6.anchor: والغرض من هذا التشبيه تقريب المعنى المعقول وهو تصرف الله تعالى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p317/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p317/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p317/r7.claim: The likeness is causation: God makes both guidance and misguidance causes for a wisdom grounded in His knowledge; people’s receptivity ranges from guidance to doubt, denial, and misunderstanding.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p317/r7.anchor: ووجه الشبه هو السببية في اهتداء من يهتدي وضلال من يضل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p317/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p317/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p317/r8.claim: The compact comparison encompasses many outward patterns, as dispositions lead from soundness to soundness, uncertainty to uncertainty, or resentment and stubbornness to further error.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p317/r8.anchor: فانطوى التشبيه من قوله : { كذلك } على أحوال وصور كثيرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p318/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p318/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p318/r1.claim: God’s attribution of misguidance reflects His creation of original dispositions, desires, worldly interconnections, prophetic invitations, and the resistance of leaders of error; all are created by God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p318/r1.anchor: وإسناد الإضلال إلى الله تعالى باعتبار أنه موجد الأسباب الأصلية في الجبلات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p318/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p318/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p318/r2.claim: Souls that seek good and salvation must expose themselves to one of the two paths after reflection; each bears what it has earned.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p318/r2.anchor: فما على الأنفس المريدة الخير والنجاة إلا التعرض لأحد المهيعين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p318/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p318/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p318/r3.claim: God’s will in this matter is connected to His knowledge of the course the guided and misguided will follow.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p318/r3.anchor: ومشيئة الله ذلك تعلق علمه بسلوك المهتدين والضالين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p318/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p318/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p318/r4.claim: كذلك is an adverbial phrase standing for an omitted cognate accusative: misguidance and guidance of this kind; it is not the construction in 2:143.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p318/r4.anchor: ومحل { كذلك } نصب بالنيابة عن المفعول المطلق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p318/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p318/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p318/r5.claim: Fronting the cognate-object description stresses the comparison; it also creates an initial grouping followed by division into misguidance and guidance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p318/r5.anchor: وقدم وصف المفعول المطلق للاهتمام بهذا التشبيه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p318/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p318/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p318/r6.claim: This comprehensive coda refutes the speculations of disbelievers and the spiritually ill about reports of the unseen and afterlife, including Abu Jahl’s question about Hell’s keepers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p318/r6.anchor: كلمة جامعة لإبطال التخرصات التي يتخرصها الضالون ومرضى القلوب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p318/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p318/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p318/r7.claim: جنود is the plural of جند, a troop or army; metaphorically it means creatures God appoints to carry out His command, like an army executing orders.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p318/r7.anchor: والجنود : جمع جند وهو اسم لجماعة الجيش واستعير هنا للمخلوقات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p318/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p318/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p318/r8.claim: Adding ‘your Lord’ to the Prophet’s pronoun honors him and hints that some of these forces will support the Prophet.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p318/r8.anchor: وإضافة رب إلى ضمير النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إضافة تشريف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p318/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p318/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p318/r9.claim: The negation concerns detailed knowledge of the forces’ numbers, qualities, and properties; people know the keepers’ number because God disclosed it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p318/r9.anchor: ونفي العلم هنا نفي للعلم التفصيلي بأعدادها وصفاتها وخصائصها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p319/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p319/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p319/r1.claim: The foremost reading continues the statement that their number is a test: the useful lesson is to remember punishment, since describing a thing helps bring it to mind; scoffers instead debate the number.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p319/r1.anchor: أعلاها أن يكون هذا تتمة لقوله : { وما جعلنا عدتهم إلا فتنة للذين كفروا }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p319/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p319/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p319/r2.claim: On the preferred reading, هي refers to the number of the keepers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p319/r2.anchor: وضمير { هي } على هذا الوجه إلى { عدتهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p319/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p319/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p319/r3.claim: The pronoun may instead refer to the preceding discourse, understood as the story, description, or Quranic verses; the sense remains similar.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p319/r3.anchor: ويجوز أن يرجع الضمير إلى الكلام السابق وتأنيث ضميره لتأويله بالقصة أو الصفة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p319/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p319/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p319/r4.claim: Another possibility is that هي refers to Saqar, which serves as a reminder through its threat and horrors; an omitted noun such as its mention or description is understood.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p319/r4.anchor: ويحتمل أن يرجع إلى سقر } ( المدثر : 26 ) وإنما تكون { ذكرى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p319/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p319/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p319/r5.claim: The pronoun may refer to the forces of the Lord, with the omitted sense being their mention or the number of some of them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p319/r5.anchor: ويحتمل أن يرجع ضمير { هي } إلى { جنود ربك }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p319/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p319/r6.speaker: الزجاج
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p319/r6.claim: Al-Zajjaj allows هي to refer to earthly fire, which reminds people of the fire of the afterlife, as in the verse calling fire a reminder.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p319/r6.anchor: وجوز الزجاج أن يكون الضمير راجعا إلى نار الدنيا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p319/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p319/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p319/r7.claim: On the earthly-fire reading, the expression uses semantic redirection (istikhdām).

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p319/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p319/r8.speaker: قيل
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p319/r8.claim: Another view says the number reminds people that God needs no helpers, so they should not wonder how nineteen can face Hell’s many inhabitants.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p319/r8.anchor: وقيل : المعنى : وما عدتهم إلا ذكرى للناس ليعلموا غنى الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p319/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p319/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p319/r9.claim: The context accommodates these readings through the eloquence of Quranic arrangement; after 74:29 the pronoun would unambiguously refer to Saqar, showing the effect of sentence placement.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p319/r9.anchor: ولو وقعت إثر قوله : { لواحة للبشر } ( المدثر : 29 ) لتمحض ضمير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p61/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p61/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p61/r1.claim: The ten sound, mutawatir readings may differ in rhetorical refinement, eloquence, semantic richness, or fame, but the differences are close and rarely make one reading superior overall.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p61/r1.anchor: بعضها من خصوصيات البلاغة أو الفصاحة أو كثرة المعاني أو الشهرة ، وهو تمايز متقارب ، وقل أن يكسب إحدى القراءات في تلك الآية رجحانا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p61/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p61/r2.speaker: محمد بن جرير الطبري والزمخشري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p61/r2.claim: Al-Tabari and al-Zamakhshari accepted preferring one transmitted reading to another.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p61/r2.anchor: ومن هؤلاء الإمام محمد بن جرير الطبري ، والعلامة الزمخشري

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p61/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p61/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p61/r3.claim: Ibn Ashur says many of the grounds on which such scholars preferred readings are open to criticism, which he will address in context.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p61/r3.anchor: وفي أكثر ما رجح به نظر سنذكره في مواضعه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p61/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p61/r4.speaker: أبو الوليد ابن رشد
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p61/r4.claim: Ibn Rushd says choosing a mutawatir reading for clearer grammar, sounder transmission, or easier pronunciation is unobjectionable.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p61/r4.anchor: وقد سئل ابن رشد عما يقع في كتب المفسرين والمعربين من اختيار إحدى القراءتين المتواترتين وقولهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p61/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p61/r5.speaker: الشيوخ المتقدمون بالأندلس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p61/r5.claim: Early Andalusian shaykhs chose Warsh, and the mosque imam recited only that reading, which eases the articulation of hamzas.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p61/r5.anchor: كرواية ورش التي اختارها الشيوخ المتقدمون عندنا أي بالأندلس فكان الإمام في الجامع لا يقرأ إلا بها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p61/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p61/r6.speaker: مالك
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p61/r6.claim: Malik disliked explicit hamza pronunciation in Quran recitation during prayer and said he did not approve of it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p61/r6.anchor: وفي كتاب الصلاة الأول من العتبية : سئل مالك عن النبر في القرآن فقال : إني لأكرهه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p61/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p61/r7.speaker: أبو الوليد ابن رشد
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p61/r7.claim: Ibn Rushd explains nabr as pronouncing hamza in its original form and favors Warsh's facilitation, consistent with Malik's dislike.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p61/r7.anchor: قال ابن رشد في البيان يعنى بالنبر ههنا إظهار الهمزة في كل موضع على الأصل فكره ذلك واستحب فيه التسهيل على رواية ورش

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p61/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p61/r8.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p61/r8.claim: A report says the Prophet's speech did not pronounce hamza explicitly; examples of facilitation include Ya'juj, dhi'b as dhib, and mu'min as mumin.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p61/r8.anchor: لما جاء من أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لم تكن لغته الهمز أي إظهار الهمز في الكلمات المهموزة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p61/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p61/r9.speaker: أبو الوليد ابن رشد
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p61/r9.claim: Ibn Rushd reports that Cordoba's mosque had long required Warsh in prayer, a practice abandoned only in recent times.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p61/r9.anchor: كان العمل جاريا في قرطبة قديما أن لا يقرأ الإمام بالجامع في الصلاة إلا برواية ورش

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p61/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p61/r10.speaker: خلف بن هشام البزار
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p61/r10.claim: Khalaf selected a distinct reading from the Kufan readings, counted as the tenth; he differs from Hamza, al-Kisa'i, and Abu Bakr only at 21:95, reading wa-ḥarāmun with an alif after rāʾ like Hafs and the majority.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p61/r10.anchor: وهذا خلف بن هشام البزار راوي حمزة ، قد اختار لنفسه قراءة من بين قراءات الكوفيين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p61/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p61/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p61/r11.claim: Inimitability means matching every demand of the situation and admits no degrees, so preferring one reading does not make another less inimitable.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p61/r11.anchor: حد الإعجاز مطابقة الكلام لجميع مقتضى الحال ، وهو لا يقبل التفاوت

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p61/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p61/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p61/r12.claim: An inimitable passage may still have particular beauties, such as paronomasia, hyperbole, eloquence, or variation; Ibn Ashur illustrates this with 23:72.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p61/r12.anchor: كالجناس والمبالغة ، أو تتعلق بزيادة الفصاحة ، أو بالتفنن مثل ) أم تسألهم خرجا فخراج ربك خير (

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p61/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p61/r13.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p61/r13.claim: Some readings may preserve a Prophetic concession to use synonyms for ease, as suggested by Umar's dispute with Hisham; another reading may reach the highest rhetorical level while the concession remains close to inimitability.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p61/r13.anchor: على أنه يجوز أن تكون إحدى القراءات نشأت عن ترخيص النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم للقارئ أن يقرأ بالمرادف تيسيرا على الناس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p61/r14.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p61/r14.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p61/r14.claim: The challenge is to produce a surah, not every individual verse; since the shortest surah has three verses, any set of three Quranic verses must be inimitable as a whole.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p61/r14.anchor: وأما الإعجاز فلا يلزم أن يتحقق في كل آية من آي القرآن لأن التحدي إنما وقع بسورة مثل سور القرآن ، وأقصر سورة ثلاث آيات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p61/r15.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p61/r15.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p61/r15.claim: Ibn Ashur limits discussion to the ten famous mutawatir readings, chiefly their best-known transmissions, despite the seven's greater fame; he begins with Nafiʿ through Qalun, the Tunisian reading, then gives other readers' variants.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p61/r15.anchor: أنا أقتصر في هذا التفسير على التعرض لاختلاف القراءات العشر المشهورة خاصة في أشهر روايات الراوين عن أصحابها لأنها متواترة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p61/r16.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p61/r16.speaker: author
