IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p61/r16.claim: Today Qalun is read in parts of Tunisia and Egypt and in Libya; Warsh is read in parts of Tunisia and Egypt and throughout Algeria, Morocco and its dependencies, and Sudan.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p61/r16.anchor: والقراءات التي يقرأ بها اليوم في بلاد الإسلام من هذه القراءات العشر ، هي قراءة نافع برواية قالون في بعض القطر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p408/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p408/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p408/r1.claim: The keepers of the Fire are angels, not humans, so who could withstand or overpower them?
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p408/r1.anchor: وما جعلنا أصحاب النار إلا ملائكة لا أدميين فمن يطيقهم ومن يغلبهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p408/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p408/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p408/r2.claim: The small number of keepers was made a trial for disbelievers and a means for scripture-recipient believers to confirm the Prophet's truth from their scripture, which gives the number as nineteen; this strengthens their faith and prevents doubt.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p408/r2.anchor: وما جعلنا عدتهم في هذه القلة إلا فتنة أي ضلالة للذين كفروا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p408/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p408/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p408/r3.claim: People of the Book who believe gain faith in Muḥammad when they find his report agreeing with their scripture.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p408/r3.anchor: ويزداد الذين آمنوا من أهل الكتاب إيمانا أي تصديقا بمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم إذ وجدوا ما يخبرهم موافقا لما في كتابهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p408/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p408/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p408/r4.claim: The People of the Book and believers will not doubt the number of the keepers.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p408/r4.anchor: ولا يرتاب الذين أوتوا الكتاب والمؤمنون أي ولا يشك هؤلاء في عدد الخزنة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p408/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p408/r5.speaker: الأكثرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p408/r5.claim: The sickness in their hearts means hypocrisy, according to most exegetes.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p408/r5.anchor: وليقول الذين في قلوبهم مرض وفيه ثلاثة أقوال أحدها أنه النفاق ذكره الأكثرون

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p408/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p408/r6.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p408/r6.claim: It means doubt; Muqātil identifies these people as Jews of Medina and considers the verse Medinan.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p408/r6.anchor: والثاني أنه الشك قاله مقاتل وزعم أنهم يهود أهل المدينة وعنده أن هذه الآية مدنية

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p408/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p408/r7.speaker: الحسين بن الفضل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p408/r7.claim: It means opposition; al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Faḍl argues there was no hypocrisy in Mecca and this sūra is Meccan.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p408/r7.anchor: والثالث أنه الخلاف قاله الحسين بن الفضل وقال لم يكن بمكة نفاق وهذه مكية

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p408/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p408/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p408/r8.claim: The disbelievers here are the Arab polytheists.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p408/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p408/r9.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p408/r9.claim: They ask what God meant by this statement or report; mathal can mean the report itself.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p408/r9.anchor: ماذا أراد الله أي أي شيء أراد الله بهذا الحديث والخبر مثلا والمثل يكون بمعنى الحديث نفسه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p408/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p408/r10.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p408/r10.claim: As God misguides those who reject the number of keepers, He guides those who believe it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p408/r10.anchor: كذلك أي كما أضل من انكر عدد الخزنة وهدى من صدق يضل الله من يشاء ويهدي من يشاء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p408/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p408/r11.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p408/r11.claim: The armies are angels God created to punish the people of the Fire; each of the nineteen has helpers whose number only God knows.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p408/r11.anchor: يعني من الملائكة الذين خلقهم لتعذيب أهل النار وذلك أن لكل واحد من هؤلاء التسعة عشر من الأعوان ما لا يعلمه إلا الله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p408/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p408/r12.speaker: أبو جهل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p408/r12.claim: The verse was revealed after Abū Jahl said that Muḥammad had no more soldiers than nineteen.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p408/r12.anchor: وأنزل في قول أبي جهل أما لمحمد من الجنود إلا تسعة عشر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p408/r13.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p408/r13.speaker: الماوردي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p408/r13.claim: Al-Māwardī offers as a possible wisdom that nineteen combines the largest single-digit number, nine, with the smallest number above the single digits, ten.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p408/r13.anchor: وذكر الماوردي في وجه الحكمة في كونهم تسعة عشر قولا محتملا فقال التسعة عشر عدد يجمع أكثر القليل وأقل الكثير

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p408/r14.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p408/r14.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p408/r14.claim: The Fire in this world is only a reminder of the Fire of the Hereafter.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p408/r14.anchor: ثم رجع إلى ذكر النار فقال تعالى وما هي إلا ذكرى أي ما النار في الدنيا إلا مذكرة لنار الآخرة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p269/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p269/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p269/r1.claim: The keepers of Hell are harsh and powerful angels; this corrects Quraysh’s reaction to the stated number of keepers.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p269/r1.anchor: يقول تعالى: {وما جعلنا أصحاب النار} أي: خزانها، {إلا ملائكة} أي: [زبانية] (3) غلاظا شدادا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p269/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p269/r2.speaker: أبو جهل
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p269/r2.claim: Abu Jahl taunts Quraysh by asking whether ten of them can overcome one keeper.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p269/r2.anchor: فقال أبو جهل: يا معشر قريش، أما يستطيع كل عشرة منكم لواحد منهم فتغلبونهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p269/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p269/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p269/r3.claim: God’s answer is that the keepers are so formidable that no one can withstand or overpower them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p269/r3.anchor: أي: شديدي الخلق لا يقاومون ولا يغالبون

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p269/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p269/r4.speaker: أبو الأشدين
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p269/r4.claim: Abu al-Ashaddayn, named Kilda ibn Asid ibn Khalaf, boasts that he can handle seventeen keepers if Quraysh handle two; he was said to stand on a cowhide while ten people pulled until it tore without moving him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p269/r4.anchor: وقد قيل: إن أبا الأشدين -واسمه: كلدة بن أسيد بن خلف-قال: يا معشر قريش، اكفوني منهم اثنين وأنا أكفيكم منهم سبعة عشر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p269/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p269/r5.speaker: السهيلي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p269/r5.claim: Al-Suhayli says the strongman was the man who challenged the Prophet to a wrestling match, promising belief if thrown; the Prophet threw him repeatedly, yet he did not believe.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p269/r5.anchor: قال السهيلي: وهو الذي دعا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى مصارعته وقال: إن صرعتني آمنت بك، فصرعه النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم مرارا، فلم يؤمن

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p269/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p269/r6.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p269/r6.claim: Ibn Ishaq attributes the wrestling story to Rukana ibn Abd Yazid ibn Hashim ibn al-Muttalib.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p269/r6.anchor: وقد نسب ابن إسحاق خبر المصارعة إلى ركانة بن عبد يزيد بن هاشم بن المطلب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p269/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p269/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p269/r7.claim: Ibn Kathir sees no contradiction between al-Suhayli’s and Ibn Ishaq’s identifications of the wrestler.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p269/r7.anchor: قلت: ولا منافاة بين ما ذكراه، والله أعلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p269#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p269#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p269#2/r1.claim: God stated that the keepers number nineteen as a test for people.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p269#2/r1.anchor: أي: إنما ذكرنا عدتهم أنهم تسعة عشر اختبارا منا للناس،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p269#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p269#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p269#2/r2.claim: People given scripture become certain that the Messenger is true because his statement matches what their previously revealed scriptures contain.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p269#2/r2.anchor: أي: يعلمون أن هذا الرسول حق؛ فإنه نطق بمطابقة ما بأيديهم من الكتب السماوية المنزلة على الأنبياء قبله.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p269#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p269#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p269#2/r3.claim: Believers increase in faith when they witness the truthfulness of Muhammad’s reports.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p269#2/r3.anchor: أي: إلى إيمانهم. بما يشهدون من صدق إخبار نبيهم محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p269#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p269#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p269#2/r4.claim: The verse also means that the People of the Book and believers do not doubt.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p269#2/r4.anchor: ولا يرتاب الذين أوتوا الكتاب والمؤمنون

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p269#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p269#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p269#2/r5.claim: Those whose hearts are sick are hypocrites; with the disbelievers, they ask what God intends by this example.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p269#2/r5.anchor: أي: من المنافقين {والكافرون ماذا أراد الله بهذا مثلا} ؟

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p269#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p269#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p269#2/r6.claim: Matters like this strengthen faith in some hearts and unsettle others; God’s wisdom is profound and His proof decisive.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p269#2/r6.anchor: أي: من مثل هذا وأشباهه يتأكد الإيمان في قلوب أقوام، ويتزلزل عند آخرين، وله الحكمة البالغة، والحجة الدامغة.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p270/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p270/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p270/r1.claim: Only God knows the number and multitude of His troops, so the nineteen keepers must not be mistaken for all His forces.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p270/r1.anchor: أي: ما يعلم عددهم وكثرتهم إلا هو تعالى، لئلا يتوهم متوهم أنهم تسعة عشر فقط

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p270/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p270/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p270/r2.claim: Some misguided Greek philosophers and their followers among the two religious communities reduced the verse to ten intellects and nine souls, doctrines they invented without proof; they accepted the verse’s opening but rejected its close.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p270/r2.anchor: فأرادوا تنزيلها على العقول العشرة والنفوس التسعة، التي اخترعوا دعواها وعجزوا عن إقامة الدلالة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p270/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p270/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p270/r3.claim: In the Israʾ report, the Prophet says that seventy thousand angels enter the Bayt al-Maʿmur each day and do not return to it again.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p270/r3.anchor: عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال في صفة البيت المعمور الذي في السماء السابعة: "فإذا هو يدخله في كل يوم سبعون ألف ملك، لا يعودون إليه آخر ما عليهم"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p270/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p270/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p270/r4.claim: The Prophet tells Abu Dharr that heaven groans, with no space the breadth of fingers lacking an angel prostrating; knowing what he knows would make people weep more, laugh less, and cry out to God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p270/r4.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "إني أرى ما لا ترون، وأسمع ما لا تسمعون

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p270/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p270/r5.speaker: الترمذي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p270/r5.claim: Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah transmit the Abu Dharr report through Israʾil; al-Tirmidhi grades it hasan gharib and notes it is also transmitted as Abu Dharr’s own statement.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p270/r5.anchor: ورواه الترمذي وابن ماجه، من حديث إسرائيل (5) وقال الترمذي: حسن غريب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p270/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p270/r6.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p270/r6.claim: Jabir reports that every foot, handspan, or palm’s space in the seven heavens contains an angel standing, prostrating, or bowing; at Judgment they will confess they did not worship God as He deserves, while affirming they never associated partners with Him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p270/r6.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "ما في السموات السبع موضع قدم ولا شبر ولا كف إلا وفيه ملك قائم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p272#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p272#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p272#2/r1.claim: Mujahid and other early authorities say “it” refers to the described fire, which is a reminder to humankind.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p272#2/r1.anchor: قال مجاهد وغير واحد: {وما هي} أي: النار التي وصفت، {إلا ذكرى للبشر}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p9/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p9/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p9/r1.claim: The third class of Israelite reports is neither confirmed nor contradicted by Islamic sources; one should neither believe nor deny it, though it may be related, and it usually has no religious benefit.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p9/r1.anchor: والثالث: ما هو مسكوت عنه لا من هذا القبيل ولا من هذا القبيل، فلا نؤمن به ولا نكذبه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p9/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p9/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p9/r2.claim: Examples include the Cave Companions' names, dog's color and number, the tree of Moses' staff, Abraham's birds, the cow part used in the murder, and the tree from which God spoke to Moses; Quranic silence leaves these details without useful consequence.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p9/r2.anchor: كما يذكرون في مثل هذا أسماء أصحاب الكهف، ولون كلبهم، وعدتهم، وعصا موسى من أي الشجر كانت؟

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p9/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p9/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p9/r3.claim: In 18:22, Ibn Kathir says the Quran weakens the claims of three or five sleepers and leaves the claim of seven unchallenged, showing it is correct; it teaches people not to argue beyond what is useful or ask the People of the Book.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p9/r3.anchor: فقد اشتملت هذه الآية الكريمة على الأدب في هذا المقام وتعليم ما ينبغي في مثل هذا، فإنه تعالى أخبر عنهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p9/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p9/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p9/r4.claim: The Quran says that only a few know the sleepers' number and directs the Prophet to answer that God knows it, since seeking the detail has no value.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p9/r4.anchor: فإنه ما يعلم بذلك إلا قليل من الناس، ممن أطلعه الله عليه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p9/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p9/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p9/r5.claim: The best way to report disagreement is to include all views, identify the sound one, reject false ones, and state what practical benefit the disagreement has.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p9/r5.anchor: فهذا أحسن ما يكون في حكاية الخلاف: أن تستوعب الأقوال في ذلك المقام، وأن تنبه على الصحيح منها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p9/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p9/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p9/r6.claim: A report of disagreement is incomplete if it omits views or gives them without identifying the correct one, since the omitted view may be right and uncorrected error misleads.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p9/r6.anchor: فأما من حكى خلافا في مسألة ولم يستوعب أقوال الناس فيها فهو ناقص، إذ قد يكون الصواب في الذي تركه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p9/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p9/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p9/r7.claim: Someone who knowingly endorses a false view has deliberately lied; someone who does so unknowingly has erred.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p9/r7.anchor: فإن صحح غير الصحيح عامدا فقد تعمد الكذب، أو جاهلا فقد أخطأ

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p9/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p9/r8.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p9/r8.claim: Inventing disagreements about useless matters or multiplying wordings that reduce to one or two positions wastes time and is like wearing two garments of falsehood.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p9/r8.anchor: وكذلك من نصب الخلاف فيما لا فائدة تحته، أو حكى أقوالا متعددة لفظا ويرجع حاصلها إلى قول أو قولين معنى

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p32#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p32#2/r1.speaker: سالم بن عبد الله
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p32#2/r1.claim: Salim reports that Marwan sought Hafsa’s source sheets; after her death Ibn Umar sent them, and Marwan destroyed them to prevent later doubts because their contents were preserved in the codex; Ibn Kathir grades the chain sound.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p32#2/r1.anchor: أخبرني سالم بن عبد الله: أن مروان كان يرسل إلى حفصة يسألها الصحف

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p32#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p32#2/r2.speaker: الزهري عن خارجة عن أبيه
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p32#2/r2.claim: A report through al-Zuhri, Kharija, and his father says an al-Ahzab verse was attached to its surah; Ibn Kathir says this report is wrongly placed after Uthman’s compilation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p32#2/r2.anchor: ما رواه الزهري (3) عن خارجة عن أبيه في شأن آية الأحزاب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p32#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p32#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p32#2/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir holds that attaching the al-Ahzab verse occurred during Abu Bakr’s collection, citing another al-Zuhri report via Ubayy ibn al-Sabbaq from Zayd ibn Thabit; Uthmani copies do not place it in a margin.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p32#2/r3.anchor: هذا كان حال جمع الصديق الصحف كما جاء مصرحا به في غير هذه الرواية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p32#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p32#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p32#2/r4.claim: Ibn Kathir praises Abu Bakr and Umar’s collection to preserve the Qur’an and Uthman’s unification of the readings in one codex, following the final presentation to Gabriel.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p32#2/r4.anchor: فهذه الأفعال (6) من أكبر القربات التي بادر إليها الأئمة الراشدون

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p32#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p32#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p32#2/r5.claim: The Prophet reviewed the Qur’an with Gabriel twice in his final Ramadan; Ibn Kathir links this to the Prophet telling Fatima during his illness that he thought his death was near, a report found in both Ṣaḥīḥ collections.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p32#2/r5.anchor: فإنه عارضه به عامئذ مرتين؛ ولهذا قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لفاطمة ابنته

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p32#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p32#2/r6.speaker: محمد بن سيرين
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p32#2/r6.claim: Ibn Sirin reports that after the Prophet’s death Ali vowed to collect the Qur’an in a codex before wearing his robe again, then explained to Abu Bakr that his vow was not opposition to the caliphate and gave allegiance.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p32#2/r6.anchor: عن محمد بن سيرين قال: لما توفي النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أقسم علي ألا يرتدي برداء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p32#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p32#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p32#2/r7.claim: Ibn Kathir notes the Ali report is disconnected; only the weak narrator Ashʿath mentions a codex, while other transmitters’ wording means Ali completed memorizing the Qur’an, since a memorizer is called one who collected it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p32#2/r7.anchor: هكذا رواه وفيه انقطاع، ثم قال: لم يذكر المصحف أحد إلا أشعث (10) وهو لين الحديث (11)

JISHUMI:v10p7161/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7161/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7161/r9.claim: Malak originally means messenger, then became specific to a class of accountable beings with a particular form; the cited poetry illustrates messenger and angel usage.
JISHUMI:v10p7161/r9.anchor: والملك: أصله الرسالة إلا أنه اختص بنوع من المكلفين

JISHUMI:v10p7161/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7161/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7161/r10.claim: The form tisʿata ʿashara is accusative because two nouns have been joined to form one name.
JISHUMI:v10p7161/r10.anchor: نصب (تسعة عشر) لأنهما اسمان جعلا اسما واحدا

JISHUMI:v10p7161/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7161/r11.speaker: ابن عباس، وقتادة، والضحاك
JISHUMI:v10p7161/r11.claim: After hearing that Hell has nineteen keepers, Abū Jahl mocked Quraysh's numbers; Abū al-Asad offered to handle seventeen while they handled two, and the verse was revealed.
JISHUMI:v10p7161/r11.anchor: فأنزل الله تعالى: (وما جعلنا أصحاب النار) الآية، عن ابن عباس، وقتادة، والضحاك

JISHUMI:v10p7162/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r1.speaker: مقاتل
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r1.claim: A report from Muqātil says Abū Jahl claimed Muhammad had only nineteen helpers, prompting revelation that only God knows His hosts.
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r1.anchor: فأنزل الله تعالى: (وما يعلم جنود ربك إلا هو)، عن مقاتل

JISHUMI:v10p7162/r21.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r21.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r21.claim: The companions or keepers of the Fire whom God appointed are angels.

JISHUMI:v10p7162/r22.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r22.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r22.claim: The keepers' number is a trial and test for disbelievers, who are challenged to believe it, and a test for the People of the Book concerning the Prophet's truthfulness.
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r22.anchor: أي: شدة تعبد واختبار؛ لأنه كلفهم تصديقه، وامتحن أهل الكتاب ليعلموا صدقه

JISHUMI:v10p7162/r23.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r23.speaker: الأصم
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r23.claim: Al-Aṣamm says the small number is a test to show that God can strengthen them so that they can do the work of a much larger number.
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r23.anchor: ليعلموا أنه قادر على تقويتهم، وأنهم يقومون مقام العدد الكثير، عن الأصم

JISHUMI:v10p7162/r24.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r24.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r24.claim: The People of the Book, Jews and Christians, are to become certain the report is true because it agrees with their scriptures.
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r24.anchor: من اليهود والنصارى أنه حق؛ لموافقة خبره لما في كتبهم

JISHUMI:v10p7162/r25.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r25.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r25.claim: Another view says the number proves that God can give one being strength equal to that of many.
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r25.anchor: ليعلموا أنه يقدر أن يجعل في واحد من القوة ما يقوم بخلق كثير

JISHUMI:v10p7162/r26.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r26.speaker: ابن عباس، وقتادة، والضحاك
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r26.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Qatādah, and al-Ḍaḥḥāk report that the number nineteen is stated in the Torah and Gospel.
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r26.anchor: وقيل: هي في التوراة والإنجيل: تسعة عشر، عن ابن عباس، وقتادة، والضحاك

JISHUMI:v10p7162/r27.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r27.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r27.claim: One explanation is that believers' faith is first made manifest, then grows stronger.
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r27.anchor: ليظهر إيمانهم أيضا كما ظهر لغيره ليزدادوا إيمانا

JISHUMI:v10p7162/r28.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r28.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r28.claim: Another explanation says believers grow in faith because the report conveys what only God could know, so they recognize it as a miracle and God's speech.
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r28.anchor: لأنه يخبرهم بما لا يعلم إلا الله فيعلمون أنه معجز، وأنه كلام الله سبحانه

JISHUMI:v10p7162/r29.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r29.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r29.claim: The People of the Book and believers should not doubt that the report is true, God's power, or the Prophet's prophethood.
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r29.anchor: لا يشك الذين أوتوا الكتاب والمؤمنون في أنه الحق، وفي قدرة الله

JISHUMI:v10p7162/r30.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r30.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r30.claim: One explanation takes the lām as the lām of consequence: they hear it and say this while intending disbelief; another takes it as a prediction of what they will say.
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r30.anchor: قيل: اللام لام العاقبة، يعني إذا سمعوا قالوا هذا، وغرضهم التكذيب

JISHUMI:v10p7162/r31.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r31.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r31.claim: Although one view takes those with sickness in their hearts as hypocrites, the author favors dissent and disbelief because the verse is Meccan and there was no hypocrisy there.
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r31.anchor: الآية مكية وليس بها نفاق والكافرون ماذا أراد

JISHUMI:v10p7162/r32.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r32.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r32.claim: One view says the disbelievers ask what the count nineteen means and grow more doubtful.
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r32.anchor: قيل: ببيان هذا العدد وما معنى تسعة عشر، يزدادون شكا

JISHUMI:v10p7162/r33.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r33.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r33.claim: Another view says they ask why nineteen should frighten them when they vastly outnumber that count, not realizing one angel could equal many.
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r33.anchor: قالوا: ما معنى التخويف بتسعة عشر مع كثرة عددنا؟ وظنوا أن العدد شرط

JISHUMI:v10p7162/r34.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r34.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r34.claim: Just as God made the angel keepers and their number a trial, He imposes duties that reveal who is astray and who is guided; misguidance is attributed to Him because the test originates in His command.
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r34.anchor: كما جعلنا خزنة النار ملائكة ذوي عدد محنة واختبارا، كذلك يكلف ليظهر الضلال والهدى

JISHUMI:v10p7162/r35.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r35.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r35.claim: Abū Muslim interprets this as God leading whom He wills away from Paradise and reward and guiding whom He wills to them, or destroying some and rewarding others.
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r35.anchor: وقيل: يهلك من يشاء ويثيب من يشاء، عن أبي مسلم

JISHUMI:v10p7162/r36.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r36.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r36.claim: Another explanation says God rules that people are astray or guided according to what He finds in them.
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r36.anchor: وقيل: يحكم بضلال من يشاء، وبهداية من يشاء على حسبما يوجد منهم

JISHUMI:v10p7162/r37.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r37.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r37.claim: As He consigns this disbeliever to Saqar, God likewise deals with whom He wills by leading astray or rewarding them.
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r37.anchor: كما أصلى هذا الكافر سقر كذلك يفعل الله بمن يشاء أن يضله أو يثيبه

JISHUMI:v10p7162/r38.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r38.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r38.claim: Abū ʿAlī takes kadhalika to mean that God punishes whom He wills and turns him away from Paradise, while guiding whom He wills to it.
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r38.anchor: يعذب من يشاء ويصرفه عن الجنة، ويهدي إليه من يشاء، عن أبي علي

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r2.claim: Abū Jahl mocked the nineteen and challenged Quraysh to overpower them; Abū al-Ashadd volunteered to handle seventeen, and the revelation answered that the guardians are angels, not vulnerable men.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r2.anchor: قال أبو جهل لقريش : ثكلتكم أمهاتكم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r3.claim: Abū al-Ashadd ibn Usayd ibn Kalda, described as strong, offered to handle seventeen guardians and asked the others to handle two.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r3.anchor: فقال أبو الأشد بن أسيد بن كلدة الجمحى

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r4.claim: The reply says guardians are angels rather than men of the disbelievers' kind who can be overpowered.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r4.anchor: أي ما جعلناهم رجالا من جنسكم يطاقون

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r5.claim: The trial itself is not the cause of the outcomes; the number nineteen is substituted with a number liable to cause that trial.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r5.anchor: وإنما العدة نفسها هي التي جعلت سببا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r6.claim: People of Scripture recognize nineteen from their books and take it as confirmation of the Qur'an's divine origin, while unbelievers mock the number.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r6.anchor: لأن عدتهم تسعة عشر في الكتابين

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r7.claim: Believers grow in faith by accepting this as they accepted other revelations and by seeing Scripture readers confirm it.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r7.anchor: لتصديقهم بذلك كما صدقوا سائر ما أنزل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r8.claim: Stating certainty and absence of doubt emphasizes believers' composure and contrasts them with doubting hypocrites and unbelievers.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r8.anchor: إذا جمع لهم إثبات اليقين ونفي الشك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r9.claim: Although hypocrisy arose in Medina, this Meccan verse predicts the hypocrites who would appear there after the Hijra.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r9.anchor: المنافقون الذين ينجمون في مستقبل الزمان بالمدينة بعد الهجرة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r10.claim: Alternatively, disease means doubt: most Meccans doubted, while some were certain the message was false.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r10.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد بالمرض : الشك والارتياب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r11.claim: The causal لام need not state an intended goal; it can state a cause, as when one leaves town from fear of evil.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r12.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r12.claim: مثلا is either a specification for هذا or a circumstantial accusative, as in the cited she-camel called a sign.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r13.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r13.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r13.claim: Calling the number a parable borrows from unusual speech and conveys astonishment that God chose nineteen rather than twenty, implying a defective number and nondivine origin.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r13.anchor: لأنه مما غرب من الكلام وبدع

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r14.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r14.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r14.claim: The كاف is accusative, and كذلك points back to the account of guidance and misguidance.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r15.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r15.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r15.claim: Believers see God's wise act as wisdom and gain faith; disbelievers deny or doubt it and increase in disbelief and error.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r15.anchor: يفعل فعلا حسنا مبنيا على الحكمة والصواب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r16.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r16.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r16.claim: Only God knows each host's exact number and its wisdom, as with the counts of creation, calendar divisions, stars, and prescribed acts.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r16.anchor: إلا هو } ولا سبيل لأحد إلى معرفة ذلك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r17.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r17.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r17.claim: Alternatively, only God knows the armies because they are innumerable; nineteen does not limit His power, and the number has hidden wisdom.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r17.anchor: وما يعلم جنود ربك لفرط كثرتها إلا هو

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r18.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r18.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r18.claim: Alternatively, this answers Abū Jahl's question about whether Muhammad's Lord has only nineteen helpers, with the intervening clause parenthetical.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r19.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r19.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r19.claim: هي refers either to Saqar and its description as a reminder or to the verses describing it.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652#2/r19.anchor: أو ضمير الآيات التي ذكرت فيها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p44/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p44/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p44/r1.claim: The author shortened an earlier work while preserving many benefits and probing its hidden meanings; it was completed during Abū Bakr’s caliphate though he had expected the work to take over thirty years, and he credits the sanctuary’s blessing.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p44/r1.anchor: فأخذت في طريقة أخصر من الأولى مع ضمان التكثير من الفوائد والفحص عن السرائر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p44/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p44/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p44/r2.claim: Al-Fātiḥa is Meccan, though another view says it is both Meccan and Medinan because it descended once in each city.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p44/r2.anchor: مكية وقيل مكية ومدنية لأنها نزلت بمكة مرة وبالمدينة أخرى

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p44/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p44/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p44/r3.claim: It is called Umm al-Qurʾān because it contains the Qurʾān’s meanings: praise of God, worship through commands and prohibitions, and promise and threat.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p44/r3.anchor: وتمسمى أم القرآن لاشتمالها على المعاني التي في القرآن من الثناء على الله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p44/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p44/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p44/r4.claim: It is also called Sūrat al-Kanz and al-Wāfiya because it encompasses those meanings.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p44/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p44/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p44/r5.claim: It is called al-Ḥamd and al-Mathānī because it is repeated in every prayer unit.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p44/r5.anchor: وسورة الحمد والمثاني لأنه تثني في كل ركعة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p44/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p44/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p44/r6.claim: It is called al-Ṣalāh because reciting it in prayer makes the prayer excellent or sufficient.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p44/r6.anchor: وسورة الصلاة لأنها تكون فاضلة أو مجزئة بقراءتها فيها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p44/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p44/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p44/r7.claim: Its other names include Sūrat al-Shifāʾ and al-Shāfiya.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p44/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p44/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p44/r8.claim: The sūra has seven verses by agreement, though the excerpt breaks off while introducing a differing counting view.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p44/r8.anchor: وهي سبع آيات بالاتفاق الا أن منهم من عد

MUJAHID:v2p704#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p704#2/r1.speaker: رجل من بني تميم
MUJAHID:v2p704#2/r1.claim: A man of Banū Tamīm argues that the nineteen are nineteen thousand, reasoning from 74:31 that their number is a trial for unbelievers; Abū al-ʿAwwām affirms his answer.
MUJAHID:v2p704#2/r1.anchor: عن رجل من بني تميم قال كنا عند أبي العوام

MUJAHID:v2p704#2/r2.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p704#2/r2.speaker: أبو العوام
MUJAHID:v2p704#2/r2.claim: Abū al-ʿAwwām says each angel carries an iron mace with two prongs, whose blow sends seventy thousand flying, with a great distance between their shoulders.
MUJAHID:v2p704#2/r2.anchor: قال أبو العوام صدقت وبيد كل ملك منهم مرزبة من حديد لها شعبتان

MUQATIL:74:31/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:74:31/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:74:31/r1.claim: The keepers of the Fire are angels, and their small number was made a test for unbelievers, including Abu Jahl, Abu al-Ashdayn, and Quraysh's mockers.
MUQATIL:74:31/r1.anchor: قال الله تعالى: { وما جعلنا أصحاب النار إلا ملائكة } يعني خزان النار { وما جعلنا عدتهم } يعني قلتهم { إلا فتنة للذين كفروا }

MUQATIL:74:31/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:74:31/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:74:31/r2.claim: Believers among the People of the Torah know Muhammad's statement is true because their scripture gives the number of Hell's keepers as nineteen.
MUQATIL:74:31/r2.anchor: { ليستيقن } لكي يستيقين { الذين أوتوا الكتاب } يقول: ليعلم مؤمنو أهل التوراة أن الذي قال محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم حق، لأن عدة خزان جهنم في التوراة تسعة عشر.

MUQATIL:74:31/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:74:31/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:74:31/r3.claim: The description of angels as stern and mighty answers Abu al-Ashdayn's boast that he could defeat seventeen guardians.
MUQATIL:74:31/r3.anchor:
وأنزل الله في قول أبي الأشدين: أنا أكفيكم منهم سبعة عشر:
عليها ملائكة غلاظ شداد
[التحريم: 6]

MUQATIL:74:31#2/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:74:31#2/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:74:31#2/r1.claim: The believers increase in faith, meaning in confirmation, and do not doubt Muhammad or what he brought.
MUQATIL:74:31#2/r1.anchor: يعني تصديقا ولا يشكوا في محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم بما جاء به

MUQATIL:74:31#2/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:74:31#2/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:74:31#2/r2.claim: The People of the Torah and the believers should not doubt that Hell has nineteen keepers.
MUQATIL:74:31#2/r2.anchor: يقول: ولكى لا يرتاب يعني لكي لا يشك يقول: لئلا يشك

MUQATIL:74:31#2/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:74:31#2/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:74:31#2/r3.claim: Those with disease in their hearts are the doubting Jews of Medina; the unbelievers are Meccan Arab polytheists.
MUQATIL:74:31#2/r3.anchor: { وليقول الذين في قلوبهم مرض } يعني الشك، وهم اليهود من أهل المدينة { والكافرون } من أهل مكة، يعني مشركى العرب

MUQATIL:74:31#2/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:74:31#2/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:74:31#2/r4.claim: The deniers ask what God intends by the example because they consider the number of keepers too small.
MUQATIL:74:31#2/r4.anchor: { ماذآ أراد الله بهذا مثلا } يعني ذكره عدة خزنة جهنم، يستقلونهم

MUQATIL:74:31#2/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:74:31#2/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:74:31#2/r5.claim: Through this example God leads astray whom He wills from His religion and guides whom He wills to it.
MUQATIL:74:31#2/r5.anchor: يقول الله عز وجل: { كذلك يضل الله } بهذا المثل { من يشآء } عن دينه { ويهدي من يشآء } إلى دينه

MUQATIL:74:31#2/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:74:31#2/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:74:31#2/r6.claim: God alone knows the innumerable size of His armies, in response to Abu Jahl's mockery of the nineteen keepers.
MUQATIL:74:31#2/r6.anchor: { وما يعلم جنود ربك إلا هو } من الكثرة حين استقلوهم، فقال أبو جهل لقريش: أيعجز

MUQATIL:74:31#2/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:74:31#2/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:74:31#2/r7.claim: The pronoun refers to Saqar, which serves as a reminder and warning to humankind.
MUQATIL:74:31#2/r7.anchor: ثم رجع إلى سقر، فقال: { وما هي } يعني سقر { إلا ذكرى للبشر } [آية: 31] يعني سقر تذكر وتفكر للعالم.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#7/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#7/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#7/r1.claim: The keepers of the Fire are angels, unlike the punished; they show no pity and each has the strength of both humans and jinn.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#7/r1.anchor: لانهم خلاف جنس المعذبين فلا تأخذهم الرأفة والرقة لأنهم أشد الخق بأسا

NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#7/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#7/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#7/r2.anchor: تسعة عشر ﴿ إلا فتنة ﴾ أي ابتلاء واختيارا

NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#7/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#7/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#7/r3.claim: Abu Jahl boasted that, being strong, he could handle seventeen keepers and challenged others to deal with two; the verse clarifies that the keepers are powerful angels, not men one can overcome.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#7/r3.anchor: حتى قال أبو جهل لما نزلت وكان شديد البطش أنا أكفيكم سبعة عشر فاكفوني أنتم اثنين

NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#7/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#7/r4.speaker: قيل
NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#7/r4.claim: One explanation assigns six angels to lead unbelievers into the Fire, six to drive them, six to strike with iron maces, and Malik to guard Hell as their chief.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#7/r4.anchor: ان ستة منهم يقودون الكفرة إلى النار وستة يسوقونهم وستة يضربونهم بمقامع الحديد والآخر خازن جهنم وهومالك

NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#7/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#7/r5.speaker: قيل
NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#7/r5.claim: Another explanation says Saqar has nineteen levels, each overseen by an angel.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#7/r5.anchor: وقيل في سقر تسعة عشر دركا وقد سلط على كل درك ملك

NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#7/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#7/r6.speaker: قيل
NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#7/r6.claim: Another explanation assigns an angel to each of nineteen kinds of torment in Hell.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#7/r6.anchor: وقيل يعذب فيها بتسعة عشر لونا من العذاب وعلى كل لون ملك موكل

NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#7/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#7/r7.speaker: قيل
NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#7/r7.claim: A further explanation compares the nineteen keepers to mountains securing the earth and says Hell's original number was one hundred ninety.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#7/r7.anchor: وقيل ان جهنم تحفظ بما تحفظ به الأرض من الجبال وهي تسعة عشر وكان اصلها مائة وتسعين

NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#7/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#7/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#7/r8.claim: The People of the Book know the keepers' number as nineteen from their scriptures, so hearing it in the Qur'an confirms its divine origin for them.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#7/r8.anchor: لأن عدتهم تسعة عشر في الكتابين فاذا سمعوا بمثلها في القرآن أيقنوا أنه منزل من الله

NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#7/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#7/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#7/r9.claim: Believers' faith increases because they affirm this as they affirm the rest of revelation, or gain certainty from the agreement with their scripture.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#7/r9.anchor: لتصديقهم بذلك كما صدقوا سائر ما أنزل أو يزدادوا يقينا لموافقة كتابهم كتاب أولئك

NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#7/r10.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#7/r10.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#7/r10.claim: The statement that the People of the Book and believers do not doubt reiterates the certainty and increase of faith just mentioned.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#7/r10.anchor: هذا عطف أيضا وفيه توكيد للاستيقان وزيادة الايمان إذ الاستيقان وازدياد الايمان دالان على انتفاء الارتياب

NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#7/r11.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#7/r11.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#7/r11.claim: “Those with sickness in their hearts” can mean hypocrites; although hypocrisy arose in Medina, the verse predicts future hypocrites after the Hijra, while the disbelievers are in Mecca.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#7/r11.anchor: نفاق ﴿ والكافرون ﴾ والمشركون فان قلت النفاق ظهر في المدينة والسورة مكية

NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#7/r12.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#7/r12.speaker: قيل
NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#7/r12.claim: An alternative takes the sickness as doubt, since most people of Mecca were doubtful.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#7/r12.anchor: وقيل المراد بالمرض الشك والارتياب لأن أهل مكة كن أكثرهم شاكين

NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#7/r13.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#7/r13.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#7/r13.claim: “مثلا” may be an accusative of specification or a circumstantial accusative from “هذا”.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#7/r13.anchor: ومثلا تمييز لهذا أو حال منه

NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#7/r14.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#7/r14.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#7/r14.claim: The strange number is called a parable because it would circulate like proverbs; doubters use it to deny revelation, arguing that a divine count would not be an incomplete nineteen.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#7/r14.anchor: ولما كان ذكر العدد في غاية الغرابة وان مثله حقيق بان تسير به الركبان سيرها بالأمثال سمي مثلا

NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#7/r15.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#7/r15.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#7/r15.claim: God misguides those He knows choose error and guides those He knows choose guidance; the passage supports attributing the creation of acts and guidance and misguidance to God.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#7/r15.anchor: مثل لتصديقه ورؤية الحكمة في ذلك يضل الله من يشاء من عباده وهو الذي علم منه اختيار الضلال

NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#7/r16.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#7/r16.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#7/r16.claim: After Abu Jahl questioned whether Muhammad's Lord had only nineteen helpers, God says only He knows the innumerable hosts; He could easily make the keepers twenty, but their number has hidden wisdom.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#7/r16.anchor: ولما قال أبو جهل لعنه الله اما لرب محمد اعوان إلا تسعة عشر نزل

NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#7/r17.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#7/r17.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#7/r17.claim: “هي” may refer to Saqar and its description, or to the verses describing it; the phrase means a reminder to humanity.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#7/r17.anchor: ﴿ وما هي ﴾ متصل بوصف سقر وهي ضميرها أي وما سقر وصفتها

QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#2/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#2/r8.claim: God made the keepers angels rather than men so the damned would not try to overpower them.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#2/r8.anchor: أي لم نجعلهم رجالا فتتعاطون مغالبتهم

QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#2/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#2/r9.claim: Another explanation says angels differ from the humans and jinn they punish, feel no kinship-based pity, and are devoted to God and strongest in force.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#2/r9.anchor: وقيل: جعلهم ملائكة لأنهم خلاف جنس المعذبين من الجن والإنس، فلا يأخذهم ما يأخذ المجانس

QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#2/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#2/r10.claim: Fitna means a trial or affliction.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#2/r10.anchor: أي بلية. وروي عن ابن عباس من غير وجه

QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#2/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#2/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the number as deviation for disbelievers, especially Abu Jahl and associates.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#2/r11.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس من غير وجه قال: ضلالة للذين كفروا، يريد أبا جهل وذويه

QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#2/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#2/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#2/r12.claim: Another gloss takes fitna as punishment, matching people tried in the Fire in 51:13–14.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#2/r12.anchor: وقيل: إلا عذابا، كما قال تعالى:

QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#3/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#3/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas, Qatada, al-Dahhak, Mujahid, and others say the count confirms Torah and Gospel; it may refer to believing scripturalists like Abd Allah ibn Salam or all of them.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#3/r7.anchor: قاله ابن عباس وقتادة والضحاك ومجاهد وغيرهم

QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#3/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#3/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#3/r8.claim: Believers increase in faith by trusting scripture and affirming the number of Hell’s keepers.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#3/r8.anchor: آمنوا، ثم ازدادوا إيمانا لتصديقهم بعدد خزنة جهنم

QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#3/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#3/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#3/r9.claim: Neither the People of the Book nor Muhammad’s believers doubt the number of Hell’s keepers.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#3/r9.anchor: أي ولا يشك { الذين أوتوا الكتاب } أي أعطوا الكتاب

QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#3/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#3/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#3/r10.claim: Most commentators identify diseased hearts as Medinan hypocrites who arose after the Hijra; Mecca had none.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#3/r10.anchor: أي في صدورهم شك ونفاق من منافقي أهل المدينة، الذين ينجمون في مستقبل الزمان

QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#3/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#3/r11.speaker: الحسين بن الفضل
QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#3/r11.claim: Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl says the Meccan sura has no hypocrites, so disease means disagreement or doubt and disbelievers are Arab polytheists.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#3/r11.anchor: قال الحسين بن الفضل: السورة مكية ولم يكن بمكة نفاق فالمرض في هذه الآية الخلاف

QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#3/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#3/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#3/r12.claim: Most commentators take disbelievers as Jews and Christians; another view makes disease doubt among Meccans, some certain Muhammad lied.

QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#3/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#3/r13.speaker: الليث
QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#3/r13.claim: Al-Layth says mathal can mean a report; 13:35’s likeness of Paradise means its account and description.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#3/r13.anchor: قال الليث: المثل الحديث ومنه: «مثل الجنة التي وعد المتقون» أي حديثها

QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#3/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#3/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#3/r14.claim: God disgraces Abu Jahl’s deniers while guiding Muhammad’s companions; alternatively, He misleads from Paradise or guides to it.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#3/r14.anchor: أبا جهل وأصحابه المنكرين لخزنة جهنم

QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#3/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#3/r15.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#3/r15.claim: Only God knows the number of angels created to punish Hell’s people, answering Abu Jahl’s taunt that Muhammad had only nineteen forces.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#3/r15.anchor: أي وما يدري عدد ملائكة ربك الذين خلقهم لتعذيب أهل النار «إلا هو»

QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#4/r1.speaker: النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#4/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports at Hunayn that Gabriel sat with the Prophet when an unfamiliar angel brought a command; Gabriel said not every angel of God was known to him.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#4/r1.anchor: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يقسم غنائم حنين، فأتاه جبريل

QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#4/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#4/r2.speaker: الأوزاعي
QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#4/r2.claim: Al-Awzaʿi transmits Moses asking who is in heaven and how many angels; God says twelve tribes, each as numerous as dust.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#4/r2.anchor: وقال الأوزاعي: قال موسى: «يا رب من في السماء؟ قال ملائكتي

QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#4/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#4/r3.speaker: النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#4/r3.claim: The Prophet says the sky groans rightly: each four-finger space contains an angel prostrating; al-Tirmidhi transmits it.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#4/r3.anchor: وفي الترمذي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#4/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#4/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#4/r4.claim: One view takes it as the signs, proofs, and Quran, reminders for humanity.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#4/r4.anchor: يعني الدلائل والحجج والقرآن. وقيل: { وما هي }

QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#4/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#4/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#4/r5.claim: Another view takes it as Saqar, an admonition for humanity.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#4/r5.anchor: أي وما هذه النار التي هي سقر

QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#4/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#4/r6.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#4/r6.claim: Al-Zajjaj says worldly fire reminds of the Fire of the Hereafter.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#4/r6.anchor: وقيل: نار الدنيا تذكرة لنار الآخرة. قاله الزجاج

QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#4/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#4/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#4/r7.claim: Another view makes the keepers’ number a reminder of God’s power and lack of need for helpers; the pronoun refers to the nearest antecedent, the troops.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:30-31#4/r7.anchor: وأنه لا يحتاج إلى أعوان وأنصار

ALUSI-FULL:v29p115/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p115/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p115/r2.claim: Al-Ālūsī says the verse about the number of Hell’s keepers will provide evidence suggesting that “عليها تسعة عشر” is Medinan.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p115/r2.anchor: وسيأتي إن شاء الله تعالى ما يشعر بأن قوله تعالى عليها تسعة عشر مدني
